 15.3.4.5.2.5 Receive Status Word
     At the end of the transfer of the Ethernet frame to the host, the MTL outputs the receive status to RDES0,
     except that bits 31, 14, 9, and 8 are reserved and have a value of 0. When the status of a partial frame
     (because of overflow) is given out, the Frame Length field in the status word is not valid.


                                                        NOTE

       When any feature that gives extended status is enabled, the status is composed of two parts: normal
       – [31:0], and extended – [63:32]. The extended status gives the information about the received
       Ethernet payload when it is carrying PTP packets or TCP/UDP/ICMP over IP packets. The detailed
       description of the receive status is the same as described in RDES0, except that bits 31, 14, 9, and 8 of
       normal status are reserved and have a value of 0. When the status of a partial frame because of
       overflow is given out, the Frame Length field in the status word is not valid.


 15.3.4.6 ETH MAC
     The MAC supports RMII interface towards the PHY chip. The MAC communicates with the application side via
     the MAC Transmit Interface (MTI), MAC Receive Interface (MRI) and the MAC Control Interface (MCI).

 15.3.4.6.1 Transmission
     Transmission is initiated when the MTL application pushes in data to the MAC. It accepts the data and begins
     transmitting to the RMII. The time required to transmit the frame data to the RMII after the application
     initiates transmission varies, depending on delay factors like IFG delay, time to transmit preamble or SFD, and
     any back-off delays for half-duplex mode. Until then, the MAC does not accept the data received from MTL.
     After EOF is transferred to the MAC, it completes the normal transmission and gives the status of
     transmission to the MTL. If a normal collision (in half-duplex mode) occurs during transmission, the MAC
     issues transmit status to the MTL. It then accepts and drops all further data until the next SOF is received.
     The MAC issues an underflow status if the MTL is not able to provide the data continuously during the
     transmission. During the normal transfer of a frame from MTL, if the MAC receives a SOF without getting an
     EOF for the previous frame, then it ignores the SOF and considers the new frame as continuation of the
     previous frame.

 15.3.4.6.1.1 Transmit Protocol Engine
     The transmit protocol engine (TPE) consists of a transmit state machine that controls the operation of
     Ethernet frame transmission.
     Upon a new frame transmission the transmit state machine sends out the preamble and SFD, followed by the
     data. The preamble is defined as 7 bytes of 10101010 pattern, and the SFD is defined as 1 byte of 10101011
     pattern.
     The collision window is defined as 1 slot time (512-bit times). The JAM pattern generation is applicable only
     to half-duplex mode. If a collision occurs any time from the beginning of the frame to the end of the CRC
     field, the transmit state machine sends a 32-bit JAM pattern of 0x55555555 on the RMII to inform all other
     stations that a collision has occurred. If the collision is seen during the preamble transmission phase, the
     transmit state machine completes the transmission of preamble and SFD, and then sends the JAM pattern.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        693
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


     If the collision occurs after the collision window and before the end of the FCS field, the transmit state
     machine sends a 32-bit JAM pattern and sets the TDES0[LC] bit.
     The transmit state machine uses the deferral mechanism for the flow control (backpressure) in half duplex
     mode. When the application requests to stop receiving frames, the transmit state machine sends a JAM
     pattern of 32 bytes whenever it senses a reception of a frame, provided the transmit flow control is enabled.
     This results in a collision and the remote station backs off. The application requests the flow control by
     setting ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_CTRL[FCB_BPA] bit. If the application requests a frame to be transmitted,
     then it is scheduled and transmitted even when the backpressure is activated. If the backpressure is kept
     activated for a long time (and more than 16 consecutive collision events occur) then the remote stations
     abort their transmissions because of excessive collisions.
     If IEEE 1588 timestamping is enabled for the transmit frame, this block takes a snapshot of the system time
     when the SFD is put onto the transmit RMII bus.

 15.3.4.6.1.2 Transmit Scheduler
     The transmit scheduler (STX) is responsible for scheduling the frame transmission. It maintains the inter-
     frame gap between any two transmitted frames configured via the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[IPG] field.
     The STX starts its IFG counter as soon as the carrier signal of the RMII goes inactive. At the end of
     programmed IFG value, the STX enables the frame transmission when in full-duplex mode.
     In the half-duplex mode and when IFG is configured for 96-bit times, the STX follows the rule of deference
     specified in the IEEE 802.3 Specification, Section 4.2.3.2.1. The STX resets its IFG counter if a carrier is
     detected during the first two-thirds (64-bit times for all IFG values) of the IFG interval. If the carrier is
     detected during the final one third of the IFG interval, the STX continues the IFG count and enables the frame
     transmission after the IFG interval.

 15.3.4.6.1.3 Transmit CRC Generator
     The transmit CRC generator (CTX) calculates 32-bit CRC for the FCS field of the Ethernet frame. The encoding
     is defined by the following generating polynomial equation (15-5):
                                                                                                                  (15-5)


     The CRC is calculated over the following byte data of the Ethernet frame: DA + SA + LT + DATA + PAD.

 15.3.4.6.1.4 Transmit Flow Control
     The transmit flow control (FTX) module generates Pause frames that are later appended to the calculated
     CRC.
     The application can request the FTX module to send a Pause frame by setting the ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_
     CTRL[FCB_BPA] bit. In this case the FTX module generates a single Pause frame. The value of the Pause Time
     in the generated frame contains the programmed pause time value via the ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_CTRL
     [PT] field. To extend the pause or end the pause prior to the time specified in the previously transmitted
     Pause frame, the application must request another Pause frame transmission after programming the PT field
     with appropriate value.

 15.3.4.6.2 Reception
     A receive operation is initiated when the MAC detects an SFD. The MAC strips the preamble and SFD before
     proceeding to process the frame. The header fields are checked for the filtering and the FCS field used to


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        694
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


     verify the CRC for the frame. Thereafter an address filtering is performed. The frame is dropped if it fails the
     address filter.

 15.3.4.6.2.1 Receive Protocol Engine
     The receive protocol engine (RPE) takes a snapshot of the system time when a frame SFD is detected. Unless
     the MAC filters out and drops the frame, this timestamp is passed on to the application.
     The RPE decodes the Length/Type field of the receiving Ethernet frame. If the Length/Type field is less than
     1,536 and the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[ACS] bit is set, the MAC strips the Pad or FCS field on the
     incoming frames.
     If the Length/Type field is greater than or equal to 1,536 and the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[CST] bit is
     cleared, the MAC does not strip the Pad or FCS field. If the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[CST] bit is set and the
     Receive Checksum Offload Engine (Type 1) is not enabled, then the MAC strips and drops the last 4 bytes of
     all frames of Ether type before forwarding the frames to the application.
     By default, the MAC is programmed for watchdog timer to be enabled, that is, frames above 2,048 bytes (DA
     + SA + LT + DATA + PAD + FCS) are cut off. In addition, a programmable watchdog timer via the ETH_MAC_
     WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT[PWE] bit can be used to override the fixed timeout of 2,048 bytes. Software can also
     disable the watchdog timer by programming the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[WD] bit. Even if the watchdog
     timer is disabled, frames greater than 16KB in size are cut off and a watchdog timeout status is given.
     The MAC supports loopback of transmitted frames onto its receiver. By default, the MAC loopback function is
     disabled, but this feature can be enabled by setting the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[LM] bit. Bigger frames
     than 9,022 bytes should not be looped back, as they may get corrupted.

 15.3.4.6.2.2 Receive Frame Controller
     The receive frame controller (RFC) handles the Ethernet frame data and status. It is involved in the frame
     filtering.
     If the ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER[RA] bit is set, the RFC passes all received frames, irrespective of whether
     they pass the address filter or not, to the application. The result of the SA or DA filtering is updated (pass or
     fail) in the corresponding bits in the Receive Status Word. The RFC does not drop any frame on its own in this
     mode.
     If the RA bit is reset, the RFC passes only those frames to the application that pass the SA or DA address filter.
     When the ETH module is configured for power-down mode, all received frames are dropped and not
     forwarded to the application.

 15.3.4.6.2.3 Receive CRC Module
     The receive CRC (CRX) checks for any CRC error in the receiving frame. It calculates the 32-bit CRC for the
     received frame that includes the following: DA + SA + LT + DATA + PAD + FCS. The encoding is defined by the
     following generating polynomial:
                                                                                                                (15-6)


     Irrespective of the auto pad/CRC strip, the CRX module receives the entire frame to compute the CRC check
     for the received frame.




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        695
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                              www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                       E7 Series


 15.3.4.6.2.4 Receive Flow Control
     There is a receive flow control (FRX) module which detects the receiving Pause frame and pauses the frame
     transmission for the delay specified within the received Pause frame. The FRX is enabled only in full-duplex
     mode. The Pause frame detection function can be enabled or disabled via the ETH_MAC_RX_FLOW_CTRL
     [RFE] bit. If any Pause frame is received in half-duplex mode, the frame is considered as a normal frame.
     When the receive flow control is enabled, the FRX module begins monitoring the received frame destination
     address for any match with the multicast address of the control frame (0x0180C2000001). If a match is
     detected, the received control frame is either transferred or not to the application, based on the ETH_MAC_
     PACKET_FILTER[PCF] field.
     The FRX module also decodes the Type, Op-code, and Pause Timer field of the receiving control frame.
     Thereafter, if the byte count of the status indicates 64 bytes, and there is no CRC error, the FRX module
     requests the MAC transmitter to pause the transmission of any data frame for the duration of the decoded
     Pause Time value, multiplied by the slot time. Meanwhile, if another Pause frame is detected with a zero
     Pause Time value, the FRX module resets the Pause Time and gives another pause request to the
     Transmitter. If the received control frame matches neither the Type field (0x8808), Opcode (0x00001), nor
     byte length (64 bytes), or if there is a CRC error, the FRX module does not generate a Pause request to the
     transmitter.
     In case of a Pause frame with a multicast destination address, the frame is filtered based on the address
     match (0x0180C2000001). For a Pause frame with a unicast destination address, the filtering depends on
     whether the DA matched the contents of the ETH_MAC_ADDRESS0_HIGH and ETH_MAC_ADDRESS0_LOW
     registers, and the ETH_MAC_RX_FLOW_CTRL[UP] bit is set. If the UP bit is set and the MAC receives a Pause
     frame with multicast address, then the Pause frame is not processed. The ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER[PCF]
     field controls the filtering for control frames in addition to the address filter module.

 15.3.4.6.2.5 Address Filtering
     There is an address filtering module (AFM) which performs the destination and source address checking
     function on all received frames. The address checking is based on different parameters from the ETH_MAC_
     PACKET_FILTER register chosen by the application.

 15.3.4.6.2.6 Multicast Destination Address Filter
     The MAC can be programmed to pass all multicast frames by setting the ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER[PM] bit.

 15.3.4.6.2.7 Broadcast Address Filter
     The AFM does not filter any broadcast frames in the default mode. The MAC can be programmed to reject all
     broadcast frames by setting the ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER[DBF] bit.

 15.3.4.6.2.8 Unicast Source Address Filter
     The MAC can also perform a perfect filtering based on the source address field of the received frames. By
     default, the AFM compares the SA field with the values programmed in the SA registers. Group filtering with
     SA is also supported. The user can filter a group of addresses by masking one or more bytes of the address.
     The result of the SA filter is given as a status bit in the receive status word shown in Table 15-46.

 15.3.4.6.2.9 Inverse Filtering Operation
     For destination address filtering, there is an option to invert the filter-match result at the final output. This is
     controlled by the ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER[DAIF] bit. The DAIF bit is applicable for both unicast and
     multicast DA frames. The result of the unicast or multicast destination address filter is inverted in this mode.

 15.3.4.7 ETH Power Management
     There is a Power Management (PMT) block in the ETH module that supports reception of remote wake-up
     and magic packet frames. The PMT block does not perform clock gating function, but generates interrupt for
     these type of frames that the MAC receives.
     When the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[PWRDWN] bit is set to 1, the power-down mode is enabled
     and the MAC drops all received frames and does not forward any frame to the MTL RxFIFO. The MAC comes
     out of the power-down mode only when a magic packet or a remote wake-up frame is received if the
     corresponding detection is enabled via the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[MGKPKTEN] and ETH_MAC_
     PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPKTEN] bits.

 15.3.4.7.1 Remote Wake-Up Frame Filter Register
     The register wkupfmfilter_reg, at address 0xC4, loads the Wake-up Frame Filter register. To load values in the
     Wake-up Frame Filter register, the entire register wkupfmfilter_reg must be written. The wkupfmfilter_reg
     register is loaded by sequentially loading the eight register values in address 0xC4 for wkupfmfilter_reg0 to
     wkupfmfilter_reg7, respectively. The wkupfmfilter_reg register is read in a similar way. The ETH module
     updates the wkupfmfilter_reg current pointer value in the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPTR]
     field.
     Table 15-48 shows the Wake-Up Frame Filter Register.

 15.3.4.7.2 Remote Wake-Up Frame Detection
     When the MAC is in sleep mode and the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPKTEN] bit is set to 1, the
     normal operation is resumed after a remote wake-up frame is received.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                     Alif Semiconductor
                                                                700
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                       www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     There are four programmable filters that allow support of different receive frame patterns. If the incoming
     frame passes the address filtering (ETH_RWK_FILTER_COMMAND), and if filter CRC-16 (ETH_RWK_FILTER_
     CRC) matches the CRC of the incoming pattern, then the MAC identifies the frame as wake-up frame.
     The filter offset (ETH_RWK_FILTER_OFFSET) determines the offset from which the frame is to be examined.
     The filter byte mask (ETH_RWK_FILTER_BYTE_MASK) determines which bytes of the frame must be
     examined. Bit 31 of the byte mask must be set to 0.
     There is a remote wake-up CRC block that determines the CRC value to be compared with filter CRC-16. The
     remote wake-up frame is checked only for length error, FCS error, dribble bit error, RMII error or collision. In
     addition, the remote wake-up frame is checked to ensure that it is not a runt frame. Even if the remote
     wake-up frame is more than 512 bytes long, if the frame has a valid CRC value, it is considered valid. The
     remote wake-up frame detection is reflected via the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPRCVD] bit for
     every remote wake-up frame received and an interrupt (ETH_PMT_IRQ) is generated.

 15.3.4.7.3 Magic Packet Detection
     The magic packet frame is based on a method that uses Advanced Micro Device’s magic packet technology to
     power up the sleeping device on the network. The MAC receives a specific packet of information, called a
     magic packet, addressed to the node on the network.
     The MAC checks only those magic packets that are addressed to the MAC or a broadcast address to
     determine whether these packets meet the wake-up requirements. The magic packets that pass the address
     filtering (unicast or broadcast) are checked to determine whether they meet the remote wake-up frame data
     format of 6 bytes of all ones followed by a MAC address appearing 16 times.
     The application enables the magic packet wake-up by writing 1 to the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS
     [MGKPKTEN] bit. The PMT block constantly monitors each frame addressed to the node for a specific magic
     packet pattern. Each frame received is checked for a 0xFF_FF_FF_FF_FF_FF pattern following the destination
     and source address field. The PMT block then checks the frame for 16 repetitions of the MAC address
     without any breaks or interruptions. In case of a break in the 16 repetitions of the address, the PMT block
     again scans the 0xFF_FF_FF_FF_FF_FF pattern in the incoming frame. The 16 repetitions can be anywhere in
     the frame, but must be preceded by the synchronization stream (0xFF_FF_FF_FF_FF_FF). The device can also
     accept a multicast frame, as long as the 16 duplications of the MAC address are detected.
     The magic packet detection is reflected via the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[MGKPRCVD] bit and an
     interrupt (ETH_PMT_IRQ) is generated.




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                        701
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                       E7 Series


 15.3.5 ETH Programming Guide

 15.3.5.1 DMA Initialization
      1. Provide software reset by setting the ETH_DMA_MODE[SWR] bit. This resets all of the ETH internal
         registers and logic.
      2. Poll the SWR bit, which is only cleared after the reset operation completes.
      3. Poll the bits of the ETH_DMA_DEBUG_STATUS0 register to confirm that all previously initiated (before
         soft reset) or ongoing AXI transactions are complete. If the application cannot poll the ETH_DMA_
         DEBUG_STATUS0 register after soft reset because of performance reasons, then it is recommended to
         continue with the next steps and check this register again in step 11 before triggering the DMA
         operations.
      4. Program the ETH_DMA_SYSBUS_MODE register. If fixed burst length is enabled, then select the
         maximum burst length possible on the AXI bus.
      5. Create a proper descriptor chain for transmit and receive. In addition, ensure that the receive
         descriptors are owned by DMA (TDES0[OWN] = 1). When OSF mode is used, at least two descriptors are
         required. For more information about descriptors, see Section 15.3.4.4.6 DMA Descriptors.
      6. Make sure that software creates three or more different transmit or receive descriptors in the chain
         before reusing any of the descriptors.
      7. Program the ETH_DMA_CH0_RXDESC_LIST_ADDRESS and ETH_DMA_CH0_TXDESC_LIST_ADDRESS
         registers.
      8. Program the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_OPERATION_MODE[TSF], ETH_MTL_TXQ0_OPERATION_MODE[TTC], ETH_
         MTL_RXQ0_OPERATION_MODE[RSF], ETH_MTL_RXQ0_OPERATION_MODE[RTC], ETH_MTL_RXQ0_
         OPERATION_MODE[FEP], ETH_MTL_RXQ0_OPERATION_MODE[FUP], and ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL
         [OSF] fields.
      9. Enable the interrupts by programming the ETH_DMA_CH0_INTERRUPT_ENABLE register.
     10. Perform this step only if step 3 is not performed. Read the ETH_DMA_DEBUG_STATUS0 register to
         confirm that all previous AXI transactions are complete. If any previous transaction is still in progress
         when the ETH_DMA_DEBUG_STATUS0 register is read, it is strongly recommended to check the slave
         components addressed by the AXI master interface of the ETH module.
     11. Start the receive and transmit DMA by setting the ETH_DMA_CH0_RX_CONTROL[SR] and ETH_DMA_
         CH0_TX_CONTROL[ST] bits.

 15.3.5.2 MAC Initialization
     The following MAC Initialization operations can be performed after DMA initialization. If the MAC
     initialization is done before the DMA is set-up, then enable the MAC receiver (last step in following
     sequence) only after the DMA is active. Otherwise, received frames fill the Rx FIFO and cause overflow.
      1. Program the ETH_MAC_MDIO_ADDRESS register for controlling the management cycles for external
         PHY. Set the ETH_MAC_MDIO_ADDRESS[GB] bit for writing into PHY and reading from PHY.
      2. Read the ETH_MAC_MDIO_DATA[GD] field from the PHY for link up, speed of operation, and mode of
         operation, by specifying the appropriate address value via the ETH_MAC_MDIO_ADDRESS[PA] field.
      3. Program the ETH_MAC_ADDRESS0_HIGH and ETH_MAC_ADDRESS0_LOW registers.
      4. Program the RA, PR, PM, DBF, and PCF fields in the ETH_MAC_PACKET_FILTER register to set the
         appropriate filters for the incoming frames.
      5. Program the ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_CTRL[PT], ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_CTRL[PLT], ETH_MAC_Q0_
         TX_FLOW_CTRL[TFE], ETH_MAC_Q0_TX_FLOW_CTRL[FCB_BPA], ETH_MAC_RX_FLOW_CTRL[UP], ETH_
         MAC_RX_FLOW_CTRL[RFE] fields.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                        Alif Semiconductor
                                                      702
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                          www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                      E7 Series


      6. Program the appropriate fields in the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION register and then set the ETH_MAC_
         CONFIGURATION[TE] and ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bits.


                                                      NOTE

       Do not change the configuration (such as duplex mode, speed, port, or loopback) when the ETH
       controller is actively transmitting or receiving. Software should change these parameters only when
       the ETH transmitter and receiver are not active.


 15.3.5.3 Performing Normal Receive and Transmit Operation
      1. For normal transmit and receive interrupts, read the ETH_MAC_INTERRUPT_STATUS register. Then, poll
         the descriptors, reading the status of the descriptor owned by the host (either transmit or receive).
      2. Set appropriate values for the descriptors, ensuring that transmit and receive descriptors are owned by
         the DMA to resume the transmission and reception of data.
      3. If the descriptors are not owned by the DMA (or no descriptor is available), the DMA goes into suspend
         state. The transmission or reception can be resumed by freeing the descriptors and issuing a Transmit
         Poll Demand or Recieve Poll Demand command.
      4. The values of the current host transmitter or receiver descriptor address pointer can be read for debug
         process via the ETH_DMA_CH0_CURRENT_APP_TXDESC and ETH_DMA_CH0_CURRENT_APP_RXDESC
         registers.
      5. The values of the current host transmit buffer address pointer and receive buffer address pointer can be
         read for debug process via the ETH_DMA_CH0_CURRENT_APP_TXBUFFER and ETH_DMA_CH0_
         CURRENT_APP_RXBUFFER registers.

 15.3.5.4 Stopping and Starting Transmission
      1. If applicable, disable the transmit DMA by clearing the ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL[ST] bit.
      2. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete. This can be checked by reading the appropriate
         bits of the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_DEBUG register.
      3. Disable the MAC transmitter and MAC receiver by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[TE] and
         ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bits.
      4. If applicable, disable the receive DMA, after making sure that the data in the Rx FIFO is transferred to
         the system memory by reading the ETH_MTL_RXQ0_DEBUG register.
      5. Make sure that both Tx FIFO and Rx FIFO are empty.
      6. To restart the operation, first start the DMAs, and then enable the MAC transmitter and receiver.

 15.3.5.5 Transmit and Receive Clocks are Running when the Link is Down
     Complete the following steps when the link is down but the transmit and receive clocks are running:
      1. If applicable, disable the transmit DMA by clearing the ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL[ST] bit.
      2. Disable the MAC receiver by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bit.
      3. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete from the Tx FIFO. This can be checked by reading
         the appropriate bits of the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_DEBUG register.
         OR
         Flush the Tx FIFO for faster empty operation.
      4. Disable the MAC transmitter by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[TE] bit.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                       Alif Semiconductor
                                                      703
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                          www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


      5. After the link is up, read the PHY registers to know the latest configuration and accordingly program the
         MAC registers.
      6. Restart the operation by starting the Tx DMA, and then enable the MAC transmitter and receiver. It is
         not need to disable the Rx DMA. As the receiver is disabled, the FIFO does not get any data in the Rx
         FIFO.

 15.3.5.6 Transmit and Receive Clocks are Stopped when the Link is Down
     Complete the following steps when the link is down and the transmit and receive clocks are stopped:
      1. Wait till the link is up and the transmit and receive clocks are active. When the transmit and receive
         clocks are stopped, then disabling the transmit or receive operations does not have any effect.
         Therefore, software must wait till the link is up again.
      2. If applicable, disable the transmit DMA, by clearing the ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL[ST] bit.
      3. Disable the MAC receiver by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bit.
      4. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete from the Tx FIFO. This can be checked by reading
         the appropriate bits of the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_DEBUG register.
         OR
         Flush the Tx FIFO for faster empty operation.
      5. Disable the MAC transmitter by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[TE] bit.
      6. After the link is up, read the PHY registers to know the latest configuration and accordingly program the
         MAC registers.
      7. Restart the operation by starting the Tx DMA, and then enable the MAC transmitter and receiver.

 15.3.5.7 System Time Generation
     The user can enable IEEE 1588 timestamping by setting the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSENA] bit.
     However, it is essential that the timestamp counter should be initialized after this bit is set. Complete the
     following steps during ETH initialization:
      1. Disable the timestamp interrupt by clearing the ETH_MAC_INTERRUPT_ENABLE[TSIE] bit.
      2. Set the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSENA] bit to enable timestamping.
      3. Program the ETH_MAC_SUB_SECOND_INCREMENT register based on the CLK_PTP frequency.
      4. If the fine correction approach is used, program the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_ADDEND register and set
         the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSADDREG] bit.
      5. Poll the TSADDREG bit until it is cleared.
      6. If required, program the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSCFUPDT] bit to select the fine update
         method.
      7. Program the ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_SECONDS and ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_NANOSECONDS
         registers with the appropriate time value.
      8. Set the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSINIT] bit. The timestamp counter starts operation as soon
         as it is initialized with the value written in the ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_SECONDS and ETH_MAC_
         SYSTEM_TIME_NANOSECONDS registers.
      9. Enable the MAC receiver and transmitter for proper timestamping.




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       704
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                        E7 Series


                                                       NOTE

       If timestamp operation is disabled by clearing the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSENA] bit, the
       user needs to repeat all these steps to restart the timestamp operation.


 15.3.5.8 System Time Correction
     To synchronize or update the system time in one process (coarse correction method), complete the following
     steps:
      1. Set the offset (positive or negative) in the ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_SECONDS and ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_
         TIME_NANOSECONDS registers.
      2. Set the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSUPDT] bit. The value in the ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_
         SECONDS and ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_NANOSECONDS registers is added to or subtracted from the
         system time when the TSUPDT bit is cleared.
     To synchronize or update the system time to reduce system-time jitter (fine correction method), complete
     the following steps:
      1. Calculate the rate by which the user wants to make the system time increments slower or faster.
      2. Update the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_ADDEND register with the new value and set the ETH_MAC_
         TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSADDREG] bit.
      3. Wait for the time for which the user wants the new value of the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_ADDEND
         register to be active.
      4. Program the required target time in the ETH_MAC_PPS0_TARGET_TIME_SECONDS and ETH_MAC_
         PPS0_TARGET_TIME_NANOSECONDS registers.
      5. Enable the timestamp interrupt by setting the ETH_MAC_INTERRUPT_ENABLE[TSIE] bit.
      6. Set the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSTRIG] bit.
      7. When this trigger causes an interrupt, read the ETH_MAC_INTERRUPT_STATUS register.
      8. Reprogram the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_ADDEND register with the old value and set the ETH_MAC_
         TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TSADDREG] bit again.

 15.3.5.9 Switching the AXI Clock Frequency
     To dynamically change the AXI clock frequency without applying soft reset or hard reset, complete the
     following:
      1. If applicable, disable the transmit DMA and wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete.
         When the frame transmissions are complete, the Tx FIFO becomes empty and the Tx DMA enters stop
         state. The Tx FIFO status is given in the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_DEBUG register and the status of DMA is given
         in the ETH_DMA_CH0_STATUS register.
      2. Disable the MAC transmitter and the MAC receiver by clearing the appropriate bits in the ETH_MAC_
         CONFIGURATION register.
      3. If applicable, disable the receive DMA after making sure that the data in the Rx FIFO is transferred to the
         system memory. The Rx FIFO empty status is given in the ETH_MTL_RXQ0_DEBUG register.
      4. Ensure that the application does not perform any register read or write operation.
      5. Change the frequency of the AXI clock.
      6. Enable the MAC transmitter or the MAC receiver and the transmit or receive DMA.
     These steps ensure that no valid data is present in the Tx FIFO or Rx FIFO at the time of clock frequency
     switching and prevent any data corruption.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                         Alif Semiconductor
                                                       705
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                           www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


 15.3.5.10 Power-Down Sequence
      1. If applicable, disable the Tx DMA by clearing the ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL[ST] bit.
      2. Wait for any previous frame transmissions to complete by reading the ETH_MTL_TXQ0_DEBUG[TXQSTS]
         and ETH_MAC_DEBUG[TPESTS] bits.
      3. Disable the MAC transmitter and MAC receiver by clearing the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[TE] and
         ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bits.
      4. Configure the magic packet detection, remote wake-up detection or both via the ETH_MAC_PMT_
         CONTROL_STATUS[MGKPKTEN] and ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPKTEN] bits.
      5. Enable the MAC receiver by setting the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bit to 0x1, and then set the
         ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[PWRDWN] bit to 0x1 to start the MAC power-down sequence.
      6. Poll the ETH_STAT0[SBD_PWR_DOWN_ACK_O] bit until it reads 0x1.
      7. Set the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_CLAMP_CTRL_I] bit to 0x1 to reset the ETH always-ON logic.
      8. Set the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_ISOLATE_I] bit to 0x1 to enable the ETH isolation cells which provide required
         signal values to the ETH always-ON logic.
      9. Set the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_DOWN_CTRL_I] bit to 0x1 to power OFF all ETH blocks except the always-ON
         logic.

 15.3.5.11 Power-Up Sequence
      1. Clear the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_DOWN_CTRL_I] bit to power ON all ETH blocks except the always-ON logic
         which is powered.
      2. Clear the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_ISOLATE_I] bit to disable the ETH isolation cells.
      3. Clear the ETH_CTRL0[PWR_CLAMP_CTRL_I] bit to release the ETH always-ON logic from reset.
      4. Read the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS[RWKPRCVD] or ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS
         [MGKPRCVD] bit to clear the ETH_PMT_IRQ interrupt.
      5. If needed, perform a write operation with reset values to the ETH_MAC_PMT_CONTROL_STATUS
         register.
      6. Perform write operations to the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION, ETH_MAC_ADDRESS0_HIGH, and ETH_
         MAC_ADDRESS0_LOW registers to synchronize their values to the corresponding signals in the always-
         ON logic. Otherwise, the MAC receiver will be ON even though the ETH_MAC_CONFIGURATION[RE] bit is
         set to 0x0.
     After completing these steps, software must initialize all registers, enable the transmitter, and program the
     DMA to resume normal operation.

                                                  These bits control the minimum IPG between packets during

                                                  for tagged packet).
     23    GPSLCE            R/W        0x0       The watchdog timeout limit, Jumbo Packet Enable and 2KB Packet

                                                  When this bit is set, the MAC attempts only one transmission.
                                                  When a collision occurs on the RMII interface, the MAC ignores
                                                  the current packet transmission and reports a Packet Abort with
     8     DR                R/W        0x0       excessive collision error in the Tx packet status.
                                                  When this bit is reset, the MAC retries based on the settings of the
                                                  BL field. This bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode.

                                                  Back-Off Limit
                                                  The back-off limit determines the random integer number (r) of
                                                  slot time delays (512-bit times) for which the MAC waits before
                                                  rescheduling a transmission attempt during retries after a
                                                  collision.n = retransmission attempt.
    6-5    BL                R/W        0x0       The random integer r takes the value in the range 0 ≤ r < 2^k
                                                  This bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode.
                                                  0x0: k = min(n, 10)
                                                  0x1: k = min(n, 8)
                                                  0x2: k = min(n, 4)
                                                  0x3: k = min(n, 1)

                                                  When this bit is set, the deferral check function is enabled in the
                                                  MAC. The MAC issues a Packet Abort status, along with the
     4     DC                R/W        0x0
                                                  excessive deferral error bit set in the Tx packet status, when the Tx
                                                  state machine is deferred for more than 24,288-bit times in 10 or
                                                  100 Mbps mode.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                   713
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                 www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                     E7 Series


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            The defer time is not cumulative. For example, if the transmitter
                                                            defers for 10,000-bit times because the ETH_CRS_DV signal is
                                                            active and the ETH_CRS_DV signal becomes inactive, the
                                                            transmitter transmits and collision happens. Because of collision,
                                                            the transmitter needs to back off and then defer again after back
                                                            off completion. In such a scenario, the deferral timer is reset to 0,
                                                            and it is restarted.
                                                            When this bit is reset, the deferral check function is disabled and
                                                            the MAC defers until the ETH_CRS_DV signal goes inactive.
                                                            This bit is applicable only in the half-duplex mode.
                                                            0x0: Deferral check function is disabled
                                                            0x1: Deferral check function is enabled
                                                            Preamble Length for Transmit packets
                                                            These bits control the number of preamble bytes that are added to
                                                            the beginning of every Tx packet. The preamble reduction occurs
                                                            only when the MAC is operating in the full-duplex mode.
    3-2       PRELEN                  R/W         0x0
                                                            0x0: 7 bytes of preamble
                                                            0x1: 5 bytes of preamble
                                                            0x2: 3 bytes of preamble
                                                            0x3: Reserved
                                                            Transmitter Enable
                                                            When this bit is set, the Tx state machine of the MAC is enabled
                                                            for transmission on the RMII interface. When this bit is reset, the
                                                            MAC Tx state machine is disabled after it completes the
     1        TE                      R/W         0x0
                                                            transmission of the current packet. The Tx state machine does not
                                                            transmit any more packets.

                                                               detected packet. If the bit is 1, the corresponding byte is taken
                                                               into the CRC-16 calculation.
                                                               - 8-bit offset pointer: Specifies the byte to start the CRC-16
                                                               computation.
                                                               The pointer and the mask are used together to locate the bytes to
                                                               be used in the CRC-16 calculations.

   31-28 RESERVED                      R          0x0       Reserved
                                                            Preamble Suppression Enable
                                                            When this bit is set, the MDIO suppresses the 32-bit preamble and
     27       PSE                     R/W         0x0       transmits MDIO packets with only 1 preamble bit. When this bit is
                                                            0, the MDIO packets always has 32 bits of preamble as defined in

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                     Alif Semiconductor
                                                              740
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                       www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


    Bits   Field Name       Access   Reset Value Description
                                                  0x0: Preamble suppression disabled
                                                  0x1: Preamble suppression enabled
                                                  Back to Back Transactions
                                                  When this bit is set and the NTC has value greater than 0, then the
                                                  MAC informs the completion of a read or write command at the
                                                  end of frame transfer (before the trailing clocks are transmitted).
                                                  The software can thus initiate the next command which is
                                                  executed immediately irrespective of the number trailing clocks
     26    BTB               R/W        0x0       generated for the previous frame. When this bit is reset, then the
                                                  read/write command completion (GB is cleared) only after the
                                                  trailing clocks are generated. In this mode, it is ensured that the
                                                  NTC is always generated after each frame. This bit must not be set
                                                  when NTC = 0.
                                                  0x0: Back to back transactions disabled
                                                  0x1: Back to back transactions enabled
                                                  Physical Layer Address
                                                  Specifies the address of the PHY device, out of the 32 possible PHY
   25-21 PA                  R/W        0x0       devices.
                                                  Note: The value programmed in the C45E field determines if the
                                                  PHY device is Clause 45 capable or Clause 22 capable.
                                                  Register or Device Address
                                                  - For Clause 22 PHY: Specifies the PHY register address of the
   20-16 RDA                 R/W        0x0
                                                  selected PHY device.
                                                  - For Clause 45 PHY: Specifies the selected MDIO device.
     15    RESERVED           R         0x0       Reserved
                                                  Number of Trailing Clocks
                                                  This field controls the number of trailing clock cycles generated on
                                                  ETH_MDC after the end of MDIO frame transfer. The valid values
   14-12 NTC                 R/W        0x0
                                                  can be from 0 to 7. When this field is programmed with a value of
                                                  0x3, MAC generates three clock cycles on the ETH_MDC line after
                                                  the end of MDIO frame transfer.
                                                  CSR Clock (CLK_CSR) Range
                                                  The CLK_CSR range selection determines the frequency of the
                                                  MDC clock (ETH_MDC) according to the CLK_CSR frequency:
                                                  0x0: CLK_CSR = 60-100 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 42
                                                  0x1: CLK_CSR = 100-150 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 62
    11-8   CR                R/W        0x0       0x2: CLK_CSR = 20-35 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 16
                                                  0x3: CLK_CSR = 35-60 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 26
                                                  0x4: CLK_CSR = 150-250 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 102
                                                  0x5: CLK_CSR = 250-300 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 124
                                                  0x6: CLK_CSR = 300-500 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 204
                                                  0x7: CLK_CSR = 500-800 MHz; ETH_MDC = CLK_CSR / 324


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                   741
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                        E7 Series


    Bits   Field Name       Access   Reset Value Description
                                                  The suggested range of CLK_CSR frequency applicable for each
                                                  value (when Bit 11 = 0) ensures that the ETH_MDC is
                                                  approximately between 1.0 MHz to 2.5 MHz freqency range.
                                                  When Bit 11 is set, the user can achieve a higher frequency of the
                                                  ETH_MDC than the frequency limit of 2.5 MHz (specified in the
                                                  IEEE 802.3 Specification) and program a clock divider of lower
                                                  value. For example, when CLK_CSR is of 100 MHz frequency and
                                                  the user programs the CR field to 0xA, the resultant ETH_MDC is of
                                                  12.5 MHz which is beyond the range specified in IEEE 802.3
                                                  Specification. Program the following values only if the interfacing
                                                  chips support faster MDC clocks:
                                                  0x8: CLK_CSR / 4
                                                  0x9: CLK_CSR / 6
                                                  0xA: CLK_CSR / 8
                                                  0xB: CLK_CSR / 10
                                                  0xC: CLK_CSR / 12
                                                  0xD: CLK_CSR / 14
                                                  0xE: CLK_CSR / 16
                                                  0xF: CLK_CSR / 18
    7-5    RESERVED           R         0x0       Reserved

                                                  When this bit is set, the MDIO does not send the address packets

     4     SKAP              R/W        0x0
                                                  bit is valid only when the C45E bit is set.
                                                  0x0: Skip address packet is disabled
                                                  0x1: Skip address packet is enabled
                                                  Operation Command 1
                                                  This is the higher bit of the operation command to the PHY. GOC_1
                                                  and GOC_O are encoded as follows:
                                                  0x0: Reserved
                                                  0x1: Write
     3     GOC_1             R/W        0x0
                                                  0x2: Post read increment address for Clause 45 PHY
                                                  0x3: Read
                                                  GOC_1 is encoded as follows:
                                                  0x0: Operation command 1 is disabled
                                                  0x1: Operation command 1 is enabled
                                                  Operation Command 0
                                                  This is the lower bit of the operation command to the PHY. When
                                                  in MDIO mode (MDIO master) this bit along with GOC_1
     2     GOC_0             R/W        0x0
                                                  determines the operation to be performed to the PHY.
                                                  0x0: Operation command 0 is disabled
                                                  0x1: Operation command 0 is enabled

    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            Clause 45 PHY Enable
                                                            When this bit is set, Clause 45 capable PHY is connected to MDIO.

     1        C45E                    R/W         0x0

                                                            read transfer is completed (GB=0), the data read from the PHY
                                                            register is valid in the ETH_MAC_MDIO_DATA[GD] field.
                                                            Access restriction applies. Setting 1 sets. Self-cleared. Setting 0 has

 15.3.6.3.38 ETH_MAC_TX_TIMESTAMP_STATUS_NANOSECONDS Register
           Offset           Access         Description
                                           MAC Transmit Timestamp Status Register (Nanoseconds)
                                           This register contains the nanosecond part of timestamp captured for Transmit
                                           packets when Tx status is disabled. The ETH_MAC_TX_TIMESTAMP_STATUS_
                                           NANOSECONDS register, along with ETH_MAC_TX_TIMESTAMP_STATUS_SECONDS,
                                           gives the 64-bit timestamp captured for the PTP packet successfully transmitted by
                                           the MAC. This value is considered to be read by the application when the last byte
        0xB30                              of ETH_MAC_TX_TIMESTAMP_STATUS_SECONDS is read. In the little-endian mode,
                              R
     Base address                          this means when bits[31-24] are read; in big-endian mode, bits[7-0] are read. If the
                                           application does not read these registers and timestamp of another packet is
                                           captured, then either the current timestamp is lost (overwritten) or the new
                                           timestamp is lost (dropped), depending on the setting of the ETH_MAC_
                                           TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TXTSSTSM] bit. The status bit TXTSSIS bit [15] in ETH_MAC_
                                           TIMESTAMP_STATUS register is set whenever the MAC transmitter captures the
                                           timestamp.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            Transmit Timestamp Status Missed
                                                            When this bit is set, it indicates one of the following:
                                                            The timestamp of the current packet is ignored if the ETH_MAC_
                                                            TIMESTAMP_CONTROL[TXTSSTSM] bit is reset
                                                            The timestamp of the previous packet is overwritten with
     31       TXTSSMIS                 R         0x0        timestamp of the current packet if the ETH_MAC_TIMESTAMP_
                                                            CONTROL[TXTSSTSM] bit is set.
                                                            Access restriction applies. Clears on read. Self-set to 1 on internal
                                                            event.
                                                            0x0: Transmit timestamp status missed status not detected
                                                            0x1: Transmit timestamp status missed status detected
                                                            Transmit Timestamp Status Low

 15.3.6.3.44 ETH_MAC_PPS_CONTROL Register
           Offset           Access          Description
        0xB70
                             R/W            PPS Control Register
     Base address


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
    31-4      RESERVED                 R                     Reserved
                                                             Pulse Per Second (PPS) Frequency Control
                                                             This field controls the PPS frequency. The default value of PPSCTRL
    3-0       PPSCTRL                 R/W         0x0
                                                             is 0x0, and the PPS frequency is 1 pulse every second. For other
                                                             values of PPSCTRL, the PPS becomes a generated clock of the


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                    Alif Semiconductor
                                                               757
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                       www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                     E7 Series


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                           following frequencies:
                                                           0x1: The binary rollover is 2 Hz, and the digital rollover is 1 Hz.
                                                           0x2: The binary rollover is 4 Hz, and the digital rollover is 2 Hz.
                                                           0x3: The binary rollover is 8 Hz, and the digital rollover is 4 Hz.
                                                           0x4: The binary rollover is 16 Hz, and the digital rollover is 8 Hz.
                                                           ...
                                                           0xF: The binary rollover is 32.768 kHz and the digital rollover is
                                                           16.384 kHz.
                                                           Note:
                                                           In the binary rollover mode, the PPS frequency has a duty cycle of
                                                           50 percent with these frequencies.
                                                           In the digital rollover mode, the PPS frequency is an average
                                                           number. The actual clock is of different frequency that gets
                                                           synchronized every second. For example:
                                                           When PPSCTRL = 0x1, the PPS (1 Hz) has a low period of 537 ms
                                                           and a high period of 463 ms
                                                           When PPSCTRL = 0x2, the PPS (2 Hz) is a sequence of:
                                                           - One clock of 50 percent duty cycle and 537 ms period
                                                           - Second clock of 463 ms period (268 ms low and 195 ms high)
                                                           When PPSCTRL = 0x3, the PPS (4 Hz) is a sequence of:
                                                           - Fourth clock of 195 ms period (134 ms low and 61 ms high)
                                                           This behavior is because of the non-linear toggling of bits in the
                                                           digital rollover mode in the ETH_MAC_SYSTEM_TIME_
                                                           NANOSECONDS register.

    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                           When this bit is set, the Tx Queue controller logic is reset to its
                                                           default values. Therefore, all the data in the Tx Queue is lost or
                                                           flushed. This bit is internally reset when the flushing operation is
                                                           complete. Until this bit is reset, the user must not write to the
                                                           ETH_MTL_TXQ0_OPERATION_MODE register. The data which is

                                                           packet transmission.

    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            When this bit is reset, the Rx Queue drops packets with error

 15.3.6.3.66 ETH_DMA_CH0_RX_CONTROL Register
           Offset           Access          Description
       0x1108                               The DMA Channel Receive Control Register
                             R/W
     Base address                           This register controls the Rx features such as PBL, buffer size, and extended status.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                             Rx Packet Flush.
                                                             When this bit is set to 1, then the ETH module automatically
                                                             flushes the packet from the Rx Queues destined to this DMA Rx
                                                             Channel, when it is stopped. When this bit remains set and the
                                                             DMA is re-started by the software driver, the packets residing in
                                                             the Rx Queues that were received when this Rx DMA was stopped,
                                                             still get flushed out. The packets received by the MAC only after
                                                             the DMA is re-started is routed to the Rx DMA. The flushing is
                                                             done on the Read side of the Rx Queue. When the packet is
                                                             duplicated to multiple Rx DMA, it is flushed by the Rx DMA to
                                                             which it is routed only when it is stopped to prevent head-of-line
                                                             blocking. The packet duplicated to multiple Rx DMA is not flushed
                                                             when the Rx DMA is re-started, irrespective of whether the packet
     31       RPF                     R/W          0x0       was received during one or more Rx DMAs were stopped.
                                                             When this bit is set to 0, the ETH module does not flush the packet
                                                             in the Rx Queue destined to this Rx DMA Channel when it is in
                                                             STOP state. This might in turn cause head-of-line blocking in the
                                                             corresponding RxQueue.
                                                             Note: The stopping of packet flow from a Rx DMA Channel to the
                                                             application by setting RPF works only when there is one-to-one
                                                             mapping of Rx Queue to Rx DMA channels. In Dynamic mapping
                                                             mode, setting RPF bit in any ETH_DMA_CH0_RX_CONTROL register
                                                             might flush packets from unintended Rx Queues which are
                                                             destined to the stopped Rx DMA Channel.
                                                             0x0: Rx packet flush is disabled
                                                             0x1: Rx packet flush is enabled
   30-22 RESERVED                      R           0x0       Reserved

                                                             These bits indicate the maximum number of beats to be

     15    RESERVED           R         0x0       Reserved
                                                  Receive Buffer Size High
                                                  RBSZ[13-0] is split into two fields higher RBSZ_13_y and lower

 15.3.6.3.67 ETH_DMA_CH0_TXDESC_LIST_ADDRESS Register
           Offset           Access          Description
                                            The Channel Tx Descriptor List Address Register
                                            This register points the DMA to the start of Transmit descriptor list. The descriptor
                                            lists reside in the physical memory space of the application and must be Dword-
                                            aligned. The DMA internally converts it to bus width aligned address by making the
       0x1114                               corresponding LSB to low. The user can write to this register only when the Tx DMA
                             R/W
     Base address                           has stopped, that is, the ST bit is set to zero in ETH_DMA_CH0_TX_CONTROL
                                            register. When stopped, this register can be written with a new descriptor list
                                            address. When the user sets the ST bit to 1, the DMA takes the newly-programmed
                                            descriptor base address. If this register is not changed when the ST bit is set to 0,
                                            the DMA takes the descriptor address where it was stopped earlier.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                             Start of Transmit List
    31-3      TDESLA                  R/W          0x0       This field contains the base address of the first descriptor in the
                                                             Transmit descriptor list.
    2-0       RESERVED                 R           0x0       Reserved

                                                             RDES3[30].
                                                             When the watchdog timer runs out, the RI bit is set and the timer
                                                             is stopped. The watchdog timer is reset when the RI bit is set high
                                                             because of automatic setting of RI as per the Interrupt Enable bit
                                                             RDES3[30] of any received packet.

 15.4 Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C)

 15.4.1 I2C Overview
     The Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C) module is a synchronous, master/slave serial communication bus which is
     suitable for different system control applications.
     The device includes:
       n   Up to four I2C modules in Shared Peripherals
       n   One Low-Power I2C (LPI2C) slave-only module in the RTSS-HE
     The I2C modules support the following main features:
       n Operating bus speed:
         l Standard Speed (SS) mode (up to 100 kbps)

         l Fast Speed (FS) mode (up to 400 kbps)

         l Fast Mode Plus (FM+) mode (up to 1 Mbps)

         l High Speed (HS) mode (up to 3.4 Mbps)

       n Master or slave operation
       n 7- or 10-bit addressing
       n 7- or 10-bit combined format transfers
       n 32-byte deep receive and transmit FIFOs
       n Bulk transmit mode
       n Interrupt or polled-mode operation
       n Bit and byte waiting at all bus speeds
       n DMA handshaking interface
       n Programmable SDA hold time
       n Bus clear feature

     The LPI2C module supports the following main features:
       n Operating bus speed:
           lStandard Speed (SS) mode (up to 100 kbps)
         l Fast Speed (FS) mode (up to 400 kbps)

       n Slave operation only
       n 7-bit addressing only
       n Hardcoded slave bus address (0x40)
       n 8-byte deep inbound and outbound FIFOs
       n Burst writes only (burst reads are not supported)
       n Interrupt or polled-mode operation
       n The LPI2C interrupt can be used as a wake-up source from STANDBY low-power mode



                                                      NOTE

       All Low Power peripherals are single-master accessible, including LPI2C. Ensure that application
       software manages access to these LP peripherals such that no more than one bus master (CPU or
       DMA) attempts access at a time, using semaphores or similar techniques.

 15.4.4 I2C Functional Description
                                                                  NOTE

       All information in this section applies only to the I2C modules in Shared Peripherals. For information
       on LPI2C module operation, see Section 15.4.5 LPI2C Functional Description.


 15.4.4.1 I2C Introduction
     Figure 15-29 presents a simplified diagram of the I2C main internal blocks and connections.
                                                 Figure 15-29 I2C Block Diagram(1)
           Device
                                                                       I2C
                    Clocks       Clock
                               Generator
                                                                             Master/Slave
                                                                             State Machine

           Interconnect                                                                                          SCL
                               AMBA Bus               Register                                  I/O
                             Interface Unit             File                                 Interface
                                                                                                                 SDA
                                                                                 Tx/Rx
              Interrupts                                                     FIFO and Shi�
                               Interrupt
                               Controller                                       Rx Filter

                                                   Synchronizer
                     DMA         DMA
                               Interface

                                                                                                                    I2C-004




     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     The I2C module is a two-wire, bidirectional, serial communication interface. Serial data (SDA) and serial clock
     (SCL) lines carry information between devices that are connected to the I2C™ bus. Each device can operate as
     either a transmitter or a receiver. Devices are also considered as either masters or slaves. A master initiates a
     data transfer on the bus and generates the clock that synchronizes the data transfer. A slave is addressed by
     the master and responds to its requests. Each slave on the I2C bus is recognized by a unique address.
     The I2C module includes the following main blocks:
       n AMBA Bus Interface Unit: Provides protocol conversion between APB bus and register file
       n Register File: Contains configuration registers and is the interface with software
       n Master State Machine: Generates the I2C protocol for the master transfers
       n Slave State Machine: Follows the I2C protocol for a slave and monitors the bus for address match
       n Clock Generator: Calculates the required timing to do the following:
         l Generate the SCL clock when configured as a master

         l Check for bus idle

         l Generate START and STOP conditions

         l Setup the data and hold the data

       n Synchronizer: Transfers signals between clock domains
       n Rx Shift: Takes data into the design and extracts it in byte format
       n Tx Shift: Presents data supplied by CPU for transfer on the I2C bus
Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                Alif Semiconductor
                                                                 801
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                  www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


       n Rx Filter: Detects events on the I2C bus (for example: start, stop and arbitration lost)
       n Rx/Tx FIFO: Holds the Rx/Tx FIFO register banks and controllers, along with their status levels
       n DMA Interface: Generates the handshaking signals to the central DMA controller
       n Interrupt Controller: Generates raw interrupts and interrupt flags and allows them to be set and cleared

     The I2C module can operate in any of the following speed modes:
       n Standard Speed (SS) mode (data rates up to 100 kbps)
       n Fast Speed (FS) mode (data rates up to 400 kbps)
       n Fast Mode Plus (FM+) mode (data rates up to 1 Mbps)
       n High Speed (HS) mode (data rates up to 3.4 Mbps)

     The I2C module can be setup in SS, FS, FM+ or HS mode by configuring the I2C_CON[SPEED] bit field and the
     respective *HCNT/*LCNT registers. To ensure proper I/O timing, this has to be done before there is any I2C
     bus transaction. For more information, see Section 15.4.4.16 I2C Programming Flows.

 15.4.4.2 I2C Clocks
     The I2C module uses two identical clocks:
       n PCLK: APB bus clock
       n IC_CLK: Peripheral clock that is used to clock transfers in the different speed modes


 15.4.4.3 I2C Interrupt Requests
     The I2C module has the ability to generate interrupts based on a variety of conditions within the module. It
     has a single combined interrupt output to indicate to a device interrupt controller that an interrupt condition
     has occurred. The specific cause of the I2C interrupt can be determined by reading the I2C_INTR_STAT status
     register.
     Each interrupt can be individually enabled by setting the appropriate mask bit to 1 in the I2C_INTR_MASK
     register. At any time, the status of the interrupt mask can be read from the I2C_INTR_MASK register. Both
     the raw interrupt status (prior to masking) and the final interrupt status (after masking) can be read from the
     I2C_RAW_INTR_STAT and I2C_INTR_STAT registers, respectively.
     The I2C module generates the following interrupts:
       n SCL stuck condition detect interrupt (SCL_STUCK_AT_LOW)
       n I2C activity interrupt (ACTIVITY)
       n Stop condition detect interrupt (STOP_DET)
       n Start condition detect interrupt (START_DET)
       n General Call received interrupt (GEN_CALL)
       n Receive buffer underflow interrupt (RX_UNDER)
       n Receive buffer overflow interrupt (RX_OVER)
       n Receive done interrupt (RX_DONE)
       n Receive buffer full interrupt (RX_FULL)
       n Slave read request interrupt (RD_REQ)
       n Transmit abort interrupt (TX_ABRT)
       n Transmit buffer overflow interrupt (TX_OVER)
       n Transmit buffer empty interrupt (TX_EMPTY)

     For a detailed description of each configurable interrupt source, refer to the I2C_RAW_INTR_STAT register.
     Upon detection of an interrupt event, as configured in the I2C_INTR_MASK register, the I2C interrupt signal is
     generated. It is then routed to a device interrupt controller for further processing. If the interrupt is software
     clearable, it can be cleared by reading its corresponding interrupt clear register, or the I2C_CLR_INTR register

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        802

                                                                                                                          E7 Series


     which clears all software clearable interrupts at once. If the interrupt is clearable by hardware only, it will be
     cleared automatically when the interrupt conditions have changed.

 15.4.4.4 I2C DMA Requests
     The I2C supports a DMA handshaking interface to a DMA Controller (DMAC) at device level to request and
     control data transfers on the APB bus. To enable the DMA Controller interface for the I2C configure the I2C_
     DMA_CR register:
       n Writing a 1 into the I2C_DMA_CR[TDMAE] register bit enables the I2C transmit handshaking interface.
       n Writing a 1 into the I2C_DMA_CR[RDMAE] register bit enables the I2C receive handshaking interface.


 15.4.4.4.1 Transmit Watermark Level and Transmit FIFO Underflow
     During I2C serial transfers, Tx FIFO requests are made to the DMAC whenever the number of entries in the Tx
     FIFO is less than or equal to the value of the I2C_DMA_TDLR[DMATDL] bit field. This is known as transmit
     Watermark Level (WL). The DMAC responds by writing a burst of data to the Tx FIFO buffer.
     Data should be fetched from the DMA often enough for the Tx FIFO to perform serial transfers continuously;
     that is, when the Tx FIFO begins to empty, another DMA request should be triggered. Otherwise, the Tx FIFO
     runs out of data causing a STOP to be inserted on the I2C bus (Tx FIFO underflow occurs).

 15.4.4.4.1.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level
     The goal in choosing a proper WL is to minimize the number of transactions per DMA block transfer, while at
     the same time keeping the probability of an underflow condition to an acceptable level. In practice, this is a
     function of the ratio of the rate at which the I2C transmits data to the rate at which the DMA controller can
     respond to destination burst requests.

           Number of Data Items (NDI) per DMA Burst, as defined by equation 15-7:

           The value of DMA Transfer Block Size is programmed at DMAC level. It defines the number of data
           transfers that the DMAC performs when it writes the destination data. See Section 12.2 DMA
           Controllers for more information.

           l Tx FIFO Depth is as specified in Section 15.4.1 I2C Overview.
