 15.5.4.3.1 I2S Transmitter Block Enable
     The transmitter block can be enabled or disabled during operation by programming the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit.
     This bit also turns on and off the Tx channel. To enable the transmitter block, set the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit to
     0x1. To disable the transmitter block, set the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit to 0x0.
     When the transmitter block is disabled, the following events occur:
       n   Outgoing data is lost and the output channel is held low.
       n   Data in the Tx FIFO is preserved and the FIFO can be written to.

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                   Alif Semiconductor
                                                                 877
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                     www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


       n Any previous programming (like changes in word size, threshold levels, and so on) of the Tx channel is
         preserved.
       n The TX channel enables are overridden.

     When the transmitter block is enabled, if there is data in the Tx FIFOs, the channel resumes transmission on
     the next left stereo data cycle (such as when the WS line goes low).
     When the transmitter block is disabled, the following procedures can be performed:
       n Program (or further program) the Tx channel registers.
       n Flush the channel Tx FIFO by setting the I2S_TFF0[TXCHFR] bit to 0x1 (or by setting the I2S_TXFFR[TXFFR]
         bit to 0x1).
     On reset, the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit is set to 0x0 (disable).

 15.5.4.3.2 I2S Transmit Channel Enable
     The Tx channel can be enabled or disabled by programming the I2S_TER0[TXCHENX] bit. To enable the Tx
     channel, set the I2S_TER0[TXCHENX] bit to 0x1. To disable the Tx channel, set the I2S_TER0[TXCHENX] bit to
     0x0.
     When the Tx channel is disabled, the following events occur:
       n Outgoing stereo data is lost.
       n Channel output is held low.
       n Data in the Tx FIFO is preserved, and the FIFO can be written to.
       n Any previous programming of the Tx channel registers is preserved, and the Tx channel can be further
         reprogrammed.
     When the Tx channel is disabled, the channel Tx FIFO can be flushed by setting the I2S_TFF0[TXCHFR] bit to
     0x1. When the Tx channel is enabled, if there is data in the Tx FIFO, the channel resumes transmission on the
     next left stereo data cycle (when the WS line goes low).
     On reset, the I2S_TFF0[TXCHFR] bit is set to 0x1 (enable).

 15.5.4.3.3 I2S Transmit Channel Audio Data Resolution
     The Tx channel is initially configured with the maximum audio data resolution supported. The Tx channel can
     be reprogrammed during operation to any supported audio data resolution that is less than the maximum
     audio data resolution.
     For example, if the Tx channel maximum audio data resolution is 32 bits, it can be programmed to support a
     resolution of 12, 16, 20, 24, or 32 bits. Any other resolution values are considered invalid. Furthermore, if the
     channel is programmed with an invalid audio resolution, the Tx channel defaults to the maximum audio data
     resolution supported.
     Reprogramming of the audio resolution ensures that the MSB of the data is still transmitted first if the
     resolution of the data to be sent is reduced. Changes to the resolution are programmed by the I2S_TCR0
     [WLEN] bit field. The Tx channel must be disabled prior to any resolution changes. For more information
     about the Tx channel enable and disable, refer to Section 15.5.4.3.2 I2S Transmit Channel Enable.
     On reset or if an invalid resolution is selected, the Tx channel audio data resolution defaults back to the to
     the maximum audio data resolution supported.
     For more information about I2S supported audio data resolutions, refer to Section 15.5.1 I2S Overview.

 15.5.4.3.4 I2S Transmit Channel FIFO
     The Tx channel has two FIFO banks - for left and right stereo data.

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        878
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     The FIFO width (word size) is determined by the maximum audio data resolution supported by the I2S.
     For more information about I2S supported audio data resolutions and FIFOs depth, refer to Section 15.5.1
     I2S Overview.
     There are several ways to clear the Tx FIFO and reset the read/write pointers:
       n On reset
       n By disabling the I2S (I2S_IER[IEN] = 0x0)
       n By flushing the transmitter block (I2S_TXFFR[TXFFR] = 0x1)
       n By flushing the Tx channel (I2S_TFF0[TXCHFR] = 0x1)

     The transmitter block/Tx channel must be disabled before the transmitter block/Tx channel FIFO can be
     flushed.
     The default empty trigger threshold level for the Tx FIFO is 3. The trigger level can be set to any value in the
     range of 0 to [FIFO depth – 1]. When this level is reached, a Tx FIFO Empty interrupt is generated. The trigger
     level can be reprogrammed during operation by writing to the I2S_TFCR0[TXCHET] bit field. The Tx channel
     must be disabled prior to changing the trigger level.

 15.5.4.3.5 I2S Transmit Channel Interrupts
     All interrupts generated from the I2S are active high. The Tx channel generates two interrupts:
       n Tx FIFO Empty—This interrupt is asserted when the empty trigger threshold level for the Tx FIFO is
         reached. A Tx FIFO Empty interrupt is cleared by writing data to the Tx FIFO to bring its level above the
         empty trigger threshold level for the channel.
       n Tx FIFO Data Overrun—This interrupt is asserted when an attempt is made to write to a full Tx FIFO; any
         data being written is lost, while data in the FIFO is preserved. A Tx FIFO Data Overrun interrupt is cleared
         by reading the I2S_TOR0[TXCHO] bit.
     The interrupt status of the Tx channel can be determined by polling the Interrupt Status Register (I2S_ISR0).
     The I2S_ISR0[TXFE] bit indicates the status of the Tx FIFO Empty interrupt, while the I2S_ISR0[TXFO] bit
     indicates the status of the Tx FIFO Data Overrun interrupt.
     Both the Tx FIFO Empty and Tx FIFO Data Overrun interrupts can be masked off by writing 0x1 to the I2S_
     IMR0[TXFEM] and I2S_IMR0[TXFOM] bits, respectively. This prevents the interrupts from driving their output
     lines, however, the I2S_ISR0 register always shows the current status of the interrupts regardless of any
     masking.
     The I2S has a single global interrupt output.

 15.5.4.3.6 Writing to a Transmit Channel
     Normally, the stereo data pairs to be transmitted by the Tx channel are written to the Tx FIFO through the
     Left Transmit Holding register (I2S_LTHR0) and the Right Transmit Holding register (I2S_RTHR0). All stereo
     data pairs must be written using the following two-stage process:
      1. Write left stereo data to the I2S_LTHR0 register.
      2. Write right stereo data to the I2S_RTHR0 register.
     When Tx DMA is enabled, data to be transmitted by the Tx channel is written to the Tx FIFO through the I2S_
     TXDMA register rather than through the I2S_LTHR0 and I2S_RTHR0 registers. Data is written cyclically in the
     I2S_TXDMA register in the following order:
      1.      Left stereo data
      2.      Right stereo data


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                        879
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                            E7 Series


     When the I2S is enabled, if the Tx FIFO is empty and data is not written to the FIFO before the next left cycle,
     the channel outputs zeros for a full frame (left and right cycle). Transmission only commences if there is data
     in the Tx FIFO prior to the transition to the left data cycle. In other words, if the start of the frame is missed,
     the channel output idles until the next available frame.
     Note that data should only be written to the FIFO when it is not full. Any attempt to write to a full FIFO
     results in data being lost and a Data Overrun interrupt being generated.

 15.5.4.4 I2S as a Receiver
     The I2S receiver (Rx) stereo channel operates in Master mode. Stereo data pairs (such as, left and right audio
     data) are received serially from the SDI line. These data words are stored in the Rx FIFO until they are read
     through the APB bus. The receiving is timed with respect to the SCLK and the WS line.

 15.5.4.4.1 I2S Receiver Block Enable
     The receiver block can be enabled or disabled during operation by programming the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit. This
     bit also turns on and off the Rx channel. To enable the receiver block, set the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit to 0x1. To
     disable the receiver block, set the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit to 0x0.
     When the receiver block is disabled, the following events occur:
       n   Incoming data is lost.
       n   Data in the Rx FIFO is preserved and the FIFO can be read.

                                                                881
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                              www.alifsemi.com

       n Any previous programming (like changes in word size, threshold levels, and so on) of the Rx channel is
         preserved.
       n The RX channel enables are overridden. Enabling the channel resumes receiving on the next left stereo
         data cycle (for instance, when WS goes low).
     When the receiver block is disabled, the following procedures can be performed:
       n   Program (or further program) the Rx channel registers.
       n   Flush the channel Rx FIFO by setting the I2S_RFF0[RXCHFR] bit to 0x1 (or by setting the I2S_RXFFR
           [RXFFR] bit to 0x1).
     On reset, the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit is set to 0x0 (disable).

 15.5.4.4.2 I2S Receive Channel Enable
     The Rx channel can be enabled or disabled by programming the I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] bit. To enable the Rx
     channel, set the I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] bit to 0x1. To disable the Rx channel, set the I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] bit to
     0x0.
     When the Rx channel is disabled, the following events occur:
       n Incoming data is lost.
       n Data in the Rx FIFO is preserved, and the FIFO can be read.
       n Any previous programming of the Rx channel registers is preserved, and the Rx channel can be further
         reprogrammed.
     When the Rx channel is disabled, the channel Rx FIFO can be flushed by setting the I2S_RFF0[RXCHFR] bit to
     0x1. When the Rx channel is enabled, it resumes receiving on the next left stereo data cycle (such as when
     the WS line goes low).
     On reset, the I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] bit is set to 0x1 (enable).

 15.5.4.4.3 I2S Receive Channel Audio Data Resolution
     The Rx channel is initially configured with the maximum audio data resolution supported. The Rx channel can
     be reprogrammed during operation to any supported audio data resolution that is less than the maximum
     audio data resolution.
     For example, if the Rx channel maximum audio data resolution is 32 bits, it can be programmed to support a
     resolution of 12, 16, 20, 24, or 32 bits. Any other resolution values are considered invalid. Furthermore, if the
     channel is programmed with an invalid audio resolution, the Rx channel defaults to the maximum audio data
     resolution supported.
     Reprogramming of the audio resolution ensures that the LSB of the received data is placed in the LSB position
     of the Rx FIFO if the resolution of the data being received is reduced.
     Changes to the resolution are programmed by the I2S_RCR0[WLEN] bit field. The Rx channel must be
     disabled prior to any resolution changes. For more information about the Rx channel enable and disable,
     refer to Section 15.5.4.4.2 I2S Receive Channel Enable.
     On reset or if an invalid resolution is selected, the Rx channel audio data resolution defaults back to the to
     the maximum audio data resolution supported.
     For more information about I2S supported audio data resolutions, refer to Section 15.5.1 I2S Overview.

 15.5.4.4.4 I2S Receive Channel FIFO
     The Rx channel has two FIFO banks - for left and right stereo data.
     The FIFO width (word size) is determined by the maximum audio data resolution supported by the I2S.
Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        882
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                           E7 Series


     For more information about I2S supported audio data resolutions and FIFOs depth, refer to Section 15.5.1
     I2S Overview.
     There are several ways to clear the Rx FIFO and reset the read/write pointers:
       n On reset
       n By disabling the I2S (I2S_IER[IEN] = 0x0)
       n By flushing the receiver block (I2S_RXFFR[RXFFR] = 0x1)
       n By flushing the Rx channel (I2S_RFF0[RXCHFR] = 0x1)

     The receiver block/Rx channel must be disabled before the receiver block/Rx channel FIFO can be flushed.
     The default data available trigger threshold level for the Rx FIFO is 3. The trigger level can be set to any value
     in the range of 0 to [FIFO depth – 1]. When this level is reached, an Rx FIFO Data Available interrupt is
     generated. The trigger level can be reprogrammed during operation by writing to the I2S_RFCR0[RXCHDT] bit
     field. The Rx channel must be disabled prior to changing the trigger level.

 15.5.4.4.5 I2S Receive Channel Interrupts
     All interrupts generated from the I2S are active high. The Rx channel generates two interrupts:
       n Rx FIFO Data Available—This interrupt is asserted when the data available trigger threshold level for the
         Rx FIFO is reached. The Rx FIFO Data Available interrupt is cleared by reading data from the Rx FIFO until
         its level drops below the data available trigger threshold level for the channel.
       n Rx FIFO Data Overrun—This interrupt is asserted when an attempt is made to write received data to a
         full Rx FIFO (any data being written is lost, while data in the FIFO is preserved). A Rx FIFO Data Overrun
         interrupt is cleared by reading the I2S_ROR0[RXCHO] bit.
     The interrupt status of the Rx channel can be determined by polling the Interrupt Status Register (I2S_ISR0).
     The I2S_ISR0[RXDA] bit indicates the status of the Rx FIFO Data Available interrupt, while the I2S_ISR0[RXFO]
     bit indicates the status of the Rx FIFO Data Overrun interrupt.
     Both the Rx FIFO Data Available and Rx FIFO Data Overrun interrupts can be masked off by writing 0x1 to the
     I2S_IMR0[RXDAM] and I2S_IMR0[RXFOM] bits, respectively. This prevents the interrupts from driving their
     output lines, however, the I2S_ISR0 register always shows the current status of the interrupts regardless of
     any masking.
     The I2S has a single global interrupt output.

 15.5.4.4.6 Reading from a Receive Channel
     Normally, the stereo data pairs received by the Rx channel are written to the Rx FIFO. The Rx FIFO can be
     read through the Left Receive Buffer register (I2S_LRBR0) and the Right Receive Buffer register (I2S_RRBR0).
     All stereo data pairs must be read using the following two-stage process:
      1. Read the left stereo data from the I2S_LRBR0 register.
      2. Read the right stereo data from the I2S_RRBR0 register.
     The stereo data must be read in this order to avoid the status and interrupt lines becoming out of sync.
     When Rx DMA is enabled, data can be read from the Rx FIFO through the I2S_RXDMA register rather than
     through the I2S_LRBR0 and I2S_RRBR0 registers.

 15.5.4.5.1 I2S Clock Generation Enable
     The I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit enables and disables the Master mode clock signals: WS_OUT, SCLK_EN (external
     SCLK enable signal), and SCLK_GATE. To enable these signals, set the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1. To disable
     them, set the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x0, in which case WS_OUT is held low (WS_OUT = 0).
     When the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit is disabled, any incoming or outgoing data is lost. However, data already in the
     Rx and Tx FIFOs are preserved. After the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit is enabled, transmission recommences at the
     start of the next stereo frame.
     On enabling the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit, WS_OUT always starts in the left stereo data cycle (WS_OUT = 0). One
     SCLK cycle later, it transitions to the right stereo data cycle (WS_OUT = 1); hence—WS 0-to-1 transition. This
     allows for half a frame of SCLK to write data to the Tx FIFO and ensures that any connected slave receivers do
     not miss the start of the data frame (the WS 1-to-0 transition) once SCLK restarts.
     To further explain this behavior, the WS transitions (0-to-1 and 1-to-0) are used by the I2S to clock the start
     of the right or left stereo data cycle. The transition 1-to-0 indicates the start of a new stereo data pair.
     Because the I2S is simple in terms of control, for every 1-to-0 transition, the I2S sends the next entry in its
     FIFO (similarly, the receiver assumes new data is being sent and starts receiving). On enabling the I2S_CER
     [CLKEN] bit, the I2S starts with WS = 0 for one SCLK cycle and then transitions 0-to-1. This allows connected
     devices to clock off the transition and determine which cycle they are in. However, because it is not 1-to-0
     transition, the devices do not have to start Tx or Rx with potential incorrect data (assuming FIFOs are empty

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                              Alif Semiconductor
                                                                 884
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                                        E7 Series


     prior to enable). Additionally, the transmission ensures that after enabling the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit (SCLK_EN
     signal), there is ample time to configure Tx or Rx and to input some data for transmission before the start of
     the next frame.

 15.5.4.5.2 I2S Word Select Generation
     The number of SCLK cycles for which the word select line (WS_OUT) stays in the left or right sample mode
     can be reprogrammed during operation of the I2S by setting the I2S_CCR[WSS] bit field (word select size).
     The clock generation block must be disabled (I2S_CER[CLKEN] = 0x0) before changing the word select size.
     Note that the Word Select Size (WSS) should be equal to or greater than the Rx/Tx channel audio resolution
     to prevent data loss. If this is not observed, the LSB bits of the transmission data and/or the received data are
     truncated.
     The I2S supports 16, 24, or 32 SCLK cycles per left/right WS cycle as presented in Figure 15-62.

 15.5.4.5.3 I2S SCLK Gating
     When the audio data resolution of the Rx and Tx channels is less than the current word select size, the SCLK
     can be gated off for the remainder of the left/right cycle, as presented in Figure 15-63. However, this can be
     reprogrammed during operation of the I2S by setting the I2S_CCR[SCLKG] bit field. The default value of the
     I2S_CCR[SCLKG] bit field is 0x0 (clock gating is disabled).

     The clock generation block must be disabled prior to any changes to SCLK gating value.
     In slave mode, when the word size length is larger than the valid audio bits (word size) then:
       n   The I2S receiver ignores the audio bits after sampling the valid audio bits
       n   The I2S transmitter transmits 0s on the data line after transmitting valid audio bits

 15.5.4.6 I2S DMA Interface
     The I2S has one DMA handshake interface for the Tx channel and one DMA handshake interface for the
     Rx channel. The DMA interface on the Tx/Rx channel can be enabled by setting the DMA Control register
     (I2S_DMACR).
       n Writing 0x1 to the I2S_DMACR[DMAEN_TXBLOCK] bit field, enables the I2S transmit DMA handshake
         interface.
       n Writing 0x1 to the I2S_DMACR[DMAEN_RXBLOCK] bit field, enables the I2S receive DMA handshake
         interface.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                             Alif Semiconductor
                                                                 887
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                               www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     When transmit DMA interface is enabled, data to be transmitted by the Tx channel is written to the Tx FIFO
     through the I2S_TXDMA register.
     When receive DMA interface is enabled, data can be read from the Rx FIFO through the I2S_RXDMA register.

 15.5.4.6.1 Transmit Watermark Level and Transmit FIFO Underflow
     During I2S serial transfers, Tx FIFO requests are made to the DMAC whenever the number of entries in the Tx
     FIFO is less than or equal to the value of the I2S_TFCR0[TXCHET] bit field. This is known as transmit
     Watermark Level (WL). The DMAC responds by writing a burst of data to the Tx FIFO buffer.
     Data should be fetched from the DMA often enough for the Tx FIFO to perform serial transfers continuously;
     that is, when the Tx FIFO begins to empty, another DMA request should be triggered. Otherwise, the Tx FIFO
     runs out of data causing a STOP to be inserted on the I2S bus (Tx FIFO underflow occurs).

 15.5.4.6.1.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level
     The goal in choosing a proper WL is to minimize the number of transactions per DMA block transfer, while at
     the same time keeping the probability of an underflow condition to an acceptable level. In practice, this is a
     function of the ratio of the rate at which the I2S transmits data to the rate at which the DMA controller can
     respond to destination burst requests.
     Figure 15-64 and Figure 15-65 illustrate two example cases for different WL settings. In both examples the
     following assumptions are made:
       n   The needed Number of Burst Transactions (NBT) equals the DMA Transfer Block Size divided by the
           Number of Data Items (NDI) per DMA Burst, as defined by equation 15-11:
                                                                                                              (15-11)

           Where:
           The value of DMA Transfer Block Size is programmed at DMAC level. It defines the number of data
           transfers that the DMAC performs when it writes the destination data. See Section 12.2 DMA
           Controllers for more information.
       n   The value of NDI per DMA Burst is defined by equation 15-12, where:
           l Tx FIFO Depth is as specified in Section 15.5.1 I2S Overview.
           l Tx FIFO WL is programmed in the I2S_TFCR0[TXCHET] bit field.


                                                                                                              (15-12)
     Figure 15-64 (Case 1) shows an example where the selected WL is low. Therefore, the probability of an I2S
     underflow is high where the I2S serial transmit line needs to transmit data, but where there is no data left in
     the Tx FIFO. This occurs because the DMAC has not had time to service the DMA request before the Tx FIFO
     becomes empty.

     Figure 15-65 (Case 2) shows an example where the selected WL is high. Therefore, the probability of an I2S
     underflow is low because the DMAC has plenty of time to service the destination burst transaction request
     before the Tx FIFO becomes empty.

     Figure 15-65 (Case 2) has a lower probability of underflow at possibly the expense of more burst transactions
     per block. This may provide a potentially greater amount of data bursts per block and worse bus utilization
     than Figure 15-64 (Case 1).
     To increase the rate at which the DMA controller can respond to burst transaction requests, the I2S DMA
     channel could be promoted to the highest priority channel in the DMA, and the DMA master interface could
     be promoted to the highest priority master at system interconnect level. This in turn allows to decrease the
     WL, which improves bus utilization without compromising the probability of an underflow occurring.

 15.5.4.6.1.2 Selecting Number of Data Items per DMA Burst and Transmit FIFO Overflow
     As shown in Figure 15-65, programming the NDI per DMA Burst to a value greater than the WL that triggers
     the DMA request may cause overflow when there is not enough space in the Tx FIFO to service the
     destination burst request. Therefore, the equation 15-13 must be adhered to in order to avoid overflow:
                                                                                                                        (15-13)




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                    Alif Semiconductor
                                                                889
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                      www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                           E7 Series


     In Case 2 (refer to Section 15.5.4.6.1.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level), the amount of space in the Tx
     FIFO at the time the burst request is made is equal to the destination burst length (NDI per DMA Burst). Thus,
     the Tx FIFO may be full, but not overflowed, at the completion of the burst transaction.
     For optimal operation, in equation 15-12, the NDI per DMA Burst should be set at the Tx FIFO level that
     triggers a transmit DMA request.
     Adhering to this equation reduces the number of DMA bursts needed for a block transfer, and this in turn
     improves AMBA bus utilization.
     Note that the Tx FIFO is not full at the end of a DMA burst transfer if the I2S has successfully transmitted one
     data item or more on the I2S serial transmit line during the transfer.

 15.5.4.6.2 Receive Watermark Level and Receive FIFO Overflow
     During I2S serial transfers, Rx FIFO requests are made to the DMA controller whenever the number of entries
     in the Rx FIFO is at or above the I2S_RFCR0[RXCHDT] bit field value plus 1. This is known as the WL. The
     DMA controller responds by fetching a burst of data from the Rx FIFO buffer.
     Data should be fetched by the DMA often enough for the Rx FIFO to accept serial transfers continuously (that
     is, when the FIFO begins to fill, another DMA transfer is requested). Otherwise, the FIFO fills with data
     (overflow). To prevent this condition, watermark level must be set correctly.

 15.5.4.6.2.1 Choosing Receive Watermark level
     Similar to choosing the transmit WL described in Section 15.5.4.6.1.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level,
     the receive WL (I2S_RFCR0[RXCHDT] + 1), should be set to minimize the probability of overflow, as shown in
     Figure 15-66. It is a trade-off between the number of DMA burst transactions required per block versus the
     probability of an overflow occurring.

 15.5.4.6.2.2 Selecting Source Burst Transaction Length and Receive FIFO Underflow
     As shown in Figure 15-66, programming a Source Burst Transaction Length greater than the WL may cause
     underflow when there is not enough data to service the source burst request.
     If the NDI in the Rx FIFO is equal to the Source Burst Transaction Length at the time the burst request is
     made—the Rx FIFO may be emptied, but not underflowed, at the completion of the burst transaction. For
     optimal operation, the Source Burst Transaction Length should be set at the WL, as shown in equation (15-
     14):

     Adhering to this equation reduces the number of DMA bursts in a block transfer, which in turn can avoid
     underflow and improve AMBA bus utilization.
     Note that the Rx FIFO is not empty at the end of the source burst transaction if the I2S has successfully
     received one data item or more on the I2S serial receive line (SDI) during the burst.

 15.5.4.7 I2S Programming

 15.5.4.7.1 I2S as Transmitter Master

 15.5.4.7.1.1 Transmitter Master in Normal Mode
     To program the I2S when it is a transmitter in Master mode, complete the following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Transmitter block by setting the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Fill the Tx FIFO by writing data to the Left Transmit Holding register (I2S_LTHR0) and the Right Transmit
         Holding register (I2S_RTHR0), respectively. Keep writing in this order—left and then right—until the FIFO
         is filled with data. The I2S starts transmitting stereo data on the first left cycle when the WS signal goes
         low.
      4. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.

 15.5.4.7.1.2 Transmitter Master in DMA Mode
     To program the I2S as a master transmitter in DMA mode, complete the following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Transmitter block by setting the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Fill the Tx FIFO by writing data to the Transmitter Block DMA register (I2S_TXDMA).
      4. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.

 15.5.4.7.1.3 Transmitter Master with DMA Handshake Interface
     To program the I2S when it is a master transmitter in DMA mode, and with DMA handshake interface
     enabled, complete the following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Transmitter block by setting the I2S_ITER[TXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Enable DMA handshaking by setting the I2S_DMACR[DMAEN_TXBLOCK] bit to 0x1.
      4. Enable the Tx channel by setting the I2S_TER0[TXCHENX] bit to 0x1.
      5. Fill the Tx FIFO by writing to the Transmitter Block DMA register (I2S_TXDMA).
      6. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.

 15.5.4.7.2 I2S as Receiver Master

 15.5.4.7.2.1 Receiver Master in Normal Mode
     To program the I2S when it is a receiver in Master mode, complete the following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Receiver block by setting the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.
      4. Read the I2S_ISR0[RXDA] bit. When the I2S_ISR0[RXDA] bit goes high, the trigger level has been reached.
      5. Read the contents of the Left Receive Buffer register (I2S_LRBR0) and the Right Receive Buffer register
         (I2S_RRBR0).

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       891
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                               E7 Series


 15.5.4.7.2.2 Receiver Master in DMA Mode
     To program the I2S when it is a receiver in Master mode, and when Rx DMA mode is enabled, complete the
     following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Receiver block by setting the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.
      4. Read the I2S_ISR0[RXDA] bit. When the I2S_ISR0[RXDA] bit goes high, the trigger level has been reached.
      5. Read the contents of the Receiver Block DMA register (I2S_RXDMA).

 15.5.4.7.2.3 Receiver Master with DMA Handshake Interface
     To program the I2S when it is a master receiver in DMA mode, with DMA handshake interface enabled,
     complete the following steps:
      1. Enable the I2S by setting the I2S_IER[IEN] bit to 0x1.
      2. Enable the I2S Receiver block by setting the I2S_IRER[RXEN] bit to 0x1.
      3. Enable the I2S Clock Generation block by setting the I2S_CER[CLKEN] bit to 0x1.
      4. Enable DMA handshaking by setting the I2S_DMACR[DMAEN_RXBLOCK] bit to 0x1.
      5. Enable the Rx channel by setting the I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] bit to 0x1.
      6. Empty the Rx FIFO by reading from the Receiver Block DMA register (I2S_RXDMA).

 15.5.5.3.9 I2S_LTHR0 Register
           Offset           Access         Description
         0x20                              Left Transmit Holding Register 0
                              W
     Base address                          This register holds the left transmit stereo data.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            The left stereo data to be transmitted serially through the transmit
                                                            channel output (SDO) is written through this bit field.
                                                            Writing is a two-stage process:
                                                            1. A write to this bit field passes the left stereo sample to the
                                                            transmitter.
    31-0      LTHRX                    W          0x0
                                                            2. This must be followed by writing the right stereo sample to the
                                                            I2S_RTHR0[RTHRX] bit field.
                                                            Note: Data must only be written to the FIFO when it is not full. Any
                                                            attempt to write to a full FIFO results in that data being lost and an
                                                            overrun interrupt being generated.



 15.5.5.3.10 I2S_RRBR0 Register
           Offset           Access         Description
         0x24                              Right Receive Buffer Register 0
                              R
     Base address                          This register specifies the Right Receive Buffer.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                            The right stereo data received serially from the receive channel
                                                            input (SDI) is read through this bit field.
                                                            If the Rx FIFO is full and the two-stage read operation (for
                                                            instance, read from the I2S_LRBR0[LRBRX] bit field followed by a
                                                            read from the I2S_RRBR0[RRBRX] bit field) is not performed before
    31-0      RRBRX                    R          0x0
                                                            the start of the next stereo pair, then the new data is lost and an
                                                            overrun interrupt occurs (data already in the Rx FIFO is preserved).
                                                            Note: Prior to reading this bit field, the left stereo data must be
                                                            read from the I2S_LRBR0[LRBRX] bit field, or the status (interrupts)
                                                            will not be valid.

 15.5.5.3.14 I2S_RCR0 Register
           Offset           Access          Description
         0x30                               Receive Configuration Register 0
                             R/W
     Base address                           This register specifies the desired data resolution of the receiver.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
    31-3      RESERVED                 R           0x0       Reserved.
                                                             This bit field is used to program the desired data resolution of the
                                                             receiver and enables the LSB of the incoming left (or right) word to
                                                             be placed in the LSB of the I2S_LRBR0[LRBRX] (or I2S_RRBR0
                                                             [RRBRX]) bit field.
                                                             Programmed data resolution must be less than or equal to the
                                                             I2S_COMP_PARAM_2[I2S_RX_WORDSIZE_x] bit field value, where
                                                             x = 0 to 3. If the selected resolution is greater than the I2S_COMP_
                                                             PARAM_2[I2S_RX_WORDSIZE_x] bit field value, the receive
                                                             channel defaults back to the to the maximum audio data
    2-0       WLEN                    R/W          0x5       resolution supported.
                                                             The channel must be disabled prior to any changes in this value
                                                             (I2S_RER0[RXCHENX] = 0x0).
                                                             0x0: Ignore the word length
                                                             0x1: 12-bit data resolution of the receiver
                                                             0x2: 16-bit data resolution of the receiver
                                                             0x3: 20-bit data resolution of the receiver
                                                             0x4: 24-bit data resolution of the receiver
                                                             0x5: 32-bit data resolution of the receiver

 15.6 MIPI Improved Inter-Integrated Circuit (I3C)

 15.6.1 I3C Overview
     The MIPI Improved Inter-Integrated Circuit (I3C) provides an interface to external I3C devices.
     The device includes one I3C module in Shared Peripherals.
     The I3C module supports the following main features:
       n Secondary Master function
       n Data rates:
         l Fast Mode (FM) (up to 400 kbps)

         l Fast Mode Plus (FM+) (up to 1 Mbps)

         l Single Data Rate (SDR) (up to 10 Mbps)

         l High Data Rate—Double Data Rate (HDR-DDR) (up to 20 Mbps)

       n Support for legacy I2C devices
       n Separate command and data buffers for each of the transfers
       n Buffer depths (each location can hold 4 bytes of data):
         l Commands buffer: 8 (16 locations)

         l Response buffer: 8 (8 locations)

         l Transmit and receive data buffers: 64 (64 locations) each

       n Up to 216 (65536) write/read bytes with a single command
       n Hardware assisted Dynamic Address Assignment (DAA) support
       n Hardware assisted device role switching between current master and slave
       n Hot-Join support with user controllable filter
       n CRC/parity generation and validation
       n Broadcast and directed Common Command Code (CCC) transfers
       n DMA support through hardware handshake interface
       n Autonomous clock stalling
       n Device address table for addressing multiple slaves
       n Dedicated buffer for capturing information from ENTDAA CCC command
       n Detects arbitration loss due to incoming In-Band Interrupt (IBI) and subsequently re-transmits the
         command
       n Use of duty cycle to achieve lower effective speed for SDR transfers to work with slower I3C slaves
       n Programmable Serial Data (SDA) transmit hold
       n Programmable retry count for transfers that are addressed by slaves
       n IBI with 16 locations of IBI status (no IBI payload)
       n Defining Byte support for vendor specific broadcast and directed CCC transfers

 15.6.4.2 I3C Clocks
     The I3C module uses three identical clocks:
       n PCLK: APB clock for the bus interface unit
       n CORE_CLK: Core interface clock
       n DMA_CLK: SDMA interface clock


 15.6.4.3 I3C Interrupt Requests
     The I3C generates a single interrupt which consolidates (logical OR) all interrupts in interrupt status register.
     The I3C_INTR_STATUS register is associated with error and status condition reporting. This register triggers
     the interrupt signal (I3C_IRQ) which is synchronous with the APB interface clock (PCLK).
     The triggering of interrupt pin can be disabled by the I3C_INTR_SIGNAL_EN register. By default, all interrupts
     are enabled. When any bit of this register is set to 0, it disables the generation of interrupt in that specific
     interrupt pin. Thus, the interrupt signal outputs can be controlled by the I3C_INTR_SIGNAL_EN register.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                            Alif Semiconductor
                                                                912
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                               www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                           E7 Series


     The I3C_INTR_STATUS register is used for checking the true status of the interrupt events which are enabled
     through specific bits in the I3C_INTR_STATUS_EN register. Writing 1 to any bit of the I3C_INTR_STATUS_EN
     register enables the generation of interrupt in that specific I3C_INTR_STATUS register bit and hardware
     interrupt pin, while writing 0 disables it.
     Interrupt bit is always set in the I3C_INTR_STATUS register irrespective of the I3C_INTR_SIGNAL_EN register.
     The I3C_INTR_STATUS[4-0] status interrupts are auto-cleared, while the remaining event-based interrupts
     are cleared through writing 1 to the specific bit in the I3C_INTR_STATUS register.
     The I3C_INTR_FORCE register is used for test purposes, and allows triggering interrupt events individually,
     without the need to activate the conditions that trigger the interrupt sources, since it may be extremely
     complex to generate stimuli for that purpose. This feature also facilitates the development and testing of SW
     associated with the interrupt events. Setting any bit of this register to 1 triggers the corresponding interrupt
     in the I3C_INTR_STATUS register, provided the corresponding bit in the I3C_INTR_STATUS_EN register is set.

 15.6.4.4 I3C DMA Requests
     The I3C has a Simple-transfer DMA (SDMA) handshaking interface to an external DMA controller to request
     and control transfers.
     These transfers are exclusively for:
       n Fetching of the transmit and the receive data
       n Not fetching the I3C command
       n Posting of the I3C response to the memory

     The APB bus is used to perform the data transfer to or from the DMA.
     The I3C communicates with an external DMA. The DMA is always the flow controller for the transmit and
     receive channels. The block size must be programmed by the software in DMA. The DMA always transfers
     data using DMA burst transactions if possible, for efficiency.
     As a block flow control device, the external DMA controller is programmed by the processor with the number
     of data items that are to be transmitted or received by the I3C.
     The block is broken into a number of transactions, each initiated by a request from the I3C.
     The DMA controller must also be programmed with the number of data items to be transferred for each
     DMA request. This is also known as burst transaction length and is programmed into the SRC_MSIZE/DEST_
     MSIZE fields of the DMA control register.
     The programmed values for the MSIZE in DMA must be same as that programmed in I3C_DATA_BUFFER_
     THLD_CTRL register in RX_BUF_THLD and TX_EMPTY_BUF_THLD fields for source and destination
     respectively.
     When the block size programmed into the DMA controller is not a multiple of the burst transaction length, a
     series of burst transactions followed by single transactions are needed to complete the block transfer.
     Burst Transfer:
     For every request from the I3C, the DMA is going to provide data, which is 16 bytes. The I3C generates the
     burst request to the DMA (asserting DMA_REQ_TX) whenever the number of available locations in the
     transmit FIFO is greater than or equal to I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_CTRL[TX_EMPTY_BUF_THLD] register
     bitfield.
     Single Transfer:
     The DMA, after transferring the 32 bytes in burst, enters the single transfer region. It samples the DMA_
     SINGLE_TX signal, and if it is asserted, transfers the remaining three bytes of data in single transfers which is

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                            Alif Semiconductor
                                                        913
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                              www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     packed into 4 bytes (the MSB being invalid) of data to the input to the I3C as the DST_TR_WIDTH is 32 as
     mentioned in Burst Transfer for I3C.
     The I3C asserts the DMA_SINGLE_TX when there is at least one free entry in the transmit FIFO and clear
     when the transmit FIFO is full.

     The total depth of SPRAM is calculated as a sum of the following parameters:

 15.6.4.6 I3C Master Dynamic Address Assignment (DAA)

 15.6.4.6.1 Overview of DAA
     The I3C, configured as Main Master, is responsible for performing a Dynamic Address Assignment (DAA)
     procedure, to provide a unique dynamic address to each I3C device connected to the I3C bus.
     Once a device receives a dynamic address, this assigned dynamic address is used in all the device subsequent
     transactions on the I3C bus.

 15.6.4.6.2 Description of DAA Methods

 15.6.4.6.2.1 SETDASA Procedure: Format 1
     The I3C assigns dynamic address to any I3C device with known static address using the directed command
     code—Set Dynamic Address from Static Address (SETDASA). This is faster than using the ENTDAA procedure.
     The SETDASA process is initiated by the Main Master after cold power-up of the system.
     The following flow describes the DAA using SETDASA procedure:


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                                914
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                        E7 Series


      1. The application initializes the I3C
      2. The application programs the device address table
      3. The application generates the address assignment command with the following:
         a. SETDASA command code in the CMD field
         b. DEV_INDEX field pointing the location in the device address table from where the dynamic address is
            to be assigned
         c. DEVICE_COUNT field indicates the number of devices to be assigned with the dynamic address by
            incrementing the DEV_INDEX field of the same command sequentially as many times as DEVICE_
            COUNT. Program the DEVICE_COUNT value in such a way that DEVICE_COUNT + DEV_INDEX should
            not cross the device address table depth
      4. The I3C starts executing the SETDASA CCC transfer as soon as the address assignment command is
         generated
      5. The DAA continues until one of the following conditions occurs:
         a. NACK response is received and no I3C devices present
         b. NACK response is received and not a valid static address or the device exist
         c. DEVICE_COUNT reaches zero (end of address assignment request)
      6. The I3C writes the transfer complete status into the command response queue. The data length field of
         response data structure indicates the remaining device count, if the transfer is terminated suddenly due
         to NACK response from the slave.

 15.6.4.6.2.2 SETDASA Procedure: Format 2
     The SETDASA CCC may also be specially used for simple point-to-point communication in the I3C minimal bus
     use cases. An I3C minimal bus is an I3C bus with one I3C master device and one I3C slave device.
     In this special usage of the SETDASA CCC, the master device uses the fixed value of 7h as the static address,
     and uses the fixed (and reserved) value of 7h as the dynamic address.
     The following flow describes the DAA using SETDASA procedure in point-to-point communication:
      1. The application initializes the I3C controller.
      2. The application programs the device address table.
      3. The application generates the address assignment command with the following:
         a. SETDASA command code in the CMD field
         b. DEV_INDEX field pointing the location in the device address table in which the static and dynamic
             addresses are mentioned to be assigned
         c. DEVICE_COUNT field is programmed to 1 as there is only one device to be assigned with the dynamic
             address
      4. The I3C starts executing the SETDASA CCC transfer as soon as the address assignment command is
         generated.
      5. The DAA continues until one of the following conditions occur:
         a. NACK response is received for no I3C devices present
         b. NACK response is received for not a valid static address or the device does not exist
         c. DEVICE_COUNT reaches zero (end of address assignment request)
      6. The controller writes the transfer complete status into the command response queue. The data length
         field of response data structure indicates remaining device count in case if the transfer is terminated
         suddenly due to NACK response from the slave.

 15.6.4.6.2.3 ENTDAA Procedure
     The I3C assigns dynamic address to any I3C device not assigned earlier with dynamic address, using the
     broadcast command code—Enter Dynamic Address Assignment (ENTDAA). This process is initiated by the I3C

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                         Alif Semiconductor
                                                       915
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                           www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     after cold power-up, after completing the DAA for static address devices using SETDASA procedure or if a
     hot-join request is received from any I3C device. The Main Master may choose to use a single or multiple
     ENTDAA address assignment command to assign a dynamic address for all the connected I3C devices. The
     number of devices that can be assigned to a single command is limited by the configured value of the device
     address table and the device characteristics table.
     The following flow describes the DAA using ENTDAA procedure:
      1. The application initializes the I3C controller.
      2. The application programs the device address table with the data structure.
      3. The application generates the address assignment command with the following:
         a. ENTDAA command code in the CMD field
         b. DEV_INDEX field pointing the location in the device address table from where the dynamic address is
            to be assigned
         c. DEVICE_COUNT field indicating the number of devices to be assigned with the dynamic address with
            the single command. DEVICE_COUNT value cannot be more than the 8, and the value should be
            programmed such that DEVICE_COUNT + DEV_INDEX should not exceed the DAT table depth.
      4. The I3C starts executing the ENTDAA CCC transfer as soon as the address assignment command is
         generated.
      5. The first device gets the first dynamic address pointed by the DEV_INDEX of the command. The second
         device gets the second dynamic address pointed by the DEV_INDEX + 1, and so on. The received 48-bit
         PID, BCR and DCR along with the assigned dynamic address are captured in the device characteristics
         table.
      6. The DAA continues until one of the following conditions occurs:
         a. NACK response is received and no I3C devices present
         b. NACK response is received and all devices got the dynamic address
         c. NACK response received for the assigned dynamic address (error detected by the receiving I3C device
            on the dynamic address)
         d. DEVICE_COUNT reaches zero regardless of the number of devices yet to be assigned to the dynamic
            address (end of address assignment request)
      7. The I3C writes the transfer complete status into the command response queue. The data length field of
         response data structure indicates remaining device count in case if the transfer is terminated suddenly
         due to NACK response from the slave.

 15.6.4.6.2.4 SETAASA Procedure
     The I3C can also request for all connected slaves to use their known static address as their dynamic address.
     This is the fastest method to assign I3C dynamic addresses to all slaves with static addresses. The application
     must use regular transfer command instead of address assignment command to generate SETAASA transfer
     command.
     The following flow describes the DAA using SETAASA procedure:
      1. The application initializes the I3C.
      2. The application generates the regular transfer command to generate broadcast SETAASA CCC transfer
         without data payload.
      3. The I3C starts executing the SETAASA CCC transfer as soon as the regular transfer command is
         generated.
      4. The DAA continues until it generates SETAASA CCC on the line or it ends if it receives NACK response for
         no I3C devices present.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       916
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


      5. The controller writes the transfer complete status in to the command response queue. The ERR_STS
         field indicates whether the transfer is completed successfully, or it has terminated suddenly due to
         NACK response from the slaves.

 15.6.4.7 I3C Master In-Band Interrupt Detection and Handling
     The I3C slave devices can initiate communication to the current master through In-Band Interrupt (IBI).
     The following types of IBI are possible on an I3C bus:
       n Hot-Join Request (HJ) from a hot-join capable slave
       n Slave Interrupt Request (SIR) from a slave
       n Master Ownership Request (MR) from a master capable slave (secondary master)

     The I3C master has to be enabled to allow it to detect (SDA low) and receive the In-Band Interrupt (IBI ID).
     This enables the I3C master to start providing the SCL clocks to receive the IBI ID from the requesting slave
     device. The SCL clock period is defined by: I3C_SCL_I3C_OD_TIMING[I3C_OD_LCNT] + [I3C_OD_HCNT].
     The I3C master detects the IBI in the following scenarios:
       n Upon detecting low on the SDA input port after a POR
       n Upon detecting an arbitration loss during an address phase of any master-initiated transfer following a
         START condition (not RESTART)
       n Upon detecting the SDA input port going low (not initiated by the controller) following a STOP condition
         (slave-initiated IBI)
                                    Table 15-83 IBI Response and Notify Controls(1)
                       Control                                               Associated Register
  I3C Controller Enable                                I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ENABLE]
  MR Response Control (to slave)                       I3C_IBI_MR_REQ_REJECT[MR_REQ_REJECT]
  SIR Response Control (to slave)                      I3C_IBI_SIR_REQ_REJECT[SIR_REQ_REJECT]
  HJ Response Control (to slave)                       I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[HOT_JOIN_CTRL]
  MR Reject Notify Control (to APP)                    I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_MR_REJECTED]
  SIR Reject Notify Control (to APP)                   I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_SIR_REJECTED]
  HJ Reject Notify Control (to APP)                    I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_HJ_REJECTED]
     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.



 15.6.4.7.1 Hot-Join Request (HJ)
     If the received IBI ID matches with the Hot-Join ID (0x2, RnW = 0), then the response for the received HJ
     request is based on the programmed 'HJ Response Control' (I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[HOT_JOIN_CTRL]).
     If I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[HOT_JOIN_CTRL] = 0, then the controller responds to the HJ request with ACK and sets
     IBI_STS field to ACK to indicate to the application that the controller has ACK'ed to the received HJ request.
     If I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[HOT_JOIN_CTRL] = 1, then the controller responds to the HJ request with NACK followed
     by issuing a broadcast DISEC CCC command (DISHJ bit set) with the RESTART condition. This disables the HJ
     request generation from all the unaddressed devices at that instant. The controller sets the IBI_STS field to
     NACK to indicate to the application that the controller has rejected the received HJ request. The application
     can optionally set the 'HJ Reject Notify Control' (I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_HJ_REJECTED]) to get an IBI
     status for a rejected HJ request. Otherwise, the controller moderates the IBI status generation for rejected HJ
     requests.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                                917
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


     Based on the IBI status for the HJ request, the application must issue the ENTDAA CCC to assign the dynamic
     address for the devices that generates the HJ request.

 15.6.4.7.2 Master Request (MR)
     If the received IBI ID matches with the dynamic address of any one of the valid entries in the DAT and the
     received RnW bit is 0, then the response for the received MR is based on the programmed 'MR Response
     Control' (I3C_IBI_MR_REQ_REJECT).

 15.6.4.7.2.1 MR Response Control
     The controller handles the MR response to the targeted slave through a 32-bit vector control register (I3C_
     IBI_MR_REQ_REJECT). This register is used to control the response individually for each I3C master capable
     slave device. Each bit of the control register is mapped to a unique 7-bit slave device address through the
     modular arithmetic operation:
       n   mod32{IBI_ID[4-0] + IBI_ID[6-5]}
     The sum of the lower five bits and the upper two bits of the MR ID (Dynamic Address of the requesting slave)
     is wrap around upon reaching the value 32 (module 32) to uniquely map the bit position of the 32-bit control
     register.
     If the 'MR Response Control' bit is 0, then the controller responds to the MR request with ACK and sets IBI_
     STS field to ACK, which indicates to the application that the controller has ACK'ed the received MR request.
     If the 'MR Response Control' bit is 1, then the controller responds to the MR request with NACK followed by
     issuing a directed DISEC CCC command (DISMR bit set) with the RESTART condition to the MR initiated slave.
     The controller sets the IBI_STS field as NACK to indicate to the application that the controller has rejected the
     received MR request. The application can optionally set the 'MR Reject Notify Control' (I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL
     [NOTIFY_MR_REJECTED]) to get an IBI status for a rejected MR request. Otherwise, the controller moderates
     the IBI status generation for rejected MR requests.
     Based on the IBI status for the MR request, the application must follow the master ownership handover
     procedure.

 15.6.4.7.3 Slave Interrupt Request (SIR)
     If the received IBI ID matches with the dynamic address of any one of the valid entries in the DAT and the
     received RnW bit is 1, then the response for the received SIR is based on the programmed 'SIR Response
     Control' (I3C_IBI_SIR_REQ_REJECT).
     The following SIR features are NOT supported by the I3C controller (secondary master configuration):
       n   SIR with payload
       n   SIR auto-command

 15.6.4.7.3.1 SIR Response Control
     The controller handles the SIR response to the targeted slave through a 32-bit vector control register (I3C_
     IBI_SIR_REQ_REJECT). This register is used to control the response individually for each I3C slave device. Each
     bit of the control register is mapped to a unique 7-bit slave device address through the modular arithmetic
     operation:
       n   mod32{IBI_ID[4-0] + IBI_ID[6-5]}




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        918
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                            E7 Series


     The sum of the lower five bits and the upper two bits of the SIR ID (Dynamic Address of the requesting slave)
     is wrap around upon reaching the value 32 (module 32) to uniquely map the bit position of the 32-bit control
     register.
     If the 'SIR Response Control' bit is 0, then the controller ACKs the SIR.
     If the 'SIR Response Control' bit is 1, then the controller NACKs the SIR and then issues a directed DISEC CCC
     command (DISINT bit set) with the RESTART condition targeting the matching dynamic address. This disables
     the SIR generation in the requesting slave device. The IBI status for the corresponding SIR indicates to the
     application that the incoming IBI is NACK'ed through IBI_STS descriptor.

 15.6.4.7.4 IBI Queue Data Structure
     The IBI queue comprises of the status generated from the controller for the respective data slice of HJ, SIR or
     MR. Because the configuration does not support IBI with payload, only IBI status entry is written into the IBI
     queue.
     Figure 15-72 shows an example of the IBI queue data structure holding only the IBI status. This structure is
     applicable for all the IBI that does not support the payload, which includes HJ, SIR without payload, and MR.
                                      Figure 15-72 IBI without Payload Queue Structure(1)

                                            Only IBI Status
                                                                      IBI Status, DL = 0, L = 1
                                                                                                                       I3C-008




     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.



 15.6.4.7.5 IBI Notification Control
     Normally, the controller generates an IBI response only for the received IBIs for which ACK response is sent.
     Optionally, user can enable the response generation for the NACK'ed IBIs by setting the appropriate 'Reject
     Notify Control' (see Table 15-83).
     When I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_HJ_REJECTED] = 1, the I3C notifies the application by generating an IBI
     response when a valid HJ request is received, for which a NACK response was sent followed by broadcast
     auto-disable CCC command.
     When I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_MR_REJECTED] = 1, the I3C notifies the application by generating an IBI
     response when a valid MR request is received, for which a NACK response is sent followed by directed auto-
     disable CCC command to the requesting slave device.
     When I3C_IBI_QUEUE_CTRL[NOTIFY_SIR_REJECTED] = 1, the I3C notifies the application by generating an IBI
     response when a valid SIR request is received, for which a NACK response is sent followed by directed auto-
     disable CCC command to the requesting slave device.

 15.6.4.8 I3C Master Disabling
     The application can disable I3C when operating as a master at any time by clearing the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL
     [ENABLE] bit. The application should then poll the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ENABLE] bit for until it turns to 0 for
     confirming that the controller is in disabled state. If the master controller is busy in executing any I3C bus
     transfers (like receiving/transmitting an I3C transfer or receiving an IBI), then it enters the disabled state only
     after completing either the transfer command with TOC = 1 or the IBI reception. Once the master controller

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                             Alif Semiconductor
                                                                919
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                               www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                             E7 Series


     enters the disabled state, it does not execute any commands from the command queue and does not provide
     any clock for a new IBI. The application is expected to flush/drain all queues and FIFOs before re-enabling the
     controller.

 15.6.4.9 I3C Master Aborting Transfer
     The application of the master can request the I3C controller to abort any ongoing I3C bus transfer by setting
     the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ABORT] bit.
     In response to an abort request, the controller generates the STOP condition after the on-going data byte is
     transferred or received. The I3C then generates an interrupt, sets the I3C_INTR_STATUS[TRANSFER_ABORT_
     STAT] bit and enters the HALT state.
     The controller then waits for the application to issue the resume command by setting the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL
     [RESUME] bit to exit the HALT state. The application is expected to flush/drain all queues and FIFOs before
     programming the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[RESUME] bit to resume the controller.

 15.6.4.10 I3C Master Data Structures

 15.6.4.10.4.1 Device Address Table Registers
     The DAT is used to store the addresses of the devices that are attached to the I3C bus. The DAT registers are
     implemented in the external RAM. To initiate transfers to a device on the I3C bus, its information should be
     available in the DAT register. One DAT register is required per device. The DAT registers are named as I3C_
     DEV_ADDR_TABLE_LOCx, where x is from 1 to 11.

 15.6.4.10.5 Device Characteristics Table Data Structure
     The Device Characteristics Table (DCT) is used to capture the received device characteristics information (PID,
     BCR, DCR) and assigned dynamic address by the master for the participating devices during ENTDAA CCC
     command.
     The information captured during ENTDAA CCC can be used by the application to know what dynamic address
     is assigned to a particular slave with the captured characteristics. The application should update the DAT
     table based on the characteristics received during the ENTDAA procedure.

 15.6.4.11 I3C Operation Modes
     The I3C supports the following bus communication protocols to transfer the data between master and slave.
       n Single Data Rate (SDR) Transfer
         l Broadcast CCC Write Transfer

         l Direct CCC Write or Read Transfer

         l I3C Private Write or Read Transfer

         l I2C Private Write or Read Transfer

       n High Data Rate (HDR) Transfer
         l High Data Rate-Double Data Rate (HDR-DDR) Transfer



 15.6.4.11.1 Single Data Rate Transfers
     In SDR mode, single bit is sent on each SCL clock. All data is transmitted in byte format, with no limit on the
     number of transferred bytes. After the master sends the address and R/W bit, the slave receiver responds to
     the acknowledge signal (ACK). When a slave-receiver does not respond with an ACK pulse, the master aborts
     the transfer by generating a STOP condition. The slave leave the SDA line high, so that the master can abort
     the transfer.
     The single data rate transfers are initiated by the application through the command as explained in Table 15-
     84. Based on the command initiated by the application and device address pointed by the DEV_INDX field
     initiates command, the I3C initiate the transfers on the bus.
     Table 15-90 gives the decoded transfer type based on Transfer Command and DAT.

 15.6.4.11.2 Broadcast or Directed CCC Transfers
     The CCC transfers are used for the bus management procedures such as the following:
       n Receiving the device characteristics
       n Setting the max write or read data length
       n Enabling or disabling the event generation in the I3C devices
       n Informing the bus characteristics to all the existing devices
       n Entering the high data rate transfer modes

 15.6.4.11.2.3 Directed CCC Transfer to Multiple Slaves
     Each transfer command initiates Directed CCC transfer to only one slave since it consists of only one DEV_
     INDX/SLV_ADDR field. To transfer the Directed CCC command to multiple devices, pipeline the multiple
     transfer commands with TOC bits set to 0 and with the different DEV_INDX or SLV_ADDR fields pointing to
     multiple slaves.
     The I3C decodes the pipelined Transfer Command during the transfer of Directed CCC transfer and decides
     the next transfer based on the following:

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                      Alif Semiconductor
                                                                931
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                         www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                         E7 Series


       n If the current command and the pipelined command has same Directed CCC, then the I3C targets the
         next slave without ending the CCC command.
       n If the current command and the pipelined command are not the same Directed CCC, then the I3C ends
         the CCC command and starts generating the next transfer as indicated by the pipelined transfer
         command.
     The application can set the ROC bit to 0 for the subsequent Directed CCC commands and enable the ROC bit
     in the last CCC command if Directed CCC transfer is targeted to multiple devices to avoid unnecessary
     responses.
     The I3C halts in case of the following conditions:
       n   Receiving NACK for the address header of the Directed CCC transfer (no I3C device on the bus)
       n   Receiving NACK for the slave address of the Directed CCC transfer
     The I3C updates the ERR_STS field with appropriate error information in the response status status, halts the
     the I3C and gives back the control to the application to resume the operation of the I3C through writing 1 to
     the resume bit of the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL register.

 15.6.4.11.5 Implication of Tx FIFO Empty and Rx FIFO Full Conditions
     At SDR speeds, the I3C extends the clock by pulling the SCL low under the following conditions:
       n   Tx FIFO empty during the middle of write data transfer at SDR speeds
       n   Rx FIFO full during the middle of read data transfer at SDR speeds



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                                933
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                   E7 Series


 15.6.4.11.6 Implication of TOC and ROC Bit Settings for SDR Transfers
     The Termination on Completion (TOC) of Transfer Command is used to decide whether to generate a STOP or
     continue with the next transfer.
       n If TOC bit is set to 1, then the I3C generates STOP condition after the end of the transfer.
       n If TOC bit is set to 0, then the I3C continues the next pipelined transfer based on the current transfer
         type:
         l If the current transfer is either Broadcast CCC write or private transfer, then the I3C generates

            RESTART after the end of the transfer.
         l If the current transfer is the Directed CCC transfer, then the I3C generates RESTART followed by a

            reserved address (0x7E) after the end of the transfer.
       n If TOC bit is set to 0 and the next pipelined command is not available, then the I3C extends the clock by
         pulling SCL low until the next command is available.
     The Response on Completion (ROC) bit of the Transfer Command is used to generate the response status of
     the transfer after the end of the transfer. The Response status is automatically generated if any error
     condition is occurred for the transfer irrespective of the ROC bit.

 15.6.4.11.7 High Data Rate Transfers
     The HDR transfer protocols are different from SDR protocol and is used to transfer more data at the same
     SDR frequency. The HDR mode has bus-wide effect and master is required to enter an HDR mode through
     CCC before initiating a transfer to the slave. The slaves decode the incoming CCC and enter the HDR mode for
     the reception of the transfer.
     The following HDR mode is supported by the I3C:
       n   HDR-DDR (Double Data Rate) mode

 15.6.4.11.7.1 High Data Rate-Double Data Rate Transfers
     The HDR-DDR write and read transfers are initiated on settings, as shown in Table 15-95.

     The I3C generates the ENTHDR0 CCC to enter into the HDR-DDR mode and forms the command code through
     the CMD field of Transfer Command and slave address. The preamble and parity bits are generated by the
     I3C as per the protocol and sends along with the write data word. The I3C considers word from the Tx-FIFO
     and appends the parity bits and preamble bits to form the write data word and transmits the data. The HDR-
     RESTART and HDR-EXIT pattern is generated in place of RESTART and STOP condition.
     To avoid the initial latencies of the transfer, the I3C uses TX/RX_START_THLD before initiating the transfer.
     The TX_START_THLD indicates whether the threshold level of data is present in the transmit buffer for write
     transfer or RX_START_THLD level of space is available in the receive buffer for the read transfer before
     initiating the transfer.
     This threshold is only applicable for the transfers which are initiated with the START or RESTART condition. If
     the threshold amount of write data in the Tx-FIFO or empty space in Rx-FIFO is not available, the controller
     waits until the threshold amount of data is available to initiate the transfer. If the threshold amount of data is
     not available for the HDR-DDR transfer initiated, which must be initiated with RESTART, then the I3C
     generates EXIT pattern followed by STOP for the current transfer and waits for the threshold amount of data
     and initiate the next transfer with a START condition.
     The I3C halts in case of the following conditions:
       n Receiving NACK for the address header of the private transfers.
       n Receiving NACK for the slave address of the HDR-DDR private transfers.
       n If the controller experiences the Transfer Underflow or Receive Overflow during the HDR-DDR transfers.
       n After executing software initiated abort.
       n The I3C decodes the parity bits, CRC byte, frame mismatch and validates them for the read transfer and
         report in the ERR_STS field of the response status if there is any error.
     The I3C updates the ERR_STS field with appropriate error information in the response status and halts the
     controller and gives back the control to the application to resume the operation of the I3C through writing 1
     to the resume bit of the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL register.

 15.6.4.11.8 Clock Stalling Conditions
     The I3C stalls SCL clock during specific scenarios. This is to accommodate intermittent system latencies during
     command pipelining, transmit data prefetching, response reading, and so on. The I3C also provides additional
     knobs in the form of start thresholds and buffer thresholds to avoid clock stalling.
     Clock stalling is a feature that helps avoid overrun and underrun errors. The I3C software receiving these
     errors is an indication of a larger issue in itself and neither clock stalling by itself or termination of transfers
     during clock stalling is the solution.
     The FIFO size should be twice of what is likely to be the maximum value of threshold. This facilitates smooth
     and seamless handshake between software and hardware.

 15.6.4.11.9.4 Packing of Any Read Data
     The I3C does not distinguish read data coming from a private read transfer and read data coming from a CCC.
     The I3C is also transparent to CCC, that is, it does not decode the CCC as a master and does not treat CCC
     differently from one another. The data packing logic for CCC also follows the same rules as mentioned for
     private transfers. Therefore, for CCC, it is expected that the software performs byteswap while reading the
     data to get the required byte endianness.

     As mentioned in Table 15-97, the I3C protocol specification recommends to extend the low period (varying
