 15.6.4.13.2.1 Error Type M0
     If the I3C detects an illegally formatted CCC, then it stops the transmission, sends STOP, and retries the
     transmission.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                     Alif Semiconductor
                                                                940
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                       www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                   E7 Series


     An example of an illegally formatted CCC is the I3C receiving just one byte from the slave in a GETMWL CCC
     code. This is because the I3C expects two bytes.
     The I3C does not decode the CCC as it is transparent for the application. The I3C always initiates the CCC
     transfer and expects the number of bytes as mentioned in DATA_LENGTH field of Transfer Argument.
     If the slave terminates earlier than the DATA_LENGTH expected by the controller, the controller represents it
     in the DATA_LENGTH of the RESPONSE.
     The application has to decode this information through RESPONSE of the CCC transfer and can re-generate
     the same command in the I3C_COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT register for retransmission.

 15.6.4.13.2.2 Error Type M2
     If the I3C does not receive an ACK of a transmitted Broadcast address (0x7E), then it transmits the HDR exit
     pattern followed by STOP.
     The I3C always generates STOP upon receiving NACK for the Broadcast address (0x7E) and enters the HALT
     state. This can be detected through the I3C_INTR_STATUS[TRANSFER_ERR_STS] bit field.

 15.6.4.14 I3C Master Defining Byte Support
     The Defining Byte support feature is an extended feature to the existing CCC transfers model. The Defining
     Byte is included after the CCC code and before the payload (in broadcast CCC) or restart (in directed CCC) to
     indicate an extended capability or an action associated with the CCC. The Defining Byte is supported for both
     broadcast and directed SDR CCC transfers. In both cases, the Defining Byte is included after CCC code byte as
     sub-command before the payload.
     Figure 15-85 and Figure 15-86 describe the placement of the Defining Byte in broadcast CCC and directed
     CCC transfer.

 15.6.4.15 I3C Master Bus Reset Generation
     To prevent a malfunctioning device from locking up the I3C bus, the I3C specification defines a bus protocol
     reset mechanism.
     The I3C master controller supports the generation of following two bus reset patterns:
       n   SCL timed reset
       n   HDR exit pattern
     The reset pattern is selected in the I3C_RESET_CTRL[BUS_RESET_TYPE] field and to request the command, it
     is required to write 1 to the I3C_RESET_CTRL[BUS_RESET] field. The I3C considers this request only when it is
     in IDLE state and gives priority over scheduled regular commands. The master controller generates the timed
     reset by driving SCL low for I3C_SCL_LOW_MST_EXT_TIMEOUT[SCL_LOW_MST_TIMEOUT_COUNT] period of
     time. Once the I3C completes the timed reset, it auto-clears the I3C_RESET_CTRL[BUS_RESET] field. Software
     can poll this request bit to know whether the controller has completed the generation of the requested reset
     pattern. If enabled, the I3C_INTR_STATUS[BUS_RESET_DONE_STS] interrupt is generated indicating that the
     requested reset pattern is complete.
     The HDR exit pattern is defined as follows:
       n   SDA starts high, SCL starts low
       n   SDA falls from high-to-low four times, while SCL remains low for the whole time
     Figure 15-87 and Figure 15-88 show the SCL timed reset and HDR exit pattern, respectively.
                                                    Figure 15-87 SCL Timed Reset(1)


                       SDA


                                                                                                                         I3C-023
                        SCL

     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


                                              Figure 15-88 HDR Exit Pattern (with Stop)(1)
                            Setup (SDA/SCL)
                              (if needed)                                             End/Exit   Stop

                        SCL

     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.



 15.6.4.16 I3C Master Broadcast CCC in I2C Speed
     The I3C allows to generate certain Broadcast CCCs (DEVCTRL and SETHID) in I2C mode to indicate bus context
     before address assignment with SETAASA CCC. The I3C mandates to send these Broadcast CCCs from the
     master in limited speed 1 MHz to guarantee that these CCCs are registered by the slave devices without any
     error.

     The Broadcast CCCs with I2C FM speed are generating by setting the TRANSFER_COMMAND[SPEED] field to
     I2C FM. The I3C generates those CCCs in I3C protocol mode with I2C FM speed.

 15.6.4.18 I3C Slave Role Overview
     The I3C slave can be selected either as a static address device or a dynamic address only device.
     This selection can be done in the following way:
       n I3C_DEVICE_ADDR[STATIC_ADDR_VALID] = 0: implies that the I3C is a dynamic address only device. The
         master is responsible for setting the I3C_DEVICE_ADDR[DYNAMIC_ADDR_VALID] and [DYNAMIC_ADDR]
         fields during DAA.
       n I3C_DEVICE_ADDR[STATIC_ADDR_VALID] = 1: implies that the I3C is a static address device. The user can
         set the desired static address through the I3C_DEVICE_ADDR[STATIC_ADDR] field.
     The reset values of the STATIC_ADDR_VALID and STATIC_ADDR fields are set from corresponding I3C input
     ports. Application can overwrite these values by programming this register before enabling the controller.
     If the I3C is selected as a dynamic address device, then the device responds for only ENTDAA CCC command
     from the current master until the dynamic address is assigned successfully.
     If the I3C is selected as a static address device, then the device responds for both ENTDAA and SETDASA CCC
     commands from the current master until the dynamic address is assigned successfully.
     Once the dynamic address is assigned and valid, then the I3C stops responding for the ENTDAA and SETDASA
     CCC commands until the dynamic address is reset through RSTDAA CCC command.
     The SETNEWDA CCC from the current master allows the I3C slave to replace the current dynamic address
     with a new dynamic address.

 15.6.4.19 I3C Slave vs I2C Slave Role Selection
     The I3C slave controller can be selected as an I3C slave or as an I2C slave by two ways:
       n If the I3C strap input 'mode_i2c' is driven to 1, it brings up the slave controller as an I2C slave. Once
         selected as an I2C slave, the role cannot be changed until reset and after the 'mode_i2c' strap is driven
         to 0.
       n Adaptive selection: The adaptive selection is possible only when the 'mode_i2c' strap is driven to 0.
         During initial power-up, the I3C controller is in I2C mode as it does not have any Dynamic Address (DA)



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                         Alif Semiconductor
                                                                944
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                           www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                            E7 Series


           assigned to it. The mode changes to I3C only when a DA is assigned by any of DAA procedures as per the
           I3C protocol. The mode changes back again to I2C when RSTDAA CCC is issued or upon hardware reset.
     The 'mode_i2c' strap input is driven by the system control register bit: I3C_CTRL[I2C_MODE].
     To enable the static address match to happen, the application must enable the static address as mentioned
     in Section 15.6.4.18 I3C Slave Role Overview. Once in I2C role, the slave controller ignores all I3C related
     transfers like IBI, HJ and all the CCCs.
     In I2C mode of operation, clock stretching is not supported by the slave controller. The spike filter required
     for I2C device should be present outside the controller's interface and is not a part of the deliverable, only
     the control to enable or disable the spike filter is provided from the controller. Until the Dynamic Address is
     assigned either through ENTDAA or SETDASA CCC, the controller remains in I2C mode. Once the Dynamic
     Address is assigned and valid, the controller switches to I3C mode.
     If the auto generation of HJ is to be disabled until the correct mode of operation is identified, then the slave
     application must set the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ADAPTIVE_I2C_I3C] bit. If this bit is set, then the slave controller
     initiates a HJ request to the I3C master only when a 0x7E header is received on the bus and changes to I3C
     mode of operation.

 15.6.4.19.1 Conditions for Mode Change
     On power-up, the slave controller is in I2C mode and it changes state under the following conditions:
       n The slave controller changes to I3C mode when a dynamic address is assigned by any of the Dynamic
         Address Assignment (DAA) procedures as per the I3C specification.
       n The slave controller changes to I2C mode when a RSTDAA CCC is received from the master. The slave
         controller responds to transfers matching its static address in I2C mode.
       n On POR, the controller is in I2C mode.


 15.6.4.19.2 Conditions for Glitch Filter Enable/Disable
     On power-up, the glitch filter is enabled. In adaptive mode, the glitch filter is disabled by the I3C controller.
     Once disabled, it is in disabled state until POR. The glitch filter is always enabled if 'mode_i2c' strap input is
     high (system control register bit I3C_CTRL[I2C_MODE] = 1).

 15.6.4.20 I3C Slave Handling Address Assignment
     If the I3C is selected as a static address device, then the device responds for both ENTDAA and SETDASA CCC
     commands from the current master until the dynamic address is assigned successfully.
     If the I3C is selected as a dynamic address device, then the device responds for only ENTDAA CCC command
     from the current master until the dynamic address is assigned successfully.
     Once the dynamic address is assigned and valid, then the I3C stops responding for the ENTDAA and SETDASA
     CCC commands until the dynamic address is reset through RSTDAA CCC command.

 15.6.4.21.2 Description of CCC Transfers with I3C Slave
     The I3C slave collects the required CCC information to enable the I3C to handle the CCC transfers. During run
     time, the I3C does not involve the application to handle any CCC transfers. Upon receiving a CCC command
     from the master, the I3C handles it in one of the three ways—through configured parameters, through port
     signals or through internal registers.

 15.6.4.21.2.4 Handling of GETMXDS CCC
     Whether or not GETMXDS CCC is ACK-ed by the slave controller is determined by the value programmed in

       n I3C_MAX_DATA_SPEED[MXDS_MAX_WR_SPEED]

     The reset values of the three fields in the I3C_MAX_DATA_SPEED register are set from corresponding I3C
     strap inputs. Application can overwrite these values by programming this register before enabling the I3C.

 15.6.4.21.2.5 Handling of GETSTATUS CCC
     Figure 15-89 shows the format of the GETSTATUS CCC as supported by the I3C.
                                                  Figure 15-89 GETSTATUS CCC Format(1)

             15:14      13           12          11          10         9          8           7:6          5          4           3:0


                      FRAME_       BUFFER_    DATA_NOT_   OVERFLOW_            UNDERFLOW_   ACTIVITY_   PROTOCOL_               PENDING_
           RESERVED                                                 SLAVE_BUSY                                      RESERVED
                      ERROR       NOT_AVAIL     READY        ERR                  ERR        MODE          ERR                    INTR




                                      Vendor Reserved Fields                                                                               I3C-025




     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     The GETSTATUS CCC "vendor reserved fields" are used by the slave controller to indicate to the master the
     error conditions that has occurred in the previous transfer. In case of any error, the slave controller NACKs
     the next private transfer coming from the master. The master can understand the status of the transfer
     which was not successfully accepted or transmitted by the slave controller by issuing the GETSTATUS CCC.
     The I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS register reflects all the information passed to the master when it issues the
     GETSTATUS CCC. Refer to the description of this register for more details on the error fields and other status
     fields present in the GETSTATUS CCC format supported by the I3C slave.

 15.6.4.21.2.6 Handling of ENTDAA, GETPID and GETDCR
     CCCs can source the 48-bit PID and 8-bit DCR values from the following I3C registers:

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                                      Alif Semiconductor
                                                                     948
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                                        www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


       n I3C_SLV_MIPI_ID_VALUE (16 MSBs of PID), I3C_SLV_PID_VALUE (32 LSBs of PID)
       n I3C_SLV_CHAR_CTRL[DCR]

     The reset values of these register fields are set from corresponding I3C strap inputs. Application can override
     these values by programming the registers before enabling the controller. That is, the implementation allows
     for PID and DCR values to be set by register programming.

 15.6.4.22 I3C Slave Private Data Transfers
     The I3C slave supports private read and write transfers through I3C interface over the SCL and SDA lines.
     For private receive and transmit transfers in SDR mode of operation, if the I3C slave can accept or transmit
     the transaction from the master, it accepts the address by providing an ACK response, else the address is
     NACK-ed.
     In HDR mode, if the I3C slave is not able to accept the private write transaction from the master, the data is
     dropped because there is no mechanism to NACK a private write transfer. For private read transfer, a NACK
     response is issued.
     Receiving a NACK means that an error exists in the current or previous transfer read/write, and the master
     can choose to do on of the following:
       n Issue a START/RESTART and re-attempt the data transfer. If the previous transfer is NACK-ed because of
         unavailability of internal buffer space, the second transfer might be successful.
       n Issue a GETSTATUS CCC to check if the NACK is due to a more permanent condition encountered by the
         previous transfer due to some protocol error like parity/CRC or due to overflow/underflow errors and
         then re-issue the NACK transfer.

 15.6.4.22.1 Handling Private Receive (Master Write) Transfers
     In SDR mode of operation, the I3C slave accepts the write address (ACK response) when all of the following
     conditions are met:
       n Receive buffer has the space (in terms of empty locations) equal or more than the programmed value in
         the I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_CTRL[RX_START_THLD] register field.
       n Response queue is not full and it has some space to hold the response for the current transfer.

     Otherwise, the I3C slave responds with a NACK for the private write address.
     Once the write address is ACK-ed (accepted), the I3C expects the RX FIFO space to be available until the end
     of transfer to avoid overflow condition.
     In the DMA mode of operation, the DMA request of the handshake interface is initiated when the Rx FIFO
     level reaches the programmed I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_CTRL[RX_START_THLD] level.
     When an overflow condition is encountered (when the system latency is high to consume the receiving data),
     the controller sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[OVERFLOW_ERR] bit and drops further incoming data until
     the termination (either STOP or RESTART) is detected.
     When a parity/CRC error is encountered during the master write transfer, the controller sets the I3C_CCC_
     DEVICE_STATUS[PROTOCOL_ERR] bit and drops further incoming data until the termination is detected.
     The controller, once it sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[OVERFLOW_ERR] bit or I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS
     [PROTOCOL_ERR] bit, rejects (NACK) any further private transfer request from the master until the master
     reads the device status through a GETSTATUS CCC and the slave application resumes the slave operation by
     setting the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[RESUME] bit.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       949
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                       E7 Series


     If the Rx FIFO does not have threshold amount of space to accommodate the write transfer, the controller
     NACKs the request and the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[BUFFER_NOT_AVAIL] bit is set. The controller, once it
     sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[BUFFER_NOT_AVAIL] bit, rejects (NACK) any further private write transfer
     request from master until space is available in the receive FIFO.

 15.6.4.22.2 Handling Private Receive (Master Read) Transfers
     The data transmission for a private master read is initiated by issuing a Tx transfer command. The Tx transfer
     command can be issued by writing the Tx command data structure into the I3C_COMMAND_QUEUE_PORT
     register.
     The I3C slave responds for a private read address with ACK when all of the following conditions are met:
       n Tx command is valid in the command queue
       n Tx FIFO has data equal to either the data length size of the command or the I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_
         CTRL[TX_START_THLD] size is met.
       n Response queue non-full

     Otherwise, the I3C slave responds with NACK for the private read address.
     To determine for which of the condition the NACK occurred, the I3C provides further information as follows:
       n An additional interrupt bit I3C_INTR_STATUS[READ_REQ_RECV_STS] is asserted when there is no valid
         command in the command queue.
       n The I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[DATA_NOT_READY] bit is set when the data in the Tx FIFO is not equal to
         data length size of the command or the I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_CTRL[TX_START_THLD] field.
       n The I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[DATA_NOT_READY] bit is also set if response queue is full.

     During HDR transfers (ENTHDR CCC detected), the slave responds with "slave NACK" preamble to indicate its
     inability to transmit the data for the private read command when one of the conditions are not met.
     Once the read address is ACK-ed (accepted), the I3C expects the application to provide enough data in the Tx
     FIFO as specified in the Tx command to avoid underrun condition.
     In the DMA mode of operation, the DMA request of the handshake interface is initiated when the Tx FIFO
     empty location level reaches the programmed I3C_DATA_BUFFER_THLD_CTRL[TX_EMPTY_BUF_THLD] level.
     When an underrun condition is encountered (when the system latency is high to provide the transmit data),
     the controller sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[UNDERFLOW_ERR] bit and terminates the transfer on the
     I3C bus.
     The controller, once it sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[UNDERFLOW_ERR] bit, rejects (NACK) any further
     private transfer request from master until the master reads the device status through a GETSTATUS CCC and
     the slave application resumes the slave operation by setting the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL [RESUME] bit.
     If the Tx FIFO does not have threshold amount of data to respond for the master read request, the controller
     NACKs the request and the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[DATA_NOT_READY] bit is set. The controller, once it
     sets the I3C_CCC_DEVICE_STATUS[DATA_NOT_READY] bit, rejects (NACK) any further private read transfer
     request from master until data is available in the Tx FIFO.

 15.6.4.23 I3C Slave HJ Request Generation
     The I3C slave controller always attempts to issue the first HJ request to the current master when the
     following conditions are met:
      1. Configured as a HJ capable device
      2. I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[HJ_EN] set to 1.
      3. Dynamic address is invalid (not assigned yet)

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                        Alif Semiconductor
                                                         950
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                           www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


      4. HJ event generation is not disabled by the master (through DISEC CCC transfer)
      5. Bus IDLE condition is met (1 ms) as programmed in the I3C_BUS_IDLE_TIMING register.
     If a NACK response is received or when an arbitration loss is encountered after the first attempt, the slave
     controller attempts to resend the HJ request in the next START condition seen on the bus or on meeting bus
     IDLE condition (whichever happens first), provided conditions 3 and 4 are still valid.
     In the adaptive mode, the I3C slave does not generate the HJ request until the I3C broadcast address (0x7E)
     is seen on the I3C bus, if I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ADAPTIVE_I2C_I3C] = 1. If I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ADAPTIVE_I2C_I3C] =
     0, the I3C slave generates the HJ when the previously specified conditions to generate HJ are met. It is better
     to set I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ADAPTIVE_I2C_I3C] to 1, if the slave application does not have a prior knowledge of
     the bus (I2C/I3C) to which the controller is connected. If I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ADAPTIVE_I2C_I3C] = 1, the I3C
     slave does not send the HJ until it confirms the bus mode as I3C indicated by receipt of 0x7E header on the
     line.
     Application can program the I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[HJ_EN] bit to 0 to disable the HJ capability of the I3C.
     When this bit is set to 0, I3C does not generate HJ request and behaves as if its a non-HJ device. When this bit
     is set to 1, I3C generates HJ request when all the conditions mentioned are met. Note that programming of
     the I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[HJ_EN] bit is a one time task, which is done only when the controller is disabled.


                                                                NOTE

       When HJ is enabled (I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[HJ_EN] = 1), the I3C controller does not participate in
       ENTDAA until HJ request is sent on the bus.


 15.6.4.24 I3C Slave SIR Generation
     The I3C application can decide to send a SIR by asserting the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[SIR] bit, along with the type
     of IBI to be generated, which can be selected by I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[SIR_CTRL] field. If I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ
     [SIR_CTRL] = 0, the IBI is generated after the programmed I3C_BUS_FREE_AVAIL_TIMING[BUS_FREE_TIME]
     time value has expired, or on the next available START condition on the I3C bus.
     The status of the IBI generation is updated in the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[IBI_STS] field, which is informed to the
     application by the I3C_INTR_STATUS[IBI_UPDATED_STS] bit. On successful completion of I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ
     [IBI_STS] field update, the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[SIR] bit is auto cleared. On receiving this interrupt, the slave
     application can read the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[IBI_STS] field.
                                  Table 15-107 I3C Slave SIR Values of IBI_STS Field(1)
    IBI_STS field         Value                                            Description
  Reserved                  0x0      Default value
  Success                   0x1      SIR accepted by the master (ACK response received)
  Reserved                  0x2      Reserved
  Not Attempted             0x3      SIR not attempted
     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     The I3C controller does not attempt to issue the IBI and generates the 'Not Attempted' (0x3) status under the
     following conditions:
       n Master has not assigned the Dynamic Address
       n Master has cleared the assigned Dynamic Address through RSTDAA


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                                951
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                           E7 Series


       n Master has disabled the I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[SIR_EN] through DISEC CCC
       n I3C controller has switched the role to master


 15.6.4.25 I3C Slave MR Generation
     The I3C application can decide to send a MR by asserting the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[MR] bit.
     The status of the IBI generation is updated in the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[IBI_STS] field, which is informed to the
     application by the I3C_INTR_STATUS[IBI_UPDATED_STS] interrupt. After I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[IBI_STS] field is
     updated, the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[MR] bit is auto cleared. On receiving this interrupt, the slave application can
     read the I3C_SLV_INTR_REQ[IBI_STS] field.
                                  Table 15-108 I3C Slave MR Values of IBI_STS Field(1)
    IBI_STS field         Value                                            Description
  Reserved                  0x0      Default value
  Success                   0x1      MR accepted by the master (ACK response received)
  Reserved                  0x2      Reserved
  Not Attempted             0x3      MR not attempted
     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     The I3C controller does not attempt to issue the IBI and generates the 'Not Attempted' (0x3) status under the
     following conditions:
       n Master has not assigned the Dynamic Address
       n Master has cleared the assigned Dynamic Address through RSTDAA
       n Master has disabled the I3C_SLV_EVENT_STATUS[MR_EN] through DISEC CCC
       n I3C controller has switched the role to master


 15.6.4.26 I3C Slave Disabling
     The application can disable the I3C when operating as a slave at any time by clearing the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL
     [ENABLE] bit. The application should then poll the I3C_DEVICE_CTRL[ENABLE] bit until it turns to 0 to confirm
     that the controller is in disabled state. If the slave controller is busy in executing any I3C bus transfers (like
     receiving/transmitting an I3C transfer or transmitting an IBI), then the controller enters the disabled state
     only after it completes the present on-going transfers. Once the slave controller enters the disabled state, it
     responds with NACK for any address match including 0x7E.


                                                                NOTE

       The I3C slave controller should not be disabled when status for SIR/MR request is pending.

                                                    - If this bit is programmed to 0, the controller initiates a hot-join
                                                    without determining the bus mode assuming itself to be on I3C
                                                    bus.
                                                    This bit should be set only if the slave application does not know
                                                    to which bus the device is connected to.
     26    RESERVED             R         0x0       Reserved.

                                                    This bit is used in slave mode of operation.
                                                    After POR, the slave controller is enabled only after it sees both
                                                    the SDA and SCL lines IDLE for a specified time. This IDLE time is
           IDLE_CNT_                                calculated by multiplying IDLE_CNT_MULTPLIER with the I3C_BUS_
   25-24                       R/W        0x0       FREE_AVAIL_TIMING[BUS_AVAILABLE_TIME] field.
           MULTPLIER
                                                    0x0: BUS_AVAILABLE_TIME × 1
                                                    0x1: BUS_AVAILABLE_TIME × 2
                                                    0x2: BUS_AVAILABLE_TIME × 4
                                                    0x3: BUS_AVAILABLE_TIME × 8
    23-9   RESERVED             R         0x0       Reserved.

                                                    This bit acts as a global control to ACK/NACK the hot-join request

     8     HOT_JOIN_CTRL       R/W        0x0

 15.6.5.3.5 I3C_RESPONSE_QUEUE_PORT Register
           Offset           Access             Description
                                               I3C Response Queue Port Register.
                                               In master mode of operation, the response status for each command is written into
                                               the response queue by the I3C if the ROC bit is set or if transfer error occurs. The
                                               response queue can be read through this register. It is expected that this register is
                                               read whenever I3C_INTR_STATUS[RESP_READY_STAT_INTR] bit is set. Not doing so
                                               might result in execution of new commands getting stalled. A new command is
                                               executed only if there is space available in response queue to push corresponding
         0x10
                              R                response.
     Base address
                                               In slave mode of operation, the response status for each command is written into
                                               the response queue. The response queue can be read through this register. It is
                                               expected that this register is read whenever I3C_INTR_STATUS[RESP_READY_STAT_
                                               INTR] bit is set. Not doing so might result in execution of new commands getting
                                               stalled. A new command is executed only if there is space available in response
                                               queue to push corresponding response.
                                               Reset value of this register is not defined as it is internally mapped to a queue.


    Bits      Field Name             Access      Reset Value Description
    31-0      RESPONSE                 R              0x0       32-bit response

     3     MR                R/W        0x0       bit automatically and updates the IBI_STS field. If NACK response is

 15.7 Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) Interface

 15.7.1 PDM Overview
     The Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) module provides an interface to Digital Microphones (DMIC). The DMIC
     signal first gets amplified, and then sampled at a high rate and quantized by a DMIC's internal PDM
     modulator. The device PDM module provides clock and decodes the received 1-bit PDM stream into 16-bit
     values in Pulse Code Modulation (PCM) format.
     The device includes:
       n One PDM module in Shared Peripherals
       n One Low-Power PDM module (LPPDM) in the RTSS-HE

     Each PDM module supports the following main features:
       n 4× 2-channel PDM microphone inputs for total support of up to 8 PDM channels (mono DMICs) for
         PDM module
       n Audio signal bandwidth of up to 96 kHz
       n DMA controller interface for storing audio samples
       n 16-bit PCM output per channel
       n Selection between 9 modes of PDM clock frequencies from 512 kHz to 4.8 MHz (oversampling). The
         mode applies to all channels.
       n Microphone sleep mode when at 128 kHz PDM clock
       n Independent phase adjustment per channel to allow beam forming
       n Independent gain adjustment per channel
       n Independent peak detector per channel with programmable thresholds
       n Peak detection interrupt per channel producing wake-up event
       n Independent programmable DC blocking Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) filter per channel
       n Independent programmable Finite Impulse Response (FIR) filter per channel
       n FIFO with a capability to store up to 8 PCM samples for each channel for CPU to read
       n Programmable FIFO watermark level to generate data available interrupt
       n FIFO overrun error interrupt



                                                      NOTE

       All Low Power peripherals are single-master accessible, including LPPDM. Ensure that application
       software manages access to these LP peripherals such that no more than one bus master (CPU or
       DMA) attempts access at a time, using semaphores or similar techniques.


     Figure 15-90 provides a high-level overview of the PDM implementation in the device.

                                                            NOTE

 15.7.4.1 PDM Introduction
     Figure 15-94 and Figure 15-95 present a simplified diagram of the PDM main internal blocks and connections.
     The PDM module interfaces PDM-type digital microphones to an APB bus. The PDM microphones produce 1-
     bit digital data streams in PDM format. Each PDM channel connects to one microphone. The PDM module
     converts each 1-bit PDM audio input into a 16-bit PCM format. The Host reads the 16-bits PCM data for each
     microphone through a set of APB registers.

 15.7.4.3 PDM Interfaces

 15.7.4.3.1 Microphone Interface
     Figure 15-97 presents the PDM microphone interface block diagram.
     The input data to each channel is in PDM format. PDM module supplies PDM clock to a pair of microphones.
     The data output pins of microphones pair connect into one input line.
     The even-indexed microphone in the pair should be setup to launch its data so it could be captured by rising
     edges of PDM clock. The odd-indexed microphone in the pair should be setup to launch its data so it could be
     captured by falling edges of PDM clock. Otherwise the microphone outputs go to high-Z (high impedance) to
     avoid signal conflict.

     Firmware can program the sampling time of PDM_Di input relative to PDM_Ci output to compensate for

     microphones. Firmware can adjust sampling time in time units equal to the PDM_CLK period.

 15.7.4.3.2 Host Interfaces
     The Host communicates to the PDM module via an APB bus, interrupt lines, and DMA controller handshaking
     ports.

 15.7.4.3.2.1 APB Interface
     The APB bus provides access to configuration registers and allows reading PCM data from audio channels. All
     audio channels run at the same sample rate and therefore produce PDM samples at the same time. The Host
     reads PCM data as a set consisting of one PDM sample per enabled audio channel. The PCM data of audio
     channels are located in registers with consecutive addresses to allow burst reading.

 15.7.4.3.2.2 Warning Interrupt
     The Warning interrupt alerts the Host on PDM data availability. Firmware can adjust FIFO watermark level so
     Warning interrupt would trigger when there is a set number of PCM samples per audio channel in internal
     FIFO.




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                                  Alif Semiconductor
                                                                    1002
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                                    www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


 15.7.4.3.2.3 Error Interrupt
     The Error interrupt triggers if firmware fails to read PCM samples on time and the internal FIFO overruns. The
     PCM samples that were in FIFO prior to overrun remain intact, but new PDM samples that arrive after FIFO is
     full are lost.

 15.7.4.3.2.4 Audio Detection Interrupt
     The Audio detection interrupt triggers when the absolute value of audio signal exceeds a preset threshold on
     at least one audio channel. Firmware can set threshold for each channel and enable the channel to
     contribute to triggering of the interrupt. Once interrupt is produced, the Host can read interrupt status
     register to know which channel or channels produced the interrupt.

 15.7.4.3.2.5 DMA Controller Handshaking
     The DMA handshaking interface can be used to trigger DMA controller to read PCM data upon data sample
     availability. This eliminates the need to monitor the warning interrupt for this purpose.

 15.7.4.4 PDM Modes of Operation
     The PDM module can be programmed to operate in different modes. The mode applies to all channels.
     Therefore, all channels operate in the same mode at a given time.
     To preserve power, firmware can initially enable only one channel and set it to run at a slow clock and
     sampling rate. Upon detection of an audio signal, firmware can switch mode to the desired clock frequency
     and sampling rate and enable additional channels.
                                          Table 15-118 PDM Modes
                        PDM Clock                    Baseband       Audio Signal
                                     Decimation
     PDM Mode          Frequency                   Sampling Rate    Bandwidth      Application
                                        Ratio
                      (PDM_Ci) kHz                   (Fs) kHz(1)     (Fs/2) kHz
           9                4800        25              192             96
                                                                                   Ultrasound
           8                4800        50               96             48
           7                3072        64               48             24
                                                                                   Full-bandwidth audio
           6                2400        50               48             24
           5                1536        48               32             16         Wide-bandwidth audio
           4                1024        64               16              8
           3                 768        48               16              8         High-quality voice
           2                 512        32               16              8
           1                 512        64                8              4         Standard voice
           0                 128        N/A             N/A             N/A        Microphone sleep
     1. Sampling Frequency (Fs).

 15.7.4.5 PDM Audio Reception Procedure
     Recommended procedure to receive audio is as follows:
       n Program sampling timing of microphone inputs with respect to PDM_Ci output to meet microphone
         timing requirements.
       n Program channel-specific parameters.
       n Decide on what method the Host will use to read microphone PCM data. Two methods are possible:
         l The PDM module produces an interrupt to the Host informing it that at least one PDM sample of each

            channel (microphone) is available to be read via APB register. If this method is used, program FIFO

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                      1003
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                      E7 Series


             almost to the full watermark threshold and enable FIFO Warning and Error interrupts.
           l The DMA handshaking interface can inform DMA controller that at least one PDM sample of each

             channel (microphone) is available to be read by DMA. This method does not rely on interrupts to read
             PDM data. If this method is to be used, enable DMA handshaking interface.
       n     Set peak detection threshold and enable Audio peak detection interrupt on one channel.
       n Program PDM mode to a mode with slow PDM clock rate for power saving and enable one channel
         (microphone) to snoop on audio. Wait for Audio peak detection interrupt.
       n Once the Host receives a Audio peak detection interrupt, switch mode to a higher sampling rate and
         enable the rest of the desired channels (microphones).
       n Read audio PCM samples using either an interrupt routine, or direct DMA handshaking.


 15.7.5 PDM Registers Guide
                                                             NOTE

       All information related to PDM in this section also applies to LPPDM, unless stated otherwise.


 15.7.5.1 PDM Modules
                                             Table 15-119 PDM Modules
                Module                                                    Memory Base Address

     Offset      Access Description
                          PDM Audio Control Register 0.
                          CAUTION: Firmware should avoid writing back-to-back values to this register to allow for its content
      0x0
                  R/W     to synchronize to audio clock domain. Inserting four APB transactions between consecutive writes
  Base address
                          to this register would be sufficient for this purpose when APB and audio clock frequencies are 400
                          MHz and 76.8 MHz, respectively.

 15.7.5.3.9 PDM_CH0_CH1_AUDIO_OUT Register
     Offset      Access Description
                        Channels 0 and 1 Audio Output Register.
                        CAUTION:
                        - Although this register is R/W, firmware should not write to it.
      0x20
                  R/W   - Firmware should read this register only when there is data available in it. This means it should
  Base address
                        read it only after it receives a warning interrupt and after it reads the PDM_FIFO_STAT register to
                        see how many audio samples are available in FIFO to be read. If firmware reads this register before
                        any data is available in it, it would read invalid data or X which can cause CPU to hang in simulation.


    Bits   Field Name            Access    Reset Value Description
   31-16 CH1_AUDIO                 R/W         0x0        Channel 1 audio output
    15-0   CH0_AUDIO               R/W         0x0        Channel 0 audio output

 15.8 Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI)

 15.8.1 SPI Overview
     The Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) module is a programmable low pin count, full-duplex master or slave
     synchronous serial interface.
     The device includes:
       n   Up to four high-speed SPI modules in Shared Peripherals
       n   One Low-Power SPI module (LPSPI) in the RTSS-HE
     The SPI modules support the following main features:
       n 32-bit data bus width for AHB interface (SPI modules) and APB interface (LPSPI module)
       n Standard SPI mode
       n Up to four slave select lines for the SPI modules, one slave select line for the LPSPI
       n Multi-master contention detection
       n Programmable delay on the sample time of received serial data bit for the high-speed SPI modules only
         (when programmed in Master mode)
       n Separate Transmit and Receive FIFO buffers:
         l Buffer width of 32 bits

         l Buffer depth of 16 words

       n DMA requests
       n Combined interrupt lines and active high-level interrupts
       n Operation modes:
         l Serial Master or Slave modes for the high-speed SPI modules

         l Master mode only for LPSPI

       n Programmable frame formats:
         l Motorola Serial Peripheral Interface

         l Texas Instruments Synchronous Serial Protocol (SSP)

         l National Semiconductor Microwire

       n Programmable data transfer clock bit rate for dynamic control of the serial bit rate
       n Programmable data item size (4 to 32 bits) for each data transfer



                                                       NOTE

       All Low Power peripherals are single-master accessible, including LPSPI. Ensure that application
       software manages access to these LP peripherals such that no more than one bus master (CPU or
       DMA) attempts access at a time, using semaphores or similar techniques.

 15.8.4 SPI Functional Description
                                                                NOTE

       All information related to SPI in this section also applies to LPSPI, unless stated otherwise.


 15.8.4.1 SPI Introduction
     Figure 15-103 presents a simplified diagram of the SPI main internal blocks and connections.
                                                  Figure 15-103 SPI Block Diagram(1)
    Device
                                                                       SPI
     DMA Handshaking               DMA
                                 Interface
                                                        Receive                 Receive
                                                         FIFO                    FIFO
    Interrupt Requests                                  Control                 Memory              Shi�
                                 Interrupt                                                                          SPI I/O
                                   Logic                                                           Control         Interface

                     BUS              SPI Slave                        FSM                 Register Block

                                                                                                                               SPI-004




     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     The SPI has the following basic blocks:
       n SPI Slave Interface—AHB for SPI[0-3] and APB for LPSPI
         The host processor accesses data, control, and status information of the SPI through the SPI Slave
         Interface. The SPI Slave Interface has a 32-bit data bus and supports little-endian scheme for data
         transfer.
       n FSM Control
         This block includes a Finite State Machine (FSM) controller.
       n Register Block
         This block includes a set of all used SPI registers. For more information, refer to Section 15.8.5 SPI
         Registers Guide and Section 15.8.6 LPSPI Registers Guide.
       n DMA Interface
         The SPI has a DMA Handshaking interface. This interface controls the transfer of DMA requests between
         the SPI and the device DMA controller. For more information, refer to Section 15.8.4.4 SPI DMA
         Requests.
       n Interrupt Logic
         The SPI is able to generate interrupt requests to the device Interrupt controller. For more information,
         refer to Section 15.8.4.3 SPI Interrupt Requests.
       n Clock Pre-Scale




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                    Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1027
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                      www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                            E7 Series


         The SPI has included Clock Pre-Scale block. This block is used for SPI_CLK pre-scaling. For more
         information, refer to Section 15.8.4.2.1 SPI Clock Ratios.
       n Receive FIFO Control and Receive FIFO Memory
         The Receive FIFO Memory block is used for buffer during receive operations. The receive operations are
         controlled by the Receive FIFO Control block. For more information, refer to Section 15.8.4.10
         SPI Receive and Transmit FIFO Buffers.
       n Transmit FIFO Control and Transmit FIFO Memory
         The Transmit FIFO Memory block is used for buffer during transmit operations. The transmit operations
         are controlled by the Transmit FIFO Control block. For more information, refer to Section 15.8.4.10
         SPI Receive and Transmit FIFO Buffers.
       n Shift Control Logic
         l Shifts out data from the SPI Transmit FIFO Memory to an external serial device.

         l Shifts in data from an external serial device to the SPI Receive FIFO Memory.

       n SPI I/O Interface
         The SPI I/O Interface includes all used interface pins. For more information, refer to Section 15.8.3
         SPI External Connectivity.

 15.8.4.2 SPI Clocks
     For more information, refer to Table 15-122.

 15.8.4.2.1 SPI Clock Ratios
     This section describes details of the clock ratio between the serial bit-rate clock (SPI_SCLK) and the internal
     SPI core clock (SPI_CLK) for both master and slave modes.
     In SPI Master mode of operation, the maximum SPI_SCLK period is a multiple of the SPI_CLK. In SPI Slave
     mode of operation, a synchronized external peripheral clock is used by the SPI to receive or transmit the
     data.
     For SPI Master mode of operation, the maximum frequency of the SPI_SCLK is one-half the frequency of the
     SPI_CLK. This allows the shift control logic to capture data on one clock edge of the SPI_SCLK and propagate
     data on the opposite edge.
     The frequency of the SPI_SCLK can be derived from equation (15-15):
                                                                                                                 (15-15)

     where BAUDR is any even value between 2 and 65534. BAUDR = SCKDV × 2, and SCKDV can be set in the SPI_
     BAUDR[SCKDV]/LPSPI_BAUDR[SCKDV] bit field. If this bit field is set to 0, the SPI_SCLK is disabled.
     The SPI_SCLK line toggles only when an active transfer is in progress. At all other times, it is held inactive, as
     defined by the serial protocol under which it operates (refer to Section 15.8.4.7 SPI Connection Interfaces).
     For the high-speed SPI modules in Slave mode of operation:
       n   SPI Receive-only mode of operation (see Section 15.8.4.6.3 SPI Receive Only): the minimum frequency
           of the SPI_CLK is 6 times the maximum expected frequency of the SPI_SCLK from the master device. The
           SPI_SCLK (from the master) is double synchronized to bring it across to the SPI_CLK domain and then the
           edge is detected.
       n   For SPI Transmit and Receive modes of operation (see Section 15.8.4.6.1 SPI Transmit and Receive): the
           minimum frequency of the SPI_CLK is 12 times the maximum expected frequency of the SPI_SCLK from
           the master device. This minimum frequency is to ensure that data on the master receive line is stable


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                             Alif Semiconductor
                                                        1028
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                               www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


           before the master shift control logic captures the data. The 12:1 ratio ensures that the slave has driven
           data onto the master receive line 3 × SPI_CLK cycles before the data is captured.
     In summary, the frequency ratio restrictions between the serial bit-rate clock (SPI_SCLK) and the internal
     SPI core clock (SPI_CLK) are as follows:
     Master mode:
       n   FSPI_CLK ≥ 2 × (maximum FSPI_SCLK)
     Slave mode (high-speed SPI modules):
       n Receive Only mode: FSPI_CLK ≥ 6 × (maximum FSPI_SCLK from the master)
       n Transmit and Receive mode: FSPI_CLK ≥ 12 × (maximum FSPI_SCLK from the master)


 15.8.4.3 SPI Interrupt Requests
     The SPI supports a single interrupt request line (SPI_IRQ) that is the combined (OR-ed) result of various
     internal SPI interrupts after masking. The SPI_IMR/LPSPI_IMR register controls the interrupt masking. The
     combined interrupt request is routed to the corresponding device interrupt controller either directly (LPSPI)
     or through the Shared Interrupt Router (SPI[0-3]). For more information, refer to Section 15.8.2 SPI Internal
     Connections.
     The SPI_IRQ line is active-high, level-sensitive, and can be triggered by any of the following interrupts:
       n Transmit FIFO Empty Interrupt (SPI_TXE_IRQ)—Set when the transmit FIFO is equal to or below its
         threshold value and requires actions to prevent an under-run. The threshold value, set through the SPI_
         TXFTLR[TFT]/LPSPI_TXFTLR[TFT] bit field, determines the level of transmit FIFO entries at which an
         interrupt is generated. This interrupt is cleared by the hardware when data are written into the transmit
         FIFO, bringing it over the threshold level. To control the SPI_TXE_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR
         [TXEIM]/LPSPI_IMR[TXEIM] bit. The SPI_TXE_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR
         [TXEIS]/LPSPI_ISR[TXEIS] and SPI_RISR[TXEIR]/LPSPI_RISR[TXEIR] bits.
       n Transmit FIFO Overflow Interrupt (SPI_TXO_IRQ)—Set when an SPI slave interface attempts to write into
         the transmit FIFO after it has been completely filled. When set, data written from the SPI slave interface
         is discarded. This interrupt remains set until software reads the Transmit FIFO Overflow Interrupt Clear
         register (SPI_TXEICR/LPSPI_TXOICR). To control the SPI_TXO_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR
         [TXOIM]/LPSPI_IMR[TXOIM] bit. The SPI_TXO_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR
         [TXOIS]/LPSPI_ISR[TXOIS] and SPI_RISR[TXOIR]/LPSPI_RISR[TXOIR] bits.
       n Receive FIFO Full Interrupt (SPI_RXF_IRQ)—Set when the receive FIFO is equal to or above its threshold
         value plus 1 and requires actions to prevent an overflow. The threshold value, set through the SPI_
         RXFTLR/LPSPI_RXFTLR register, determines the level of receive FIFO entries at which an interrupt is
         generated. This interrupt is cleared by the hardware when data are read from the receive FIFO, bringing
         it below the threshold level. To control the SPI_RXF_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR[RXFIM]/LPSPI_IMR
         [RXFIM] bit. The SPI_RXF_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR[RXFIS]/LPSPI_ISR[RXFIS] and
         SPI_RISR[RXFIR]/LPSPI_RISR[RXFIR] bits.
       n Receive FIFO Overflow Interrupt (SPI_RXO_IRQ)—Set when the receive logic attempts to place data into
         the receive FIFO after it has been completely filled. When set, newly received data are discarded. This
         interrupt remains set until software reads the Receive FIFO Overflow Interrupt Clear register (SPI_
         RXOICR/LPSPI_RXOICR). To control the SPI_RXO_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR[RXOIM]/LPSPI_IMR
         [RXOIM] bit. The SPI_RXO_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR[RXOIS]/LPSPI_ISR[RXOIS]
         and SPI_RISR[RXOIR]/LPSPI_RISR[RXOIR] bits.
       n Receive FIFO Underflow Interrupt (SPI_RXU_IRQ)—Set when an SPI slave interface attempts to read
         from the receive FIFO when it is empty. When set, zeros are read back from the receive FIFO. This

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        1029
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                              www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


         interrupt remains set until software reads the Receive FIFO Underflow Interrupt Clear register (SPI_
         RXUICR/LPSPI_RXUICR). To control the SPI_RXU_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR[RXUIM]/LPSPI_IMR
         [RXUIM] bit. The SPI_RXU_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR[RXUIS]/LPSPI_ISR[RXUIS]
         and SPI_RISR[RXUIR]/LPSPI_RISR[RXUIR] bits.
       n Multi-Master Contention Interrupt (SPI_MST_IRQ)—Present only when the SPI operates as a serial-
         master device. The SPI_MST_IRQ interrupt is set when another serial master on the serial bus selects the
         SPI master as a serial-slave device and is actively transferring data (refer to Section 15.8.4 SPI Functional
         Description). This informs the processor of possible contention on the serial bus. The SPI_MST_IRQ
         interrupt remains set until software reads the Multi-Master Interrupt Clear register (SPI_MSTICR/LPSPI_
         MSTICR). To control the SPI_MST_IRQ interrupt, set the SPI_IMR[MSTIM]/LPSPI_IMR[MSTIM] bit. The
         SPI_MST_IRQ interrupt status can be read from the SPI_ISR[MSTIS]/LPSPI_ISR[MSTIS] and SPI_RISR
         [MSTIR]/LPSPI_RISR[MSTIR] bits.

 15.8.4.4 SPI DMA Requests

 15.8.4.4.1 SPI DMA Handshaking Interface
     The SPI supports a DMA handshaking interface to the device DMA controller (DMAC) to request and control
     data transfers on the SPI slave interface.
     The DMAC acts as a a flow controller. It should be programmed by the software with the number of data
     items (block size) that are to be transmitted or received by the SPI for each DMA request. This is also known
     as the burst transaction length that should be programmed into the DMAC registers for source and
     destination, respectively.
     The SPI uses two DMA channels, one for the transmit data and one for the receive data. Each SPI DMA
     channel, if enabled, can issue DMA requests.
     To enable the DMA operation on the SPI side, the DMA control register (SPI_DMACR/LPSPI_DMACR) should
     be programmed.
       n Writing a 1 into the SPI_DMACR[TDMAE]/LPSPI_DMACR[TDMAE] bit enables the SPI transmit
         handshaking interface.
       n Writing a 1 into the SPI_DMACR[RDMAE]/LPSPI_DMACR[RDMAE] bit enables the SPI receive
         handshaking interface.
     The SPI request signals for source and destination, DMA_TX_REQ and DMA_RX_REQ, are activated when
     their corresponding FIFOs reach the corresponding watermark levels.
     The DMA controller uses rising-edge detection of the DMA_TX_REQ and DMA_RX_REQ signals to identify a
     request on the channel. Upon reception of the DMA_TX_ACK/DMA_RX_ACK signal from the DMA controller
     to indicate the burst transaction is complete, the SPI de-asserts the DMA_TX_REQ/DMA_RX_REQ burst
     request signal, until the DMA_TX_ACK/DMA_RX_ACK signal is de-asserted by the DMA controller.
     When the SPI samples that DMA_TX_ACK/DMA_RX_ACK signal is de-asserted, it can re-assert the DMA_TX_
     REQ/DMA_RX_REQ signal of the request line if their corresponding FIFOs exceed their watermark levels
     (back-to-back burst transaction). If this is not the case, the DMA request lines remain de-asserted.

 15.8.4.4.2 Transmit Watermark Level and Transmit FIFO Underflow
     During SPI serial transfers, Tx FIFO requests are made to the DMAC whenever the number of entries in the Tx
     FIFO is less than or equal to the value of the SPI_DMATDLR/LPSPI_DMATDLR register. This is known as
     transmit Watermark Level (WL). The DMAC responds by writing a burst of data to the Tx FIFO buffer.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       1030
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                             www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                               E7 Series


     Data should be fetched from the DMA often enough for the Tx FIFO to perform serial transfers continuously;
     that is, when the Tx FIFO begins to empty, another DMA request should be triggered. Otherwise, the Tx FIFO
     runs out of data (Tx FIFO underflow occurs).

 15.8.4.4.2.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level
     The goal in choosing a proper WL is to minimize the number of transactions per DMA block transfer, while at
     the same time keeping the probability of an underflow condition to an acceptable level. In practice, this is a
     function of the ratio of the rate at which the SPI transmits data to the rate at which the DMA controller can
     respond to destination burst requests.
     Figure 15-104 and Figure 15-105 illustrate two example cases for different WL settings. In both examples the
     following assumptions are made:
       n   The needed Number of Burst Transactions (NBT) equals the DMA Transfer Block Size divided by the
           Number of Data Items (NDI) per DMA Burst, as defined by equation 15-16:
                                                                                                                    (15-16)

           Where:
           The value of DMA Transfer Block Size is programmed at DMAC level. It defines the number of data
           transfers that the DMAC performs when it writes the destination data. See Section 12.2 DMA
           Controllers for more information.
       n   The value of NDI per DMA Burst is defined by equation 15-17, where:
           l Tx FIFO Depth is as specified in Section 15.8.1 SPI Overview.

           l Tx FIFO WL is programmed in the SPI_DMATDLR/LPSPI_DMATDLR register.

     Figure 15-104 (Case 1) shows an example where the selected WL is low. Therefore, the probability of an SPI
     underflow is high where the SPI serial transmit line needs to transmit data, but where there is no data left in
     the Tx FIFO. This occurs because the DMAC has not had time to service the DMA request before the Tx FIFO
     becomes empty.

     be promoted to the highest priority master at system interconnect level. This in turn allows to decrease the
     WL, which improves bus utilization without compromising the probability of an underflow occurring.

     As shown in Figure 15-105, programming the NDI per DMA Burst to a value greater than the WL that triggers
     the DMA request may cause overflow when there is not enough space in the Tx FIFO to service the

 15.8.4.4.3 Receive Watermark Level and Receive FIFO Overflow
     During SPI serial transfers, Rx FIFO requests are made to the DMA controller whenever the number of entries
     in the Rx FIFO is at or above the SPI_DMARDLR/LPSPI_DMARDLR register value plus 1. This is known as the
     receive WL. The DMA controller responds by fetching a burst of data from the Rx FIFO buffer.

     Data should be fetched by the DMA often enough for the Rx FIFO to accept serial transfers continuously; that
     is, when the Rx FIFO begins to fill, another DMA transfer is requested. Otherwise, the Rx FIFO fills with data
     (Rx FIFO overflow).

 15.8.4.5 SPI Modes
     The high-speed SPI modules can operate in Master or Slave mode, while the LPSPI–in Master mode only. The
     mode of operation can be changed by programming the SPI_CTRLR0[SPI_IS_MST] bit. All master and slave
     specific registers are available in the register map (refer to Section 15.8.5 SPI Registers Guide), and
     appropriate register is active depending on the mode of operation.
     For high-speed SPI only, SPI_CTRLR0 register provides additional settings. In this register, the slave select
     input mode can be selected (slave select input from I/O pad or slave select input from bit field value).

     All data transfers to and from the SPI slave are regulated on the SPI_SCLK line, driven by the serial master.
     Data are propagated from the SPI slave on one edge of the SPI_SCLK signal and sampled on the opposite
     edge.
     When the SPI slave is not selected, it must not interfere with data transfers between the serial master and
     other slave devices. When the SPI slave is not selected, its TXD output is buffered, resulting in a high
     impedance drive onto the serial master RXD line (DI). The buffers shown in Figure 15-108 are external to the
     SPI.
     The serial clock that regulates the data transfer is generated by the serial master and input to the SPI slave
     on the SPI_SCLK input. The SPI slave remains in an IDLE state until selected by the serial master. When not
     actively transmitting data, the SPI slave must hold its TXD line in a high impedance state to avoid interference
     with serial transfers to other slave devices. The SPI_OE_N line is used to control the TXD output buffer. The
     SPI slave continues to transfer data to and from the serial master as long as it is selected. If the serial master
     transmits to all slave devices, the SPI_CTRLR0[SLV_OE] control bit can be programmed to inform the SPI slave
     if it should respond with data from its TXD line.
     The SS_IN_N line is controlled by auxiliary logic. See Section 15.8.3 SPI External Connectivity for more
     details.

 15.8.4.6 SPI Transfer Modes
     This section describes the different modes in which the SPI operates when transferring data on the serial bus.
     The transfer mode is set by writing to the SPI_CTRLR0[TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field.
     Note that the transfer mode setting does not affect the duplex of the serial transfer. The SPI_CTRLR0
     [TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field is ignored for Microwire transfers, which are controlled by the SPI_
     MWCR/LPSPI_MWCR register (refer to Section 15.8.4.7.3 National Semiconductor Microwire).


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                      Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1035
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                        www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                            E7 Series


 15.8.4.6.1 SPI Transmit and Receive
     When the SPI_CTRLR0[TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field is set to 0x0, both transmit and receive logic
     are valid. The data transfer occurs as normal according to the selected frame format (serial protocol).
     Transmit data are popped from the transmit FIFO and sent through the transmit line to the target device,
     which replies with data on the receive line. The receive data from the target device is moved from the
     receive shift register into the receive FIFO at the end of each data frame.

 15.8.4.6.2 SPI Transmit Only
     When the SPI_CTRLR0[TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field is set to 0x1, the receive data are invalid and
     should not be stored in the receive FIFO. The data transfer occurs as normal, according to the selected frame
     format (serial protocol). Transmit data are popped from the transmit FIFO and sent through the transmit line
     to the target device, which replies with data on the receive line. At the end of the data frame, the receive
     shift register does not load its newly received data into the receive FIFO. The data in the receive shift register
     is overwritten by the next transfer.
     When this mode is entered, the interrupts originating from the receive logic should be masked.

 15.8.4.6.3 SPI Receive Only
     When the SPI_CTRLR0[TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field is set to 0x2, the transmit data are invalid.
     When the SPI acts as a slave, the transmit FIFO is never popped in Receive Only mode. The transmit output
     remains at a constant logic level during the transmission. The data transfer occurs as normal according to the
     selected frame format (serial protocol). The receive data from the target device is moved from the receive
     shift register into the receive FIFO at the end of each data frame.
     When this mode is entered, the interrupts originating from the transmit logic should be masked.

 15.8.4.6.4 SPI EEPROM Read
     When the SPI_CTRLR0[TMOD]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[TMOD] bit field is set to 0x3, the transmit data is used to
     transmit an opcode and/or an address to the EEPROM device. Typically this takes three data frames (8-bit
     opcode followed by 8-bit upper address and 8-bit lower address). During the transmission of the opcode and
     address, no data is captured by the receive logic (as long as the SPI master is transmitting data on its transmit
     line, data on the receive line is ignored). The SPI master continues to transmit data until the transmit FIFO is
     empty. Therefore, the transmit FIFO should only have enough data frames to supply the opcode and address
     to the EEPROM. If more data frames are in the transmit FIFO than are needed, then read data is lost.
     When the transmit FIFO becomes empty (all control information has been sent), data on the receive line is
     valid and is stored in the receive FIFO; the transmit output is held at a constant logic level. The serial transfer
     continues until the number of data frames received by the SPI master matches the value of the SPI_CTRLR1
     [NDF]/LPSPI_CTRLR1[NDF] bit field value + 1.




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                             Alif Semiconductor
                                                        1036
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                               www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                          E7 Series


                                                         NOTE

       This transfer mode is only valid for master configurations.


                                                         NOTE

       EEPROM read mode is not supported when the SPI is programmed to be in the Texas Instruments
       Synchronous Serial Protocol (SSP) mode.


 15.8.4.7 SPI Connection Interfaces
     The SPI can operate in serial master or serial slave mode and can connect to any serial peripheral device
     using one of the following interfaces:
       n Motorola Serial Peripheral Interface
       n Texas Instruments Synchronous Serial Protocol (SSP)
       n National Semiconductor Microwire


 15.8.4.7.1 Motorola Serial Peripheral Interface
     The Motorola SPI protocol can be selected by setting to 0x0 the SPI_CTRLR0[FRF]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[FRF] register
     field. To transmit data, both SPI peripherals must have identical serial clock phase (SCPH) and clock polarity
     (SCPOL) values. The data frame can be 4 to 32 bits.
     Writing to SPI_CTRLR0[SCPOL]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[SCPOL] bit selects the polarity of the inactive serial clock. This
     bit determines whether the inactive state of the serial clock is held low or high when the SPI master is not
     actively transferring data on the serial bus.
     The SPI_CTRLR0[SCPH]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[SCPH] bit selects the serial clock phase, which determines the
     relationship of the serial clock with the slave select signal.
     When SCPH = 0, data transmission begins on the falling edge of the slave select (SS) signal. The first data bit is
     captured by the master and slave peripherals on the first edge of the serial clock; therefore, valid data must
     be present on the Transmit Data (TXD) and Receive Data (RXD) lines prior to the first serial clock edge.
     Figure 15-109 shows the timing diagram for a single SPI data transfer with SCPH = 0. The serial clock is shown
     for configuration SCPOL = 0 and SCPOL = 1, where:
       n SPI_SCLK—serial output clock when SPI operates in Master mode or serial input clock when SPI operates
         in Slave mode
       n SPI_SCLKN—inverted version of the SPI_SCLK
       n SPI_SS—slave-select (chip-select) output signal when SPI operates in Master mode or slave-select (chip-
         select) input signal when SPI operates in Slave mode
       n SPI_OE_N—output enable for the SPI
       n TXD—transmit data line
       n RXD—receive data line

 15.8.4.7.2 Texas Instruments Synchronous Serial Protocol (SSP)
     The Texas Instruments SSP can be selected by setting to 0x1 the SPI_CTRLR0[FRF]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[FRF] register
     field. Data transfers begin by asserting the frame indicator line (SPI_SS) for one serial clock period. Data to be
     transmitted is driven onto the TXD line one serial clock cycle later; similarly data from the slave device is
     driven onto the RXD line. Data are propagated on the rising edge of the serial clock (SPI_SCLK) and captured
     on the falling edge. The length of the data frame ranges from 4 to 32 bits.
     Figure 15-118 shows the timing diagram for a single SSP serial transfer.
                                                 Figure 15-118 SSP Serial Format(1)

                    SPI_SCLK

                    TXD/RXD                          MSB                                LSB


                      SPI_SS

 15.8.4.7.3 National Semiconductor Microwire
     The National Semiconductor Microwire protocol can be selected by setting to 0x2 the SPI_CTRLR0
     [FRF]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[FRF] register field. When the SPI operates as a serial master, the data transmission
     begins with the falling edge of the slave-select signal (SPI_SS). One-half serial clock (SPI_SCLK) period later,
     the first bit of the control is sent out on the TXD line. The length of the control word can be in the range 1 to
     16 bits and is set by writing in the SPI_CTRLR0[CFS]/LPSPI_CTRLR0[CFS] bit field. The remainder of the control
     word is transmitted (propagated on the falling edge of the SPI_SCLK) by the SPI master. During this
     transmission, no data are present (high impedance) on the RXD line of the SPI master.
     The direction of the data word is controlled by the SPI_MWCR[MDD]/LPSPI_MWCR[MDD] bit. When the SPI_
     MWCR[MDD]/LPSPI_MWCR[MDD] bit is set to 0, the SPI master receives data from the external SPI slave.
     One clock cycle after the LSB of the control word is transmitted, the SPI slave responds with a dummy 0 bit,
     followed by the data frame, which can be 4 to 32 bits in length. Data are propagated on the falling edge of
     the serial clock and captured on the rising edge.
     The slave-select signal is held active-low during the transfer and is de-asserted one-half clock cycle later,
     after the data are transferred. Figure 15-120 shows the timing diagram for a single SPI master read from an
     external SPI slave.

                   RXD                                       0     MSB                          LSB

     After the first data word has been transmitted to the SPI slave, the SPI master polls the RXD input waiting for
     a READY status from the SPI slave. Upon reception of the READY status, the SPI master begins transmission of
     the next control word. It is assumed that the slave will keep the READY status until it receives any
     confirmation from the master, which is provided when the clock is resumed by the master. After
     transmission of the last data frame has completed, the SPI master transmits a start bit to clear the READY
     status of the slave device before completing the transfer. The FIFO status for this transfer is the same as
     shown on Figure 15-129, except that the SPI_MWCR[MHS]/LPSPI_MWCR[MHS] bit is set to 1.

     When the SPI is programmed as a serial slave (high-speed SPI only), data transmission begins with the falling
     edge of the slave select signal (SPI_SS). One-half serial clock (SPI_SCLK) period later, the first bit of the control
     is present on the RXD line. The length of the control word can be in the range of 1 to 16 bits and is set by

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                    Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1049
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                      www.alifsemi.com

     from the serial master. The remainder of the control word is received (captured on the rising edge of the
     serial clock) by the SPI serial slave. During this reception, no data are driven (high impedance) on the serial
     slave TXD line.
     The direction of the data word is controlled by the SPI_MWCR[MDD] bit. When this bit is set to 0, this
     indicates the SPI serial slave is to receive data from the external serial master. Immediately after the control
     word is transmitted, the serial master begins to drives the data frame onto the SPI slave RXD line. Data are
     propagated on the falling edge of the serial clock and captured on the rising edge. The slave select signal is
     held active-low during the transfer and is de-asserted one-half clock cycle later after the data are transferred.
     The SPI slave output enable signal (SPI_OE_N) is held inactive for the duration of the transfer.
