     Continuous transfers for a SPI slave occur in the same way as those specified for the serial master
     configuration. The SPI slave configuration does not support the handshaking interface, as there is never a
     busy period.

 15.8.4.8 SPI Data Transfers
     For high-speed SPI, data transfers are started by the SPI master when the following 3 conditions are
     presented:

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                   Alif Semiconductor
                                                                1051
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                     www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                             E7 Series


       n The SPI is enabled (the SPI_ENR[SPI_EN] bit is set to 1)
       n The SPI slave device is enabled (the SPI_SER register is set)
       n The number of data entries in the transmit FIFO is greater than the value of the SPI_TXFTLR[TXFTHR] bit
         field
     For LPSPI, data transfers are started by the serial-master device. When the LPSPI is enabled (the LPSPI_ENR
     [SPI_EN] bit is set to 1), at least one valid data entry is present in the transmit FIFO and a serial-slave device is
     selected.
     For both high-speed SPI and LPSPI modules - while actively transferring the data, the SPI_SR[BUSY]/LPSPI_SR
     [BUSY] bit is set. Before attempting a new serial transfer, the software should wait until the busy flag (SPI_SR
     [BUSY]/LPSPI_SR[BUSY]) is cleared.


                                                          NOTE

       The SPI_SR[BUSY]/LPSPI_SR[BUSY] status bit is not set when the data are written into the transmit
       FIFO. This bit gets set only when the target SPI slave device has been selected and the transfer is
       underway. After writing data into the transmit FIFO, the shift control logic does not begin the serial
       transfer until a positive edge of the SPI_SCLK output signal is present. The delay in waiting for this
       positive edge depends on the baud rate of the serial transfer. Before polling the [BUSY] status bit, the
       software should first poll the SPI_SR[TFE]/LPSPI_SR[TFE] bit (waiting for 1) or wait for SPI_
       BAUDR/LPSPI_BAUDR register value × SPI_CLK cycles.


 15.8.4.9 SPI Receive Data (RXD) Sample Delay
                                                          NOTE

       This section is valid for high-speed SPI, when programmed as a master.


     The SPI module includes a logic to delay the default sample time of the RXD signal. This logic increases the
     maximum achievable frequency on the serial bus.
     Round trip routing delays on the SPI_SCLK signal from the master and the RXD signal from the slave can
     mean that the timing of the RXD signal—as seen by the master—has moved away from the normal sampling
     time.
     The slave uses the SPI_SCLK signal from the master as a strobe in order to drive the RXD signal onto the serial
     bus. Routing and sampling delays on the SPI_SCLK signal by the slave can mean that the RXD bit has not
     stabilized to the correct value before the master samples the RXD signal.
     With the RXD sample delay logic, a delay value can be dynamically programmed in order to move the
     sampling time of the RXD signal equal to a number of SPI_CLK cycles from the default. The RXD sample delay
     logic uses the positive edge of the SPI_CLK signal to sample the RXD signal. This increases the number of
     sampling points within an SPI_SCLK period and meet timings in higher frequencies.
     The number of the SPI_CLK cycles used to delay the sampling of the RXD signal can be set in the SPI_RX_
     SAMPLE_DELAY[RSD] bit field. Note that the maximum value that can be programmed in the SPI_RX_
     SAMPLE_DELAY[RSD] bit field is 4.



Hardware Reference Manual                                                                              Alif Semiconductor
                                                         1052
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


 15.8.4.10 SPI Receive and Transmit FIFO Buffers
     Each data entry in the FIFO buffers contains a single data frame and it is impossible to store multiple data
     frames into a single FIFO location.
     The transmit (Tx) FIFO is loaded by writing to the SPI data register (SPI_DRn/LPSPI_DRn). Data are popped
     (removed) from the Tx FIFO by the shift control logic into the transmit shift register. The Tx FIFO generates a
     Transmit FIFO Empty Interrupt request (SPI_TXE_IRQ) when the number of entries in the Tx FIFO is less than
     or equal to the Tx FIFO threshold value. The threshold value, set through the SPI_TXFTLR[TFT]/LPSPI_TXFTLR
     [TFT] bit field, determines the level of Tx FIFO entries at which an interrupt is generated. The threshold value
     allows early indication to the processor that the Tx FIFO is nearly empty. A Transmit FIFO Overflow Interrupt
     request (SPI_TXO_IRQ) is generated if an attempt to write data into an already full Tx FIFO is made. Through
     the SPI_TXFLR[TXTFL] bit field the software can read the number of valid data entries in the Tx FIFO.
     Data are popped from the receive (Rx) FIFO by reading from the SPI_DRn/LPSPI_DRn register. The Rx FIFO is
     loaded from the receive shift register by the shift control logic. The Rx FIFO generates a Receive FIFO Full
     Interrupt request (SPI_RXF_IRQ) when the number of entries in the Rx FIFO is greater than or equal to the Rx
     FIFO threshold value plus 1. The threshold value, set through the SPI_RXFTLR/LPSPI_RXFTLR register,
     determines the level of Rx FIFO entries at which an interrupt is generated. The threshold value allows early
     indication to the processor that the Rx FIFO is nearly full. A Rx FIFO Overrun interrupt (SPI_RXO_IRQ) is
     generated when the receive shift control logic attempts to load data into a completely full Rx FIFO. However,
     these newly received data are lost. A Rx FIFO Underflow interrupt (SPI_RXU_IRQ) is generated if an attempt
     to read from an empty Rx FIFO is made. This alerts the processor that the read data are invalid. Through the
     SPI_RXFLR[RXTFL]/LPSPI_RXFLR[RXTFL] bit field the software can read the number of valid data entries in the
     Rx FIFO.
     Note that the Tx and Rx FIFO buffers are cleared when the SPI is disabled (the SPI_ENR[SPI_EN]/LPSPI_ENR
     [SPI_EN] bit is set to 0).
     For more information about FIFO buffers size (width and depth), refer to Section 15.8.1 SPI Overview.

                                                             is derived from the following equation:
                                                                                  FSPI_SCLK = FSPI_CLK/SCKDV
                                                             Where SCKDV is any even value between 2 and 65534.
                                                             For example, for FSPI_CLK = 3.6864 MHz and SCKDV = 1b'1:
                                                             BAUDR = 2 and FSPI_SCLK= 3.6864/2 = 1.8432 MHz.
                                                             For more information, see Section 15.8.4.2.1 SPI Clock Ratios.
     0        RESERVED                 R          0x0        Reserved.

 15.8.5.3.25 SPI_DRn Register
           Offset           Access          Description
                                            SPI Data Register (n)
                                            The SPI data register is a 32-bit read/write buffer for the transmit/receive FIFOs.
                                            When the register is read, data in the receive FIFO buffer is accessed. When it is
                                            written, data are moved into the transmit FIFO buffer; a write can occur only when
                                            the SPI_ENR[SPI_EN] = 0x1. FIFOs are reset when the SPI_ENR[SPI_EN] = 0x0. The
    0x60 + (n × 0x4)
                             R/W            data register in the SPI occupies thirty-six 32-bit address locations of the memory
     Base address
                                            map to facilitate AHB burst transfers. Writing to any of these address locations has
                                            the same effect as pushing the data from the write data bus into the transmit FIFO.
                                            Reading from any of these locations has the same effect as popping data from the
                                            receive FIFO onto the read data bus. The FIFO buffers on the SPI are not
                                            addressable.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                             Data Register (n).
                                                             When writing to this register, the user must right-justify the data.
    31-0      DR                      R/W          0x0       Read data are automatically right-justified.
                                                             Read = Receive FIFO buffer
                                                             Write = Transmit FIFO buffer

     Base address                           default sample time) before the actual sample of the RXD input occurs. It is
                                            impossible to write to this register when the SPI is enabled.

    15-8     RESERVED           R        0x0       Reserved.

                                              LPSPI Control Register 0
    Bits   Field Name       Access   Reset Value Description
                                                    0xA: 11-bit Control Word
                                                    0xB: 12-bit Control Word
                                                    0xC: 13-bit Control Word
                                                    0xD: 14-bit Control Word
                                                    0xE: 15-bit Control Word
                                                    0xF: 16-bit Control Word
                                                    Shift Register Loop.
                                                    Used for testing purposes only. When internally active, connects
     11    SRL               R/W        0x0         the transmit shift register output to the receive shift register input.
                                                    0x0: Normal Mode Operation
                                                    0x1: Test Mode Operation
     10    RESERVED           R         0x0         Reserved.
                                                    Transfer Mode.
                                                    Selects the mode of transfer for serial communication. This field
                                                    does not affect the transfer duplicity. Only indicates whether the
                                                    receive or transmit data are valid.
                                                    In Transmit Only mode, data received from the external device is
                                                    not valid and is not stored in the receive FIFO memory; it is
                                                    overwritten on the next transfer.
                                                    In Receive Only mode, transmitted data are not valid. After the
                                                    first write to the transmit FIFO, the same word is retransmitted for
                                                    the duration of the transfer.
                                                    In Transmit and Receive mode, both transmit and receive data are
                                                    valid. The transfer continues until the transmit FIFO is empty. Data
    9-8    TMOD              R/W        0x0
                                                    received from the external device are stored into the receive FIFO
                                                    memory, where it can be accessed by the host processor.
                                                    In EEPROM-read mode, receive data is not valid while control data
                                                    is being transmitted. When all control data is sent to the EEPROM,
                                                    receive data becomes valid and transmit data becomes invalid. All
                                                    data in the transmit FIFO is considered control data in this mode.
                                                    This transfer mode is only valid when the LPSPI is programmed as
                                                    master device.
                                                    0x0: Transmit and Receive
                                                    0x1: Transmit Only mode
                                                    0x2: Receive Only mode
                                                    0x3: EEPROM Read mode
                                                    Serial Clock Polarity.
                                                    Valid when the Frame Format (FRF) bit is set to Motorola SPI. Used
                                                    to select the polarity of the inactive serial clock, which is held
     7     SCPOL             R/W        0x0
                                                    inactive when the LPSPI master is not actively transferring data on
                                                    the serial bus.
                                                    0x0: Inactive state of serial clock is low

 15.8.6.3.6 LPSPI_BAUDR Register
           Offset           Access          Description
                                            Baud Rate Select Register
         0x14                               The register derives the frequency of the serial clock that regulates the data
                             R/W
     Base address                           transfer. A 16-bit field in this register defines the LPSPI_CLK divider value. It is
                                            impossible to write to this register when the LPSPI is enabled.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
   31-16 RESERVED                      R           0x0        Reserved.
                                                              LPSPI Clock Divider.
    15-0      SCKDV                   R/W          0x0        This field contains the MSB 15 bits of the 16-bit LPSPI_CLK divider
                                                              value. The LSB for LPSPI_CLK divider is always set to 0 and is


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1076
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                       E7 Series


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                             unaffected by a write operation, which ensures the divider is
                                                             always set to an even value. If this field is set to all 0s, the serial
                                                             output clock (LPSPI_SCLK) is disabled. The frequency of the LPSPI_
                                                             SCLK is derived from the following equation:
                                                                               FLPSPI_SCLK = FLPSPI_CLK/SCKDV
                                                             Where SCKDV is any even value between 2 and 65534.
                                                             For example, for FLPSPI_CLK = 3.6864 MHz and SCKDV = 1b'1:
                                                             SCKDV = 2 and FLPSPI_SCLK= 3.6864/2 = 1.8432 MHz.
                                                             For more information, see Section 15.8.4.2.1 SPI Clock Ratios.

 15.9 Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART)

 15.9.1 UART Overview
     The Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART) module implements asynchronous serial
     communication interface based on standard Non-Return-to-Zero (NRZ) frame format.
     The device includes:
       n Up to eight UART modules in Shared Peripherals
       n One Low-Power UART module (LPUART) in the RTSS-HE
       n One UART module in the SESS (SEUART)—not accessible by user application

     The UART modules are integrated in the following power domains:
       n Power Domain PD-6: UART[0-7]
       n Power Domain PD-2: LPUART
       n Power Domain PD-5: SEUART

     Each UART module supports the following main features:
       n Full duplex operation
       n Programmable baud rates up to 2.5 Mbps with a fractional baud rate divisor
       n Interrupt driven or DMA controlled data transfer
       n Auto flow control compatible with 16750 devices
       n Configurable character length—5, 6, 7, 8 or 9 bits
       n Optional parity bit—Even, Odd, Stick
       n Number of stop bits—1, 1.5, 2 bits
       n Line break generation and detection
       n CTS/RTS signals for hardware flow control
       n Drive enable output for RS485 interface support on UART[4-7] only
       n Transmit (Tx) and Receive (Rx) FIFO depth of 32 characters
       n Loopback mode for test and troubleshooting
       n False start bit detection
       n Compatible with the industry standard 16550 devices
       n The LPUART interrupt can be used as a wake-up source from STANDBY low-power mode



                                                       NOTE

       All Low Power peripherals are single-master accessible, including LPUART. Ensure that application
       software manages access to these LP peripherals such that no more than one bus master (CPU or
       DMA) attempts access at a time, using semaphores or similar techniques.

 15.9.4.4 UART DMA Requests
       The UART supports DMA signalling with the use of the DMA_TX_REQ and DMA_RX_REQ output signals to
       indicate:
         n    When data can be read
         n    When Tx FIFO is empty


                                                                          NOTE

         The DMA_TX_REQ is not asserted upon reset. It is asserted only after the UART_LCR register is written
         and if any of the conditions for assertion from Section 15.9.4.4.1 DMA Interface is met. The reset
         under consideration is both a hardware reset and a software reset (triggered by writing to the UART_
         SRR register).


 15.9.4.4.1 DMA Interface
       The DMA_TX_REQ signal is asserted under the following conditions:
         n    When the UART_THR is empty if FIFOs are disabled
         n    When the Tx FIFO is empty if FIFOs are enabled and the programmable THRE interrupt mode is disabled

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                                  Alif Semiconductor
                                                                          1095
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                                    www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                        E7 Series


       n   When the Tx FIFO is at or below the programmed threshold with programmable THRE interrupt mode
           enabled
     The DMA_RX_REQ signal is asserted under the following conditions:
       n   When a single character is available in UART_RBR if FIFOs are disabled
       n   When Rx FIFO is at or above programmed trigger level if FIFOs are enabled
     With the presence of the additional handshake signals, the UART does not have to rely on internal status and
     level values to recognize the completion of a request and hence remove the request. Instead, the deassertion
     of the DMA transmit and receive requests is controlled by the assertion of the DMA transmit and receive
     acknowledge, respectively.
     The responsibility for the data flow falls on the DMA and is controlled by the programmed burst transaction
     lengths.

 15.9.4.4.2 Transmit Watermark Level and Transmit FIFO Underflow
     During UART serial transfers, Tx FIFO requests are made to the DMAC whenever the number of entries in the
     Tx FIFO is less than or equal to the value of the UART_FCR[TET] bit field. This is known as a transmit
     Watermark Level (WL). The DMAC responds by writing a burst of data to the Tx FIFO buffer.
     Data should be fetched from the DMA often enough for the Tx FIFO to perform serial transfers continuously;
     that is, when the Tx FIFO begins to empty, another DMA request should be triggered. Otherwise, the Tx FIFO
     runs out of data (Tx FIFO underflow occurs).

 15.9.4.4.2.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level
     The goal in choosing a proper WL is to minimize the number of transactions per DMA block transfer, while at
     the same time keeping the probability of an underflow condition to an acceptable level. In practice, this is a
     function of the ratio of the rate at which the UART transmits data to the rate at which the DMA controller
     can respond to destination burst requests.
     Figure 15-143 and Figure 15-144 illustrate two example cases for different WL settings. In both examples the
     following assumptions are made:
       n   The needed Number of Burst Transactions (NBT) equals the DMA Transfer Block Size divided by the
           Number of Data Items (NDI) per DMA Burst, as defined by equation 15-20:
                                                                                                             (15-20)

           Where:
           The value of DMA Transfer Block Size is programmed at DMAC level. It defines the number of data
           transfers that the DMAC performs when it writes the destination data. See Section 12.2 DMA
           Controllers for more information.
       n   The value of NDI per DMA Burst is defined by equation 15-21, where:
           l Tx FIFO Depth is as specified in Section 15.9.1 UART Overview.
           l Tx FIFO WL is programmed in the UART_FCR[TET] bit field.


                                                                                                             (15-21)
     Figure 15-143 (Case 1) shows an example where the selected WL is low. Therefore, the probability of an
     UART underflow is high where the UART serial transmit line needs to transmit data, but where there is no
     data left in the Tx FIFO. This occurs because the DMAC has not had time to service the DMA request before
     the Tx FIFO becomes empty.

                      FIFO Depth           EMPTY

                         Data Out           FULL                                        Data In

                                           Tx FIFO

     Figure 15-144 (Case 2) shows an example where the selected WL is high. Therefore, the probability of an
     UART underflow is low because the DMAC has plenty of time to service the destination burst transaction
     request before the Tx FIFO becomes empty.

     Figure 15-144 (Case 2) has a lower probability of underflow at possibly the expense of more burst
     transactions per block. This may provide a potentially greater amount of data bursts per block and worse bus
     utilization than Figure 15-143 (Case 1).
     To increase the rate at which the DMA controller can respond to burst transaction requests, the UART DMA
     channel could be promoted to the highest priority channel in the DMA, and the DMA master interface could
     be promoted to the highest priority master at system interconnect level. This in turn allows to decrease the
     WL, which improves bus utilization without compromising the probability of an underflow occurring.

 15.9.4.4.2.2 Selecting Number of Data Items per DMA Burst and Transmit FIFO Overflow
     As shown in Figure 15-144, programming the NDI per DMA Burst to a value greater than the WL that triggers
     the DMA request may cause overflow when there is not enough space in the Tx FIFO to service the
     destination burst request. Therefore, the equation 15-22 must be adhered to in order to avoid overflow:
                                                                                                                      (15-22)




Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                  Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1097
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                    www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                         E7 Series


     In Case 2 (refer to Section 15.9.4.4.2.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level), the amount of space in the Tx
     FIFO at the time the burst request is made is equal to the destination burst length (NDI per DMA Burst). Thus,
     the Tx FIFO may be full, but not overflowed, at the completion of the burst transaction.
     For optimal operation, in equation 15-21, the NDI per DMA Burst should be set at the Tx FIFO level that
     triggers a transmit DMA request.
     Adhering to this equation reduces the number of DMA bursts needed for a block transfer, and this in turn
     improves AMBA bus utilization.
     Note that the Tx FIFO is not full at the end of a DMA burst transfer if the UART has successfully transmitted
     one data item or more on the UART serial transmit line during the transfer.

 15.9.4.4.3 Receive Watermark Level and Receive FIFO Overflow
     During UART serial transfers, Rx FIFO requests are made to the DMA controller whenever the number of
     entries in the Rx FIFO is at or above the UART_FCR[RT] bit field value. This is known as the WL. The
     DMA controller responds by fetching a burst of data from the Rx FIFO buffer.
     Data should be fetched by the DMA often enough for the Rx FIFO to accept serial transfers continuously (that
     is, when the FIFO begins to fill, another DMA transfer is requested). Otherwise, the FIFO fills with data
     (overflow). To prevent this condition, watermark level must be set correctly.

 15.9.4.4.3.1 Choosing Receive Watermark level
     Similar to choosing the transmit WL described in Section 15.9.4.4.2.1 Choosing Transmit Watermark Level,
     the receive WL (UART_FCR[RT]), should be set to minimize the probability of overflow, as shown in Figure 15-
     145. It is a trade-off between the number of DMA burst transactions required per block versus the
     probability of an overflow occurring.
                                                Figure 15-145 UART Receive FIFO(1)
       Rx FIFO
       Watermark Level

                                            EMPTY


                              Data In         FULL                                   Data Out     DMA
                                                                                                Controller
                                                             UART_FCR[RT]
                                                                                                             UART-006
                                            Rx FIFO

     underflow when there is not enough data to service the source burst request.
     If the NDI in the Rx FIFO is equal to the Source Burst Transaction Length at the time the burst request is
     made—the Rx FIFO may be emptied, but not underflowed, at the completion of the burst transaction. For
     optimal operation, the Source Burst Transaction Length should be set at the WL, as shown in equation 15-23:

     Adhering to this equation reduces the number of DMA bursts in a block transfer, which in turn can avoid

     Note that the Rx FIFO is not empty at the end of the source burst transaction if the UART has successfully
     received one data item or more on the UART serial receive line during the burst.

 15.9.4.5 UART Serial Protocol
     Because the serial communication between the UART and a selected device is asynchronous, additional bits
     (START and STOP) are added to the serial data to indicate beginning and end. Utilizing these bits allows two
     devices to be synchronized. This structure of serial data accompanied by START and STOP bits is referred to
     as a character, as shown in Figure 15-146.
                                                 Figure 15-146 Serial Data Format(1)
                        Bit Time

   Serial Data             START           Data bits              5-8                  Parity        STOP      1, 1.5, 2

                                                                                                                              UART-007
                                                                  One Character


     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     An additional parity bit can be added to the serial character. This bit appears after the last data bit and
     before the STOP bits in the character structure in order to provide the UART with the ability to perform
     simple error checking on the received data.
     The UART_LCR is used to control the serial character characteristics. The individual bits of the data word are
     sent after the START bit, starting with the LSB bit. These are followed by the optional PARITY bit, followed by
     the STOP bits, which can be 1, 1.5, or 2.
     All the bits in the transmission are transmitted for exactly the same time duration. The exception to this is
     the half-stop bit when 1.5 stop bits are used. This duration is referred to as a Bit Period or Bit Time (one Bit
     Time equals sixteen baud clocks).
     To ensure stability on the line, the receiver samples the serial input data at approximately the midpoint of
     the Bit Time once the START bit has been detected. Because the exact number of baud clocks for which each
     bit is transmitted is known, calculating the midpoint for sampling is not difficult. That is, every sixteen baud
     clocks after the midpoint sample of the START bit.
     Together with serial input debouncing, this sampling helps to avoid the detection of false START bits. Short
     glitches are filtered out by debouncing, and no transition is detected on the line. If a glitch is wide enough to
     avoid filtering by debouncing, a falling edge is detected. However, a START bit is detected only if the line is
     again sampled low after half a bit time has elapsed.
     Figure 15-147 shows the sampling points of the first two bits in a serial character.
                                       Figure 15-147 Receiver Serial Data Sample Points(1)

 Serial Data In                    START                                   Data Bit 0 (LSB)                 Data Bit 1




                                                                                                                                   UART-008
                       8                                16                                      16

     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.

 15.9.4.6 UART 9-bit Data Transfer
     The UART can be configured to have 9-bit data transfer in both transmit and receive modes. The 9th bit in the
     character appears after the 8th bit and before the parity bit in the character. Figure 15-148 shows the serial
     transmission for a character in which D8 represents the 9th bit and also shows general serial transmission in
     the 9-bit mode.
                                                   Figure 15-148 9-Bit Character(1)

                                                     START D0 to D7     D8    Parity STOP


                         =1                                           =0                                            =0
     START D0 to D7      D8   Parity STOP   IDLE START D0 to D7       D8     Parity STOP    IDLE START D0 to D7     D8    Parity STOP


      Address Byte with 9th bit set to 1                Data Byte with 9th bit set to 0           Data Byte with 9th bit set to 0
                                                                                                                                     UART-009




     1. Contains Synopsys proprietary information. Used with permission.


     By enabling 9-bit data transfer mode, UART can be used in multi-drop systems where one master is
     connected to multiple slaves in a system. The master communicates with one of the slaves. When the master
     wants to transfer a block of data to a slave, it first sends an address byte to identify the target slave.
     The differentiation between the address and data byte is done based on the 9th bit in the incoming
     character. If the 9th bit is set to 0, then the character represents a data byte. If the 9th bit is set to 1, then the
     character represents address byte. All the slave systems compare the address byte with their own address
     and only the target slave (where the address has matched) is enabled to receive data from the master. The
     master then starts transmitting data bytes to the target slave. The non-addressed slave systems ignore the
     incoming data until a new address byte is received.
     Note that in Figure 15-148, one address is followed by two data bytes. The address byte goes out with the 9th
     bit (D8) set to 1 and the data bytes go out with 9th bit (D8) set to 0. The parity bit is an optional field.
     Configuration of the UART for 9-bit data transfer uses the following registers settings:
       n UART_LCR_EXT[DLS_E] bit to enable or disable the 9-bit data transfer
       n UART_LCR_EXT[ADDR_MATCH] bit to choose between hardware and software based address match in
         the case of receive
       n UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] bit to enable address sending in the case of transmit
       n UART_LCR_EXT[TRANSMIT_MODE] bit to choose between hardware and software based address
         transmission
       n UART_TAR and UART_RAR registers to transmit address and to match the received address, respectively
       n UART_THR, UART_RBR, UART_STHRn and UART_SRBRn registers to do the data transfers in 9-bit mode
       n UART_LSR[ADDR_RCVD] bit to indicate the address received interrupt


 15.9.4.6.1 Transmit Mode
     The UART supports two types of transmit modes:
       n   Transmit Mode 0 (when (UART_LCR_EXT[TRANSMIT_MODE]) is set to 0)
       n   Transmit Mode 1 (when (UART_LCR_EXT[TRANSMIT_MODE]) is set to 1)

 15.9.4.6.1.1 Transmit Mode 0
     In Transmit Mode 0, the address is programmed in the UART_TAR register and data is written into the UART_
     THR or the UART_STHRn register. The 9th bit of the UART_THR and UART_STHRn register is not applicable in
     this mode.
     Figure 15-149 illustrates the transmission of address and data based on UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR], Halt Tx
     (UART_HTX), and Tx FIFO/UART_THR empty conditions.

     The address of the target slave to which the data is to be transmitted is programmed in the UART_TAR
     register. The UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] bit must be enabled to transmit the target slave address present
     in the UART_TAR register on the serial UART line with 9th data bit set to 1 to indicate that the address is
     being sent to the slave. The UART clears the UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] bit after the address character
     starts transmitting on the UART line.
     The data required to transmit to the target slave is programmed through UART_THR register. The data is
     transmitted on the UART line with 9th data bit set to 0 to indicate data is being sent to the slave.
     If the application is required to fill the data bytes in the Tx FIFO before sending the address on the UART line
     (before setting UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] to 1), it is recommended to set the UART_HTX[HTX] to 1, so that
     UART does not start sending out the data in the Tx FIFO as data byte. Once the Tx FIFO is filled, set UART_
     LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] to 1 and then set UART_HTX[HTX] to 0.

 15.9.4.6.1.2 Transmit Mode 1
     In Transmit Mode 1, UART_THR and UART_STHRn registers are of 9-bit wide and both address and data are
     programmed through the UART_THR and UART_STHRn registers. The UART does not differentiate between
     address and data, and both are taken from the Tx FIFO. The UART_LCR_EXT[SEND_ADDR] bit and UART_TAR
Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                        Alif Semiconductor
                                                                     1101
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                          www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                        E7 Series


     are not applicable in this mode. The software must pack the 9th bit with 1 or 0 depending on whether
     address or data has to be sent.

 15.9.4.6.2 Receive Mode
     The UART supports two receive modes:
       n Hardware address match receive mode (when UART_LCR_EXT[ADDR_MATCH] bit is set to 1)
       n Software address match receive mode (when UART_LCR_EXT[ADDR_MATCH] bit is set to 0)


 15.9.4.6.2.1 Hardware Address Match Receive Mode
     In the hardware address match receive mode, the UART matches the received character with the address
     programmed in the UART_RAR register, if the 9th bit of the received character is set to 1. If the received
     address is matched with the programmed address in UART_RAR register, then subsequent data bytes (with
     9th bit set to 0) are pushed into the Rx FIFO. If the address matching fails, then the UART discards further
     data characters until a matching address is received.
     Figure 15-150 illustrates the flow chart for the reception of data bytes based on the address matching
     feature.

     The UART receives the character irrespective of whether the 9th data bit is set to 1. If 9th bit of the received
     character is set to 1, then it clears internal address match flag and then compares the received 8-bit
     character information with the address programmed in the UART_RAR register.
     If the received address character matches with the address programmed in the UART_RAR register, then the
     address match flag is set to 1, and the received character is pushed to the Rx FIFO if FIFOs are enabled or to
     UART_RBR register if FIFOs are disabled, and the UART_LSR[ADDR_RCVD] bit is set to indicate that the
     address has been received.
     In case of parity or if a framing error is found in the received address character, and if the address is not
     matched with the UART_RAR register, the received address character is still pushed to the Rx FIFO or UART_
     RBR register, with the UART_LSR[ADDR_RCVD] and UART_LSR[PE] or UART_LSR[FE] error bits set to 1.
     The subsequent data bytes (9th bit of received character is set to 0) are pushed to the Rx FIFO if FIFOs are
     enabled, or to the UART_RBR register if FIFOs are disabled until the new address character is received.
     If any break character is received, the UART treats it as a special character and pushes to the Rx FIFO or
     UART_RBR register based on whether FIFOs are enabled or disabled, irrespective of the address match flag.

 15.9.4.6.2.2 Software Address Match Receive Mode
     In this mode of operation, the UART does not perform the address matching for the received address
     character (9th data bit set to 1) with the UART_RAR register. The UART always receives the 9-bit data and
     pushes in to Rx FIFO if FIFOs are enabled, or to the UART_RBR register if FIFOs are disabled. Address byte is
     received and indicated through UART_LSR[ADDR_RCVD] bit. Then flush or reset the Rx FIFO in case of
     address not matched through UART_FCR[RT] bit.

 15.9.4.7 UART RS485 Serial Protocol


                                                           NOTE

       This section is valid only for UART[4-7] modules.


     The UART module supports the RS485 serial protocol that enables transfer of serial data using the RS485
     interface. The Driver Enable (DE) signal is generated for enabling the RS485 interface support. The DE signal is
     hardware generated and the assertion/deassertion times for this signal are programmable. The DE signal is
     active high level.
     Configuration of the UART for RS485 interface uses the following registers settings:
      1. UART_TCR[RS485_EN] to enable or disable the RS485 mode
      2. UART_TCR[DE_POL] to select the polarity of DE signal
      3. UART_TCR[XFER_MODE] to select the type of transfer in RS485 mode
      4. UART_DE_EN register for software control of DE signal
      5. UART_DET register to program the assertion and deassertion timings of DE signal
     To check UART RS485 status read UART_CTRL[RS485] register field.

 15.9.4.7.1 DE Signal Assertion and Deassertion Timing
     The assertion and deassertion timings of the DE signal are controlled through the UART_DET register:
       n   DE assertion time (UART_DET[DE_ASSERTION_TIME]): The assertion time is the time between the
           activation of the DE signal and the beginning of the START bit. The value represented is in terms of serial

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                           Alif Semiconductor
                                                        1103
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                              www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                      E7 Series


           clock cycles.
         n DE deassertion time (UART_DET[DE_DE-ASSERTION_TIM]): The deassertion time is the time between
           the end of the last STOP bit, in a transmitted character, and the deactivation of the DE signal. The value
           represented is in terms of serial clock cycles.
       Hardware ensures that these values are met for DE assertion and DE deassertion before/after active data
       transmission.
       Note that for simplicity only one set of data is illustrated in Figure 15-151; however, DE does not get
       deasserted if there are more data characters in Tx FIFO. DE gets de-asserted only after all the data characters
       are transmitted.

         n Full-Duplex mode—In this mode UART_TCR[XFER_MODE] is set to 0.
         n Software-Controlled Half-Duplex mode—In this mode UART_TCR[XFER_MODE] is set to 1.
         n Hardware-Controlled Half-Duplex mode—In this mode UART_TCR[XFER_MODE] is set to 2.

           l The current ongoing transmitting serial transfer is completed

       n The acceptable baud-rate error, %ERROR

 15.9.4.8.1 Fractional Division Used to Generate Baud Clock
     Fractional division of clock is used by the (N / N + 1) divider, where N is the integer part of the divisor. N / N +
     1 division works on the basis of achieving the required average timing over a long period by alternating the
     division between two numbers. If N = 1 and ratio of (N / N + 1) is same, which means equal number of divide
     by 1 and divide by 2 over a period of time, average time period would come out to be divided by 1.5. Varying
     the ratio of N / N + 1 any value can be achieved above 1 and below 2.

 15.9.4.9 UART FIFO Support
     The UART is configured to implement FIFOs that buffer transmit and receive data. If FIFO is not enabled
     (UART_FCR[FIFOE] is set to 0), then only a single receive data byte and transmit data byte can be stored at a
     time in the UART_RBR and UART_THR registers, respectively. This implies a 16450-compatible mode of
     operation. However, in this mode of operation, most of the enhanced features are unavailable.
     To enable FIFOs, the bit UART_FCR[FIFOE] has to be set to 1.
     The UART modules support FIFO Access Mode, which can be used for test purposes (not supported by
     LPUART). This mode allows:


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                          Alif Semiconductor
                                                       1109
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                                     E7 Series


       n Rx FIFO to be written by master
       n Tx FIFO to be read by master

     The FIFO Access Mode can be enabled with the FIFO access register (UART_FAR[FAR]). Once enabled, the
     control portions of the Tx/Rx FIFOs are reset and the FIFOs are treated as empty.
     Data can be written to the Tx FIFO as normal. However, no serial transmission occurs in this mode, normal
     operation halted and thus no data leave the FIFO. The data that has been written to the Tx FIFO can be read
     back with the UART_TFR register, which when read, provides the current data at the top of the Tx FIFO.
     Similarly, data can be read from the Rx FIFO as normal. Since the normal operation of the UART is halted in
     this mode, data must be written to the Rx FIFO so that it can be read back.
     Data is written to the Rx FIFO using the UART_RFW register. The upper two bits of the 10-bit register are
     used to write framing error and parity error detection information to the Rx FIFO, as follows:
       n   UART_RFW[RFFE] indicates framing error
       n   UART_RFW[RFPE] indicates parity error
     Although these bits cannot be read back through the UART_RBR, they can be checked by reading the UART_
     LSR and checking the corresponding bits when the data in question is at the top of the Rx FIFO.

Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                            Alif Semiconductor

       n Both the UART_MCR[RTS] bit and UART_MCR[AFCE] bit are both set

     If Auto RTS is enabled, the RTS output is forced inactive (high) when the receiver FIFO level reaches the
     threshold set by UART_FCR[RT], but only if the RTC flow-control trigger is disabled. Otherwise, the RTS
     output is forced inactive when the FIFO is almost full. The FIFO being almost full means that there are only
     two available slots in the FIFO.
     When RTS is connected to the CTS input of another UART device, the other UART stops sending serial data
     until the Rx FIFO has available space and that is, until it is completely empty.
     The selectable Rx FIFO threshold values are:
       n 1 character in FIFO
       n FIFO is 1/4 full
       n FIFO is 1/2 full
       n FIFO has 2 characters till full

     Since one additional character can be transmitted to the UART after RTS has become inactive due to data
     already having entered the transmitter block in the other UART, setting the threshold to “2 less than full”
     allows maximum use of the FIFO with a safety zone of one character.
     Once the Rx FIFO becomes completely empty by reading the UART_RBR, RTS again becomes active (low),
     signaling the other UART to continue sending data.

     When Auto CTS is enabled (active), the UART transmitter is disabled whenever the CTS input becomes
     inactive (high); this prevents overflowing the FIFO of the receiving UART.
     If the CTS input is not inactivated before the middle of the last STOP bit, another character is transmitted
     before the transmitter is disabled. While the transmitter is disabled, the Tx FIFO can still be written to, and
     even overflowed.

       n UART status register can be read to check if Tx FIFO is full (UART_USR[TFNF] is set to 0)
       n Current FIFO level can be read using UART_TFL register
       n Programmable THRE interrupt mode must be enabled to access FIFO full status using UART_LSR register

     When using the FIFO full status, software can poll this before each write to the Tx FIFO (see Section 15.9.4.11
     UART Programmable THRE Interrupt). When the CTS input becomes active (low) again, transmission resumes.

 15.9.4.11 UART Programmable THRE Interrupt
     The UART module has programmable THRE interrupt mode, which helps to increase system performance.
     Programmable THRE interrupt mode can be enabled using the UART_IER[PTIME] bit.
     When FIFOs and THRE mode are enabled, the THRE interrupts and DMA_TX_REQ are active at and below a
     programmed Tx FIFO empty threshold level, as opposed to empty, as shown in the flowchart in Figure 15-
     155.

     The threshold level is programmed into UART_FCR[TET]. Available empty thresholds are:
       n FIFO is empty
       n FIFO has 2 characters
       n FIFO is 1/4 full
       n FIFO is 1/2 full

     Selection of the best threshold value depends on the system ability to begin a new transmission sequence in
     a timely manner. However, one of these thresholds should be optimal for increasing system performance by
     preventing the Tx FIFO from running empty.
     In addition to the interrupt change, the UART_LSR[THRE] also switches from indicating that the Tx FIFO is
     empty to the FIFO being full. This allows software to fill the FIFO for each transmit sequence by polling
     UART_LSR[THRE] before writing another character. The flow then allows the Tx FIFO to be filled whenever an
     interrupt occurs and there is data to transmit, rather than waiting until the FIFO is completely empty. Waiting
     until the FIFO is empty causes a reduction in performance whenever the system is too busy to respond
     immediately. Further system efficiency is achieved when this mode is enabled in combination with auto flow
     control.
     If the FIFOs are disabled using the UART_FCR[FIFOE] bit, the programmable THRE interrupt mode is also
     disabled. When disabled, THRE interrupts and the UART_LSR[THRE] bit function normally, signifying an empty
     THR or FIFO.

 15.9.4.12 UART Clock Gate Enable
     The UART module supports clock gate enable output signals that are used to indicate the following:
       n Transmit and receive pipelines are clear
       n No activity has occurred
       n Modem control input signals have not changed in more than one character time—the time taken to
         transmit or receive a character—so that clocks can be gated.
     To gate the UART clock, the following criteria should be valid for at least one character (see 15-36) time:
       n No data in the UART_RBR (if FIFOs are disabled) or the RX FIFO is empty (if FIFOs are enabled)
       n No data in the UART_THR (if FIFOs are disabled) or the TX FIFO is empty (in FIFOs are enabled)
       n Serial data input (Rx) and serial data output (Tx) signals are inactive (Rx and Tx are kept high)
       n No change on the modem control input signals

     Note that the clock gating cannot be done in the following modes of operation:
       n Loopback mode
       n FIFO access mode
       n When transmitting a break

     A character consists of:
                                                                                                                         (15-36)
     Where:
     *—Optional
     Clocks are resumed under any of these conditions:
Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                     Alif Semiconductor
                                                               1114
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                       www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                           E7 Series


       n Serial data input (Rx) signal goes low
       n Write to any of registers is performed
       n Modem control input signals have changed when the UART is in low-power (sleep) mode

     The time taken for the clocks to resume is important in preventing receive data synchronization problems,
     due to the UART RX block sampling:
       n   At the midpoint of each bit period, after approximately 8 baud clocks, in UART (RS232) mode
       n   After that, every 16 baud clocks for a baud divisor of 1 that is 16 serial clock periods
     Thus, if eight or more serial clock periods pass before the serial clock starts up again, the UART can get out of
     synchronization with the serial data it is receiving. That is, the receiver can sample into the second bit period,
     and if it is still 0, the receiver uses this as the start bit, and so on.
     In order to avoid this problem, the clock should be resumed within five clock periods of the baud clock, which
     is the same as SCLK if the baud divisor is set to 1—this is the worst-case. If the divisor is greater, it gives a
     greater number of serial clock cycles available before the clock must resume. This means a sample point
     occurring at the 13 baud clock (at the latest) out of the 16 transmitted for each bit period of the character.
     For UART modules only: If the timing of the received signal is not affected by the synchronization problem,
     then if the baud divisor is 1, the minimum character receiving time is 112 SCLKs:
                                                                                                                (15-37)


     Therefore, the PCLK must be available before 112 SCLK cycles pass in order for the received character to be
     synchronized to the PCLK domain and stored in the Rx FIFO.

 15.9.4.13 UART Back-to-Back Character Stream Transmission
     This section describes:
       n Scenarios under which the UART is capable of transmitting back-to-back characters on the serial
         interface, with no idle time between them
       n Worst-case idle time that exists between back-to-back characters

     When the Tx FIFO contains multiple data entries, the UART transmits the characters in the FIFO back-to-back
     on the serial bus. Synchronization delays in the UART can cause an IDLE period between the end of the
     current STOP bit and the beginning of the next START bit. This appears as an extended STOP bit duration on
     the serial bus.

 15.9.4.13.1 Dual Clock Mode


                                                         NOTE

       This section applies only to UART modules.


     The dual clock mode indicates an asynchronous relationship between PCLK and SCLK. The UART has a
     synchronization delay between the transmitter in the SCLK domain and the Tx FIFO in the PCLK domain when
     querying if another character is ready for transmission. The transmitter begins the handshake one baud clock
     cycle before the end of the current STOP bit. The duration of the synchronization delay is given by the
     following equations:

     The following procedure is for programming RS485 in Hardware-Controlled Half-Duplex Mode (XFER_MODE =
     2).
       n Program the UART_TCR register to set the XFER_MODE to 2, UART_DE_POL (polarity of DE signal)
       n Program the DE assertion and deassertion timing in the UART_DET register
       n Program UART_DE_EN register to enable the transmit paths
       n Perform the data transmission
       n Once the UART_DE_EN is programmed to 1, then by default DE is deasserted. When the software
         pushes the data into the Tx FIFO then the DE signal gets asserted until the Tx FIFO has data to be
         transmitted
       n The UART_DE_EN still serves as the software overrides to decide when to shutdown transmit path

 15.9.5.3 UART Registers Description

 15.9.5.3.1 UART_RBR Register
           Offset             Access          Description
         0x0                                  Receive Buffer Register
                                 R
     Base address                             This register is accessed only when the UART_LCR[DLAB] is cleared.


    Bits      Field Name               Access    Reset Value Description
    31-9      RESERVED                   R            0x0      Reserved.
                                                               Receive Buffer Register Field
                                                               This field contains the data byte received on the serial input port.
                                                               The data is valid only if the UART_LSR[DR] is set.
                                                               If FIFOs are disabled (UART_FCR[FIFOE] set to 0), the data in the
                                                               UART_RBR must be read before the next data arrives, otherwise it
    8-0       RBR                        R            0x0      will be overwritten, resulting in an over-run error.
                                                               If FIFOs are enabled (UART_FCR[FIFOE] set to 1), this register
                                                               accesses the head of the Rx FIFO. If the Rx FIFO is full and this field
                                                               is not read before the next data character arrives, then the data
                                                               already in the FIFO will be preserved, but any incoming data will
                                                               be lost and an over-run error occurs.



 15.9.5.3.2 UART_DLL Register
           Offset             Access          Description
                                              Divisor Latch Low Register
         0x0
                               R/W            This register contains the lower 8 bits of 16 for the UART baud rate divisor. This
     Base address
                                              register is accessed only when the UART_LCR[DLAB] is set.


    Bits      Field Name               Access    Reset Value Description
    31-8      RESERVED                   R            0x0      Reserved.


Hardware Reference Manual                                                                                         Alif Semiconductor
                                                                 1124
AHRM0005 v2.9—June 2025                                                                                            www.alifsemi.com
                                                                                                                      E7 Series


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                             Divisor Latch Low Field
                                                             The output baud rate is equal to serial clock frequency (SCLK for
                                                             UART, PCLK for LPUART) divided by 16 times the value of the baud
                                                             rate divisor, as follows:
                                                             baud rate = (serial clock frequency) / (16 × divisor).
    7-0       DLL                     R/W          0x0
                                                             Note: With the Divisor Latch registers (UART_DLL and UART_DLH)
                                                             set to 0, the baud clock is disabled and no serial communication
                                                             will occur. Also, once the DLL is set, at least 8 clock cycles of the
                                                             slowest UART clock should be allowed to pass before transmitting
                                                             or receiving data.



 15.9.5.3.3 UART_THR Register
           Offset           Access          Description
         0x0                                Transmit Holding Register
                             R/W
     Base address                           This register is accessed only when the UART_LCR[DLAB] is cleared.


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
    31-9      RESERVED                 R           0x0       Reserved.
                                                             This field contains data to be transmitted on the serial output port.
                                                             Data should only be written to the THR when the UART_LSR[THRE]
                                                             is set.
                                                             If FIFOs are disabled (UART_FCR[FIFOE] set to 0) and UART_LSR
                                                             [THRE] is set, writing a single character to the THR field clears the
                                                             UART_LSR[THRE]. Any additional writes to the THR before the
                                                             UART_LSR[THRE] is set again cause the THR data to be
    8-0       THR                      W           0x0
                                                             overwritten.
                                                             If FIFOs are enabled (UART_FCR[FIFOE] set to 1) and UART_LSR
                                                             [THRE] is set, 32 number of characters of data may be written to
                                                             the THR before the FIFO is full. Any attempt to write data when
                                                             the FIFO is full results in the write data being lost.
                                                             Note: The 9th bit is applicable only when UART_LCR_EXT
                                                             [TRANSMIT_MODE]=1.

 15.9.5.3.8 UART_LCR Register
           Offset           Access          Description
         0xC
                             R/W            Line Control Register
     Base address


    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
    31-8      RESERVED                 R          0x0        Reserved.
                                                             Divisor Latch Access Bit
                                                             This bit is used to enable reading and writing of the Divisor Latch
                                                             registers (UART_DLL and UART_DLH). This bit must be cleared
     7        DLAB                    R/W         0x0
                                                             after initial baud rate setup in order to access other registers.
                                                             0x0: Divisor Latch register is writable only when UART is not busy
                                                             0x1: Divisor Latch register is always readable and writable
                                                             Break Control Bit
                                                             This bit is used to cause a break condition to be transmitted to the
                                                             receiving device. If set to 1, the UART_TX is forced to the spacing
                                                             (logic 0) state.

     6        BC                      R/W         0x0
                                                             [LOOPBACK], the UART_TX is forced low until the bit is cleared.
                                                             When in Loopback mode, the break condition is internally looped
                                                             back to the receiver.
                                                             0x0: UART_TX is released for data transmission
                                                             0x1: UART_TX is forced to spacing state
                                                             Stick Parity
                                                             This bit is used to force parity value. When PEN, EPS and SP bits
                                                             are set to 1, the parity bit is transmitted and checked as logic 0.
     5        SP                      R/W         0x0        If PEN and SP are set to 1 and EPS is a logic 0, then parity bit is
                                                             transmitted and checked as a logic 1.
                                                             0x0: Stick parity disabled
                                                             0x1: Stick parity enabled
                                                             Even Parity Select
                                                             This bit is used to select between even and odd parity, when PEN
     4        EPS                     R/W         0x0        set to 1.
                                                             0x0: An odd parity is transmitted or checked
                                                             0x1: An even parity is transmitted or checked
                                                             Parity Enable
     3        PEN                     R/W         0x0        This bit is used to enable/disable parity generation and detection
                                                             in transmitted and received serial character, respectively.

                                                              1129

    Bits      Field Name             Access   Reset Value Description
                                                           0x0: Disable parity
                                                           0x1: Enable parity
                                                           Number of Stop Bit
                                                           This bit is used to select the number of stop bits per character that
                                                           the peripheral will transmit and receive.
                                                           If set to 0, one stop bit is transmitted in the serial data.
                                                           If set to 1 and the data bits are set to 5 (UART_LCR[DLS] set to 0)
                                                           one and a half stop bits are transmitted. Otherwise, 2 stop bits are
                                                           transmitted.
                                                           Note that regardless of the number of stop bits selected the
     2        STOP                    R/W         0x0      receiver will only check the first stop bit.
                                                           The STOP bit duration implemented by UART may appear longer
                                                           due to IDLE time inserted between characters for some
                                                           configurations and baud clock divisor values in the transmit
                                                           direction; for details on IDLE time between transmitted transfers,
                                                           refer to Section 15.9.4.13 UART Back-to-Back Character Stream
                                                           Transmission
                                                           0x0: 1 stop bit
                                                           0x1: 1.5 stop bits when UART_LCR[DLS] is 0, 2 stop bits otherwise

    1-0       DLS                     R/W         0x0

                                                           0x3: 8 data bits per character

                                                  purposes. Data on the UART_TX is held high, while UART_TX is
                                                  looped back to the UART_RX, internally. In this mode all the
                                                  interrupts are fully functional.
                                                  In Loopback mode, the modem control inputs are disconnected
                                                  and the modem control outputs are looped back to the inputs
                                                  internally.
                                                  0x0: Loopback mode disabled
                                                  0x1: Loopback mode enabled
                                                  This bit is used to directly control the internal OUT2 signal. The
                                                  value written to this location is inverted and driven out on OUT2.
                                                  Note that in Loopback mode (UART_MCR[LOOPBACK] set to 1),
     3     OUT2              R/W        0x0       the OUT2 signal is held inactive high while the value of this
                                                  location is internally looped back to an input.
                                                  0x0: OUT2 signal deasserted (logic 1)
                                                  0x1: OUT2 signal asserted (logic 0)
                                                  This bit is used to directly control the internal OUT1 signal. The
                                                  value written to this location is inverted and driven out on OUT1.
                                                  Note that in Loopback mode (UART_MCR[LOOPBACK] set to 1),
     2     OUT1              R/W        0x0       the OUT1 signal is held inactive high while the value of this
                                                  location is internally looped back to an input.
                                                  0x0: OUT1 signal deasserted (logic 1)
                                                  0x1: OUT1 signal asserted (logic 0)
                                                  Request to Send
                                                  This bit is used to directly control the UART_RTS output. The RTS
                                                  bit is used to inform the modem that the UART is ready to
                                                  exchange data.
                                                  When Auto Flow Control mode is not enabled (UART_MCR[AFCE]
                                                  set to 0), the UART_RTS is set low by programming UART_MCR

                                                  When both Auto Flow Control mode and FIFOs are enabled
                                                  (UART_MCR[AFCE] set to 1 and UART_FCR[FIFOE] set to 1,
     1     RTS               R/W        0x0
                                                  respectively), the UART_RTS is controlled in the same way, but is
                                                  also gated with the Rx FIFO threshold trigger (UART_RTS is inactive
                                                  high when above the threshold). The UART_RTS output will be
                                                  deasserted when UART_MCR[RTS] is set to 0.
                                                  Note that in Loopback mode (UART_MCR[LOOPBACK] set to 1),
                                                  the UART_RTS output remains held inactive high, while the value
                                                  of this bit is internally looped back to an input.
                                                  0x0: UART_RTS deasserted (logic 1)
                                                  0x1: UART_RTS asserted (logic 0)
                                                  Data Terminal Ready
                                                  This bit is used to directly control the DTR output. The value
     0     DTR               R/W        0x0       written to this bit is inverted and driven out on DTR.
                                                  The DTR output is used to inform the modem that the UART is
                                                  ready to establish communications.
